  # stable: full production guardrails required
  # deprecated: no new feature work, retirement path active
  lifecycle: stable # <-- CHANGE THIS: choose one of alpha|beta|stable|deprecated based on production posture.

spec:
  # Primary operational contact for non-urgent ownership requests.
  # Valid value: team email alias or monitored mailbox.
  contact: platform-team@example.com # <-- CHANGE THIS: set monitored owner contact email.

  oncall:
    # PagerDuty service identifier used for critical routing.
    # Valid value: PagerDuty service id like PXXXXXX from PagerDuty Service settings.
    pagerduty_service: PXXXXXX # <-- CHANGE THIS: set PagerDuty service id; source PagerDuty -> Service -> Details.
    # Slack channel for warning/info notifications.
    # Valid value: channel name with # prefix.
    slack_channel: "#platform-alerts" # <-- CHANGE THIS: set team alerts channel.

  # Runtime deployment locations in format <namespace>/<deployment-name>.
  # Required for ownership discovery by namespace during incidents.
  namespaces:
    - production/my-service # <-- CHANGE THIS: replace with real namespace/deployment pair.
    - staging/my-service # <-- CHANGE THIS: replace with staging namespace/deployment pair.
    - dev/my-service # <-- CHANGE THIS: replace with dev namespace/deployment pair.

  # Container image repository without tag.
  # Used by tooling to connect to vulnerability and provenance reports.
  image: ghcr.io/your-org/my-service # <-- CHANGE THIS: set registry/repository path used by deployment.

  # Runtime dependencies used for blast-radius and change-risk analysis.
  dependencies:
    - type: service # Dependency category. Valid values: service|database|external-api.
      name: auth-service # <-- CHANGE THIS: set internal service dependency name or remove.
    - type: database # Dependency category.
      name: postgres-prod # <-- CHANGE THIS: set database dependency name or remove.
      cloud: aws # Cloud provider for this dependency. Valid values: aws|azure|gcp|onprem.
      region: us-east-1 # Region where dependency is hosted. Valid value: provider region code.
    - type: external-api # Dependency category.
      name: stripe # <-- CHANGE THIS: set external API name or remove.
      url: https://api.stripe.com # <-- CHANGE THIS: set base URL for external API dependency.

  slo:
    # Availability objective percentage for service reliability planning.
    # Valid value: numeric percentage, typically 95.0-99.99.
    availability_target: 99.9
    # p99 latency target in milliseconds for user-facing requests.
    # Valid value: positive integer representing ms threshold.
    latency_target_ms: 500
    # Path to SLO definition file tracked in repository.
    # Required for lifecycle beta/stable.
    definition_file: observability/prometheus/slos/my-service-slo.yaml # <-- CHANGE THIS: set existing SLO definition path.

  # Primary runbook URL for incidents and operational actions.
  # Required for lifecycle stable.
  runbook_url: https://github.com/your-org/repo/blob/main/docs/runbooks/my-service.md # <-- CHANGE THIS: set markdown runbook URL for this service.

  # Architecture or service documentation URL.
  # Optional but recommended for onboarding and incident triage context.
  docs_url: https://confluence.example.com/my-service # <-- CHANGE THIS: set architecture docs URL or remove if unavailable.

  # FinOps cost center owner for this service spend.
  # Must match finops/config/budgets.yaml cost_center value.
  cost_center: engineering # <-- CHANGE THIS: set one of configured cost centers from finops/config/budgets.yaml.

  # Environment label value used on runtime resources.
  # Valid values: dev|staging|production.
  environment: production # <-- CHANGE THIS: set primary environment label value.

  # Data classification for security and compliance policy selection.
  # Valid values: public|internal|confidential|restricted.
  data_classification: confidential # <-- CHANGE THIS: set classification matching data sensitivity.

  # Compliance frameworks that apply to this service.
  # For stable confidential services, SOC2 is required.
  compliance_frameworks:
    - SOC2 # <-- CHANGE THIS: keep if service is SOC2 scoped.
    - ISO27001 # <-- CHANGE THIS: remove if framework not applicable.

# ArgoCD Application — single app

# Note 2: This Kubernetes style field captures a contract; keeping schema keys stable improves portability across environments.
metadata:
  name: my-app
  # Note 3: Resource identity and metadata drive automation, selectors, and operational traceability.
  namespace: argocd
  finalizers:
    # Note 4: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
    - resources-finalizer.argocd.argoproj.io  # Cascade delete on app removal
spec:
  # Note 5: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
  project: platform-apps

  source:
    # Note 6: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
    repoURL: https://github.com/my-org/my-app.git
    targetRevision: v1.0.0
    # Note 7: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
    path: cd/kubernetes/_overlays/prod

  destination:
    # Note 8: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
    server: https://kubernetes.default.svc  # In-cluster
    namespace: production

  # Note 9: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
  syncPolicy:
    automated:
      # Note 10: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
      prune: true       # Remove resources deleted from Git
      selfHeal: true    # Revert manual changes in cluster
      # Note 11: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
      allowEmpty: false
    syncOptions:
      # Note 12: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
      - CreateNamespace=true
      - ApplyOutOfSyncOnly=true
      - PrunePropagationPolicy=foreground
    # Note 13: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
    retry:
      limit: 3
      backoff:
        duration: 5s
        factor: 2
        maxDuration: 2m

  # Health check customization
  ignoreDifferences:
    - group: apps
      kind: Deployment
      jsonPointers:

# ============================================================
# TEMPLATE: ArgoCD ConfigMap Patch — Custom Resource Health
# WHEN TO USE: Add health checks for CRDs so ArgoCD reports sync status accurately
# PREREQUISITES: ArgoCD installed and configured to merge this ConfigMap data
# MATURITY: Stable
# ============================================================
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: argocd-cm
  namespace: argocd
data:
  resource.customizations.health.external-secrets.io_ExternalSecret: |
    hs = {}
    if obj.status ~= nil and obj.status.conditions ~= nil then
      for _, condition in ipairs(obj.status.conditions) do
        if condition.type == "Ready" and condition.status == "True" then
          hs.status = "Healthy"
          hs.message = condition.message or "ExternalSecret is ready"
          return hs
        end
      end
    end
    hs.status = "Progressing"
    hs.message = "Waiting for ExternalSecret readiness"
    return hs
  resource.customizations.health.cert-manager.io_Certificate: |
    hs = {}
    if obj.status ~= nil and obj.status.conditions ~= nil then
      for _, condition in ipairs(obj.status.conditions) do
        if condition.type == "Ready" and condition.status == "True" then
          hs.status = "Healthy"
          hs.message = condition.message or "Certificate is ready"
          return hs
        end
      end
    end
    hs.status = "Progressing"
    hs.message = "Waiting for certificate issuance"
    return hs
  resource.customizations.health.kyverno.io_Policy: |
    hs = {}
    hs.status = "Healthy"
    hs.message = "Kyverno Policy applied"
    return hs
  resource.customizations.health.kyverno.io_ClusterPolicy: |
    hs = {}
    hs.status = "Healthy"
    hs.message = "Kyverno ClusterPolicy applied"
    return hs

# ============================================================
# TEMPLATE: ArgoCD Fleet - Cluster Registry
# WHEN TO USE: Single source of truth for clusters managed by fleet ApplicationSets
# PREREQUISITES: ArgoCD installed and fleet ApplicationSets deployed
# SECRETS NEEDED: None
# WHAT TO CHANGE: Cluster endpoints, labels, tier, and environment values
# RELATED FILES: cd/gitops/argocd/fleet/fleet-applicationset.yaml
# MATURITY: Beta
# ============================================================

# How to add a new cluster:
# 1. Add a new entry in data.clusters below.
# 2. Commit this file and run the fleet onboarding workflow documented in docs/golden-paths/multi-cluster-fleet.md.
#
# How ArgoCD reads this ConfigMap:
# fleet ApplicationSets use a list generator where elementsYaml is sourced from this ConfigMap's data.clusters key.
#
# tier and Kyverno behavior:
# critical clusters should use kyverno-enforcement: enforce; standard/dev clusters can start in audit.
#
# Scale limit:
# this pattern supports up to 20 clusters per fleet ApplicationSet before moving to a pull-based generator model.
# Cluster registry is human-maintained only. Do not automate writes to this file.
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: cluster-registry
  namespace: argocd
  annotations:
    fleet.argocd.io/description: "Single source of truth for all clusters in this fleet"
    fleet.argocd.io/updated: "manual"
data:
  clusters: |
    - name: prod-us-east-1
      server: https://eks-prod-us-east-1.example.com # <-- CHANGE THIS: set the target cluster API server URL from your cloud control plane endpoint.
      cloud: aws
      region: us-east-1
      environment: production
      tier: critical
      topology: hub-and-spoke
      labels:
        team: platform
        cost-center: infrastructure
      kyverno-enforcement: enforce
      prometheus-remote-write: enabled
    - name: staging-us-east-1
      server: https://eks-staging-us-east-1.example.com # <-- CHANGE THIS: set the staging cluster API server URL; differs per account/region.
      cloud: aws
      region: us-east-1
      environment: staging
      tier: standard
      topology: hub-and-spoke
      labels:
        team: platform
        cost-center: infrastructure
      kyverno-enforcement: audit
      prometheus-remote-write: enabled
    - name: dev-shared
      server: https://eks-dev.example.com # <-- CHANGE THIS: set the development cluster API server URL for your shared dev fleet target.
      cloud: aws
      region: us-east-1
      environment: dev
      tier: dev
      topology: distributed
      labels:
        team: platform
        cost-center: engineering
      kyverno-enforcement: audit
      prometheus-remote-write: disabled

# ============================================================
# TEMPLATE: ArgoCD Fleet - Platform Component ApplicationSet
# WHEN TO USE: Propagate shared platform components to all registered clusters
# PREREQUISITES: cluster-registry ConfigMap and fleet-platform AppProject
# SECRETS NEEDED: None
# WHAT TO CHANGE: Repo URL and ConfigMap data source wiring for elementsYaml
# RELATED FILES: cd/gitops/argocd/fleet/cluster-registry.yaml
# MATURITY: Beta
# ============================================================

apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: ApplicationSet
metadata:
  name: fleet-platform-components
  namespace: argocd
spec:
  goTemplate: true
  # Scale limit: keep this ApplicationSet to 20 clusters max to avoid reconciliation pressure.
  # Design choice: use list generator from cluster-registry ConfigMap instead of ArgoCD clusters generator
  # to keep cluster inventory human-maintained and auditable in Git.
  generators:
    - matrix:
        generators:
          - list:
              elementsYaml: |
                {{- /* Source from cluster-registry ConfigMap data.clusters via your rendering pipeline */ -}}
                {{ .clusters | default "[]" }}
          - list:
              elements:
                - component: kyverno
                  appNamespace: kyverno
                  sourceType: kustomize
                  sourcePath: policy/kyverno
                - component: external-secrets-operator
                  appNamespace: external-secrets-system
                  sourceType: helm
                  chartRepo: https://charts.external-secrets.io
                  chartName: external-secrets
                  chartVersion: 0.9.20
                  valueFiles: []
                - component: prometheus-stack
                  appNamespace: monitoring
                  sourceType: helm
                  chartRepo: https://prometheus-community.github.io/helm-charts
                  chartName: kube-prometheus-stack
                  chartVersion: 62.7.0
                  valueFiles:
                    - observability/prometheus/values.yaml
                - component: cert-manager
                  appNamespace: cert-manager
                  sourceType: kustomize
                  sourcePath: cd/kubernetes/cert-manager
                - component: fleet-network-policies
                  appNamespace: fleet-system
                  sourceType: kustomize
                  sourcePath: cd/kubernetes/_base/network-policies

  template:
    metadata:
      name: "{{ .name }}-{{ .component }}"
      labels:
        fleet.argocd.io/cluster: "{{ .name }}"
        fleet.argocd.io/component: "{{ .component }}"
        fleet.argocd.io/environment: "{{ .environment }}"
      finalizers:
        - resources-finalizer.argocd.argoproj.io
    spec:
      project: fleet-platform
      destination:
        server: "{{ .server }}"
        namespace: "{{ .appNamespace }}"
      source:
        repoURL: https://github.com/your-org/cicd-reference.git # <-- CHANGE THIS: set your GitOps repository URL so generated Applications point at your actual source-of-truth repo.
        targetRevision: HEAD
        path: "{{ .sourcePath }}"
      syncPolicy:
        automated:
          prune: true
          selfHeal: true
        syncOptions:
          - CreateNamespace=true
          # At fleet scale (20 clusters x 5 components), full syncs create API load spikes.
          # ApplyOutOfSyncOnly=true limits reconciliation to changed resources only.
          - ApplyOutOfSyncOnly=true
      # Retry with exponential backoff: unreachable cluster should not block healthy clusters.
      retry:
        limit: 5
        backoff:
          duration: 30s
          factor: 2
          maxDuration: 5m

  templatePatch: |
    {{- if eq .sourceType "helm" }}
    spec:
      source:
        repoURL: "{{ .chartRepo }}"
        chart: "{{ .chartName }}"
        targetRevision: "{{ .chartVersion }}"
        helm:
          {{- if .valueFiles }}
          valueFiles:
          {{- range .valueFiles }}
            - "{{ . }}"
          {{- end }}
          {{- end }}
    {{- end }}

# ============================================================
# TEMPLATE: ArgoCD Fleet - Platform AppProject
# WHEN TO USE: Security boundary for fleet-level GitOps deployments
# PREREQUISITES: ArgoCD namespace and cluster registry ConfigMap
# SECRETS NEEDED: None
# WHAT TO CHANGE: Source repo URL allow-list and namespace scopes
# RELATED FILES: cd/gitops/argocd/fleet/fleet-applicationset.yaml
# MATURITY: Beta
# ============================================================

apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: AppProject
metadata:
  name: fleet-platform
  namespace: argocd
  annotations:
    fleet.argocd.io/cascade: "true"
spec:
  description: Fleet-level project for shared platform components across registered clusters.

  sourceRepos:
    - https://github.com/your-org/cicd-reference.git # <-- CHANGE THIS: set to your authoritative GitOps repository URL so only trusted sources can deploy fleet components.

  destinations:
    - server: "*"
      namespace: kyverno
    - server: "*"
      namespace: external-secrets-system
    - server: "*"
      namespace: monitoring
    - server: "*"
      namespace: cert-manager
    - server: "*"
      namespace: argocd
    - server: "*"
      namespace: fleet-*

  clusterResourceWhitelist:
    - group: ""
      kind: Namespace
    - group: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
      kind: ClusterRole
    - group: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
      kind: ClusterRoleBinding
    - group: kyverno.io
      kind: ClusterPolicy

  namespaceResourceWhitelist:
    - group: "*"
      kind: "*"

# This project intentionally uses broad permissions because it deploys platform components.
# Application teams should use separate AppProjects with narrower scope - see cd/gitops/argocd/application.yaml for the single-app pattern.

---
# ============================================================
# TEMPLATE: ArgoCD Fleet - Workload ApplicationSet
# WHEN TO USE: Deploy workloads across selected fleet clusters by environment
# PREREQUISITES: cluster-registry ConfigMap and cd/fleet-overlays structure
# SECRETS NEEDED: None
# WHAT TO CHANGE: repoURL and targetEnvironment value
# RELATED FILES: cd/fleet-overlays/README.md
# MATURITY: Beta
# ============================================================

apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: ApplicationSet
metadata:
  name: fleet-workloads
  namespace: argocd
spec:
  goTemplate: true
  goTemplateOptions:
    - missingkey=error
  # Scale limit: this generator strategy is validated for up to 20 clusters.
  # Platform components belong in fleet-applicationset.yaml; workloads belong here.
  generators:
    - matrix:
        generators:
          - list:
              elementsYaml: |
                {{- /* Source from cluster-registry ConfigMap data.clusters via your rendering pipeline */ -}}
                {{ .clusters | default "[]" }}
          - git:
              repoURL: https://github.com/your-org/cicd-reference.git # <-- CHANGE THIS: set to your GitOps repository so ApplicationSet can discover fleet overlay directories.
              revision: HEAD
              directories:
                - path: cd/fleet-overlays/*/*

  template:
    metadata:
      name: '{{ .name }}-{{ index (splitList "/" .path.path) 3 }}'
      labels:
        fleet.argocd.io/cluster: "{{ .name }}"
        fleet.argocd.io/environment: "{{ .environment }}"
        fleet.argocd.io/app: '{{ index (splitList "/" .path.path) 3 }}'
      finalizers:
        - resources-finalizer.argocd.argoproj.io
    spec:
      project: fleet-platform
      source:
        repoURL: https://github.com/your-org/cicd-reference.git # <-- CHANGE THIS: use the same GitOps repo URL used by your overlays and ApplicationSets.
        targetRevision: HEAD
        path: "{{ .path.path }}"
      destination:
        server: "{{ .server }}"
        namespace: 'fleet-{{ index (splitList "/" .path.path) 3 }}'
      syncPolicy:
        automated:
          prune: true
          selfHeal: true
        syncOptions:
          - CreateNamespace=true
          # Required for fleet scale: avoid full-apply storms by syncing only changed objects.
          - ApplyOutOfSyncOnly=true
      retry:
        limit: 5
        backoff:
          duration: 30s
          factor: 2
          maxDuration: 5m

  # Matrix behavior:
  # For N clusters and M app overlay directories, this yields N x M Applications.
  # Example: 5 clusters x 3 apps = 15 Applications managed by one ApplicationSet.

---
# ============================================================
# TEMPLATE: Flux GitRepository — Source of Truth
# WHEN TO USE: Define the Git source consumed by Flux Kustomizations and HelmReleases
# PREREQUISITES: Flux installed and repository credentials configured if private
# MATURITY: Stable
# ============================================================
apiVersion: source.toolkit.fluxcd.io/v1
kind: GitRepository
metadata:
  name: my-app-repo
  namespace: flux-system
spec:
  interval: 1m
  url: https://github.com/my-org/gitops-repo.git           # <-- CHANGE THIS
  ref:
    branch: main

---
# ============================================================
# TEMPLATE: Flux HelmRelease — Chart Reconciliation
# WHEN TO USE: Deploy a service from a Helm chart using Flux
# PREREQUISITES: Flux installed and Helm chart path available in GitRepository
# MATURITY: Stable
# ============================================================
apiVersion: helm.toolkit.fluxcd.io/v2
kind: HelmRelease
metadata:
  name: my-app
  namespace: flux-system
spec:
  interval: 5m
  targetNamespace: production
  chart:
    spec:
      chart: ./cd/helm/webapp                                  # <-- CHANGE THIS
      sourceRef:
        kind: GitRepository
        name: my-app-repo
        namespace: flux-system
      interval: 1m
  values:
    image:
      repository: ghcr.io/my-org/my-app                        # <-- CHANGE THIS
      tag: "1.0.0"                                            # <-- CHANGE THIS
    finops:
      labels:
        costCenter: engineering
        environment: production

---
# ============================================================
# TEMPLATE: Flux ImageUpdateAutomation — Tag Promotion
# WHEN TO USE: Automatically promote image tags to Git after new image policy matches
# PREREQUISITES: Flux image-reflector and image-automation controllers installed
# MATURITY: Stable
# ============================================================
apiVersion: image.toolkit.fluxcd.io/v1beta2
kind: ImageRepository
metadata:
  name: my-app
  namespace: flux-system
spec:
  image: ghcr.io/my-org/my-app                                  # <-- CHANGE THIS
  interval: 1m
---
apiVersion: image.toolkit.fluxcd.io/v1beta2
kind: ImagePolicy
metadata:
  name: my-app
  namespace: flux-system
spec:
  imageRepositoryRef:
    name: my-app
  policy:
    semver:
      range: ">=1.0.0"
---
apiVersion: image.toolkit.fluxcd.io/v1beta2
kind: ImageUpdateAutomation
metadata:
  name: my-app
  namespace: flux-system
spec:
  interval: 5m
  sourceRef:
    kind: GitRepository
    name: my-app-repo
  git:
    checkout:
      ref:
        branch: main
    commit:
      author:
        name: flux-bot
        email: flux-bot@my-org.example                           # <-- CHANGE THIS
      messageTemplate: "chore(flux): update images"
    push:
      branch: main
  update:
    strategy: Setters
    path: ./cd/kubernetes/_overlays/prod                         # <-- CHANGE THIS

---
# ============================================================
# TEMPLATE: Flux Kustomization — GitOps Reconciliation
# WHEN TO USE: Deploying Kubernetes manifests via FluxCD
# PREREQUISITES: Flux installed, GitRepository source configured
# SECRETS NEEDED: Git credentials (configured in Flux)
# WHAT TO CHANGE: sourceRef, path, interval, namespace
# RELATED FILES: cd/kubernetes/_overlays/prod/kustomization.yaml
# MATURITY: Stable
# ============================================================

# Flux Kustomization — reconcile Kubernetes manifests from Git
# Note 1: This Kubernetes style field captures a contract; keeping schema keys stable improves portability across environments.
apiVersion: kustomize.toolkit.fluxcd.io/v1
kind: Kustomization
# Note 2: This Kubernetes style field captures a contract; keeping schema keys stable improves portability across environments.
metadata:
  name: my-app
  # Note 3: Resource identity and metadata drive automation, selectors, and operational traceability.
  namespace: flux-system
spec:
  # Note 4: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
  interval: 5m      # Reconcile every 5 minutes
  path: ./cd/kubernetes/_overlays/prod
  # Note 5: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
  prune: true       # Remove resources deleted from Git
  sourceRef:
    # Note 6: This Kubernetes style field captures a contract; keeping schema keys stable improves portability across environments.
    kind: GitRepository
    name: my-app-repo

  # Note 7: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
  healthChecks:
    - apiVersion: apps/v1
      # Note 8: This Kubernetes style field captures a contract; keeping schema keys stable improves portability across environments.
      kind: Deployment
      name: app
      # Note 9: Resource identity and metadata drive automation, selectors, and operational traceability.
      namespace: production

  # Post-build variable substitution
  postBuild:
    # Note 10: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
    substituteFrom:
      - kind: ConfigMap
        name: flux-vars
      - kind: Secret
        name: flux-secrets
        optional: true

# TEMPLATE: Helm Chart Metadata — Microservice
# WHEN TO USE: Defines chart identity, versioning, and maintainers for the microservice chart.
# PREREQUISITES: Helm 3 and semantic versioning policy for release tags.
# MATURITY: Stable
apiVersion: v2
name: microservice
description: Generic Microservice Helm Chart with sidecar support
type: application
version: 0.1.0
appVersion: "1.0.0"
keywords:
  - microservice
  - api
maintainers:
  - name: Platform Team

---
# TEMPLATE: Helm Template — Microservice HorizontalPodAutoscaler
# WHEN TO USE: Enables CPU-driven autoscaling for the microservice Deployment.
# PREREQUISITES: metrics-server installed and autoscaling.enabled set true.
# MATURITY: Stable
{{- if .Values.autoscaling.enabled }}
apiVersion: autoscaling/v2
kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
metadata:
  name: {{ include "microservice.fullname" . }}
  labels:
    {{- include "microservice.labels" . | nindent 4 }}
spec:
  scaleTargetRef:
    apiVersion: apps/v1
    kind: Deployment
    name: {{ include "microservice.fullname" . }}
  minReplicas: {{ .Values.autoscaling.minReplicas }}
  maxReplicas: {{ .Values.autoscaling.maxReplicas }}
  metrics:
    - type: Resource
      resource:
        name: cpu
        target:
          type: Utilization
          averageUtilization: {{ .Values.autoscaling.targetCPUUtilizationPercentage }}
{{- end }}

---
# TEMPLATE: Helm Template — Microservice NetworkPolicy
# WHEN TO USE: Restricts ingress/egress for microservice workloads under zero-trust defaults.
# PREREQUISITES: CNI with NetworkPolicy enforcement and networkPolicy.* values configured.
# MATURITY: Stable
{{- if .Values.networkPolicy.enabled }}
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: {{ include "microservice.fullname" . }}
  labels:
    {{- include "microservice.labels" . | nindent 4 }}
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      {{- include "microservice.selectorLabels" . | nindent 6 }}
  policyTypes:
    - Ingress
    - Egress
  ingress:
    - from:
        - namespaceSelector:
            matchLabels:
              kubernetes.io/metadata.name: {{ .Values.networkPolicy.ingressControllerNamespace | quote }}
          podSelector:
            matchLabels:
              app.kubernetes.io/name: {{ .Values.networkPolicy.ingressControllerPodLabel | quote }}
      ports:
        - protocol: TCP
          port: {{ .Values.service.targetPort }}
  egress:
    - to:
        - namespaceSelector:
            matchLabels:
              kubernetes.io/metadata.name: kube-system
          podSelector:
            matchLabels:
              k8s-app: kube-dns
      ports:
        - protocol: UDP
          port: 53
        - protocol: TCP
          port: 53
{{- end }}

---
# TEMPLATE: Helm Template — Microservice PodDisruptionBudget
# WHEN TO USE: Protects minimum pod availability during voluntary disruptions.
# PREREQUISITES: deployment replica strategy and pdb.* values configured.
# MATURITY: Stable
{{- if .Values.pdb.enabled }}
apiVersion: policy/v1
kind: PodDisruptionBudget
metadata:
  name: {{ include "microservice.fullname" . }}-pdb
  labels:
    {{- include "microservice.labels" . | nindent 4 }}
spec:
  minAvailable: {{ .Values.pdb.minAvailable }}
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      {{- include "microservice.selectorLabels" . | nindent 6 }}
{{- end }}
