# Note 1: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: "2010-09-09"
Description: "CI/CD Pipeline — CodePipeline + CodeBuild → ECS Fargate"

# ============================================================
# PARAMETERS
# ============================================================
Parameters:
  # Note 2: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
  ProjectName:
    Type: String
    Description: "Project name — used for naming all resources"
    # Note 3: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
    Default: my-app                # <-- CHANGE THIS

  RepositoryId:
    Type: String
    # Note 4: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
    Description: "GitHub repository (org/repo format) or CodeCommit repo name"
    Default: my-org/my-repo        # <-- CHANGE THIS

  BranchName:
    # Note 5: This declaration defines a reusable unit, which supports composition and makes behavior easier to test.
    Type: String
    Description: "Branch to trigger the pipeline"
    Default: main

  # Note 6: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
  ConnectionArn:
    Type: String
    Description: "ARN of the CodeStar Connection to GitHub (create in Console → Settings → Connections)"
    # <-- CHANGE THIS: create connection first, then paste ARN

  # Note 7: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
  EcrRepositoryName:
    Type: String
    Description: "ECR repository name for built images"
    # Note 8: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
    Default: my-app                # <-- CHANGE THIS

  EcsClusterName:
    Type: String
    # Note 9: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
    Description: "ECS cluster to deploy to"
    Default: my-cluster            # <-- CHANGE THIS

  EcsServiceName:
    # Note 10: This declaration defines a reusable unit, which supports composition and makes behavior easier to test.
    Type: String
    Description: "ECS service to update"
    Default: my-service            # <-- CHANGE THIS

  # Note 11: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
  ContainerName:
    Type: String
    Description: "Container name in the ECS task definition"
    # Note 12: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
    Default: my-app                # <-- CHANGE THIS

  BuildComputeType:
    Type: String
    # Note 13: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
    Description: "CodeBuild compute type"
    Default: BUILD_GENERAL1_SMALL
    AllowedValues:
      # Note 14: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
      - BUILD_GENERAL1_SMALL
      - BUILD_GENERAL1_MEDIUM
      - BUILD_GENERAL1_LARGE

# Note 15: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
Resources:
  # ============================================================
  # S3 Bucket — stores pipeline artifacts between stages
  # ============================================================
  ArtifactBucket:
    Type: AWS::S3::Bucket
    # Note 16: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
    Properties:
      BucketName: !Sub "${ProjectName}-pipeline-artifacts-${AWS::AccountId}"
      VersioningConfiguration:
        # Note 17: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
        Status: Enabled
      BucketEncryption:
        ServerSideEncryptionConfiguration:
          # Note 18: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
          - ServerSideEncryptionByDefault:
              SSEAlgorithm: AES256
      LifecycleConfiguration:
        # Note 19: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
        Rules:
          - Id: CleanupOldArtifacts
            Status: Enabled
            # Note 20: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
            ExpirationInDays: 30
      Tags:
        - Key: Project
          # Note 21: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
          Value: !Ref ProjectName
        - Key: ManagedBy
          Value: cloudformation

  # ============================================================
  # IAM Role — CodeBuild
  # ============================================================
  # Note 22: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
  CodeBuildRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      # Note 23: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
      RoleName: !Sub "${ProjectName}-codebuild-role"
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: "2012-10-17"
        # Note 24: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              # Note 25: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
              Service: codebuild.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      Policies:
        # Note 26: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
        - PolicyName: CodeBuildPolicy
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: "2012-10-17"
            # Note 27: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
            Statement:
              # CloudWatch Logs
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  # Note 28: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
                  - logs:CreateLogGroup
                  - logs:CreateLogStream
                  - logs:PutLogEvents
                # Note 29: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
                Resource: !Sub "arn:aws:logs:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:log-group:/aws/codebuild/${ProjectName}-build*"
              # S3 artifacts
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  # Note 30: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
                  - s3:GetObject
                  - s3:PutObject
                  - s3:GetBucketAcl
                  # Note 31: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
                  - s3:GetBucketLocation
                Resource:
                  - !GetAtt ArtifactBucket.Arn
                  # Note 32: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
                  - !Sub "${ArtifactBucket.Arn}/*"
              # ECR — push images
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  # Note 33: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
                  - ecr:GetAuthorizationToken
                Resource: "*"
              - Effect: Allow
                # Note 34: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
                Action:
                  - ecr:BatchCheckLayerAvailability
                  - ecr:GetDownloadUrlForLayer
                  # Note 35: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
                  - ecr:BatchGetImage
                  - ecr:PutImage
                  - ecr:InitiateLayerUpload
                  # Note 36: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
                  - ecr:UploadLayerPart
                  - ecr:CompleteLayerUpload
                Resource: !Sub "arn:aws:ecr:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:repository/${EcrRepositoryName}"

  # ============================================================
  # IAM Role — CodePipeline
  # ============================================================
  # Note 37: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
  CodePipelineRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      # Note 38: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
      RoleName: !Sub "${ProjectName}-codepipeline-role"
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: "2012-10-17"
        # Note 39: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              # Note 40: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
              Service: codepipeline.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      Policies:
        # Note 41: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
        - PolicyName: CodePipelinePolicy
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: "2012-10-17"
            # Note 42: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
            Statement:
              # S3 artifacts
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  # Note 43: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
                  - s3:GetObject
                  - s3:PutObject
                  - s3:GetBucketVersioning
                # Note 44: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
                Resource:
                  - !GetAtt ArtifactBucket.Arn
                  - !Sub "${ArtifactBucket.Arn}/*"
              # CodeBuild
              # Note 45: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - codebuild:BatchGetBuilds
                  # Note 46: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
                  - codebuild:StartBuild
                Resource: !GetAtt CodeBuildProject.Arn
              # CodeStar Connection (GitHub)
              - Effect: Allow
                # Note 47: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
                Action:
                  - codestar-connections:UseConnection
                Resource: !Ref ConnectionArn
              # ECS deploy
              # Note 48: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - ecs:DescribeServices
                  # Note 49: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
                  - ecs:DescribeTaskDefinition
                  - ecs:DescribeTasks
                  - ecs:ListTasks
                  # Note 50: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
                  - ecs:RegisterTaskDefinition
                  - ecs:UpdateService
                Resource: "*"
              # Note 51: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - iam:PassRole
                # Note 52: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
                Resource: "*"
                Condition:
                  StringEqualsIfExists:
                    # Note 53: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
                    iam:PassedToService:
                      - ecs-tasks.amazonaws.com

  # ============================================================
  # CodeBuild Project — builds the Docker image
  # ============================================================
  CodeBuildProject:
    # Note 54: This declaration defines a reusable unit, which supports composition and makes behavior easier to test.
    Type: AWS::CodeBuild::Project
    Properties:
      Name: !Sub "${ProjectName}-build"
      # Note 55: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
      Description: !Sub "Build Docker image for ${ProjectName}"
      ServiceRole: !GetAtt CodeBuildRole.Arn
      TimeoutInMinutes: 15
      # Note 56: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
      Artifacts:
        Type: CODEPIPELINE
      Environment:
        # Note 57: This declaration defines a reusable unit, which supports composition and makes behavior easier to test.
        Type: LINUX_CONTAINER
        ComputeType: !Ref BuildComputeType
        Image: aws/codebuild/amazonlinux2-x86_64-standard:5.0
        # Note 58: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
        PrivilegedMode: true      # Required for Docker builds
        EnvironmentVariables:
          - Name: AWS_ACCOUNT_ID
            # Note 59: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
            Value: !Ref AWS::AccountId
          - Name: AWS_DEFAULT_REGION
            Value: !Ref AWS::Region
          # Note 60: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
          - Name: ECR_REPOSITORY
            Value: !Ref EcrRepositoryName
          - Name: CONTAINER_NAME
            # Note 61: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
            Value: !Ref ContainerName
      Source:
        Type: CODEPIPELINE
        # Note 62: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
        BuildSpec: |
          version: 0.2
          phases:
            # Note 63: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
            pre_build:
              commands:
                - echo "Logging in to ECR..."
                # Note 64: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
                - aws ecr get-login-password --region $AWS_DEFAULT_REGION | docker login --username AWS --password-stdin $AWS_ACCOUNT_ID.dkr.ecr.$AWS_DEFAULT_REGION.amazonaws.com
                - IMAGE_URI=$AWS_ACCOUNT_ID.dkr.ecr.$AWS_DEFAULT_REGION.amazonaws.com/$ECR_REPOSITORY
                - IMAGE_TAG=$CODEBUILD_RESOLVED_SOURCE_VERSION
            # Note 65: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
            build:
              commands:
                - echo "Building Docker image..."
                # Note 66: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
                - docker build -t $IMAGE_URI:$IMAGE_TAG .
                - docker tag $IMAGE_URI:$IMAGE_TAG $IMAGE_URI:latest
            post_build:
              # Note 67: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
              commands:
                - echo "Pushing Docker image..."
                - docker push $IMAGE_URI:$IMAGE_TAG
                # Note 68: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
                - docker push $IMAGE_URI:latest
                - echo "Writing image definitions for ECS deploy..."
                - printf '[{"name":"%s","imageUri":"%s"}]' "$CONTAINER_NAME" "$IMAGE_URI:$IMAGE_TAG" > imagedefinitions.json
          # Note 69: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
          artifacts:
            files:
              - imagedefinitions.json
      # Note 70: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
      Tags:
        - Key: Project
          Value: !Ref ProjectName
        # Note 71: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
        - Key: ManagedBy
          Value: cloudformation

  # ============================================================
  # CodePipeline — Source → Build → Deploy
  # ============================================================
  Pipeline:
    # Note 72: This declaration defines a reusable unit, which supports composition and makes behavior easier to test.
    Type: AWS::CodePipeline::Pipeline
    Properties:
      Name: !Sub "${ProjectName}-pipeline"
      # Note 73: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
      RoleArn: !GetAtt CodePipelineRole.Arn
      ArtifactStore:
        Type: S3
        # Note 74: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
        Location: !Ref ArtifactBucket
      Stages:
        # --- Source Stage ---
        - Name: Source
          # Note 75: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
          Actions:
            - Name: GitHubSource
              ActionTypeId:
                # Note 76: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
                Category: Source
                Owner: AWS
                Provider: CodeStarSourceConnection
                # Note 77: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
                Version: "1"
              Configuration:
                ConnectionArn: !Ref ConnectionArn
                # Note 78: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
                FullRepositoryId: !Ref RepositoryId
                BranchName: !Ref BranchName
                DetectChanges: true
                # Note 79: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
                OutputArtifactFormat: CODE_ZIP
              OutputArtifacts:
                - Name: SourceArtifact

        # --- Build Stage ---
        # Note 80: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
        - Name: Build
          Actions:
            - Name: DockerBuild
              # Note 81: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
              ActionTypeId:
                Category: Build
                Owner: AWS
                # Note 82: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
                Provider: CodeBuild
                Version: "1"
              Configuration:
                # Note 83: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
                ProjectName: !Ref CodeBuildProject
              InputArtifacts:
                - Name: SourceArtifact
              # Note 84: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
              OutputArtifacts:
                - Name: BuildArtifact

        # --- Manual Approval (optional — remove for auto-deploy) ---
        - Name: Approval
          # Note 85: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
          Actions:
            - Name: ManualApproval
              ActionTypeId:
                # Note 86: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
                Category: Approval
                Owner: AWS
                Provider: Manual
                # Note 87: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
                Version: "1"
              Configuration:
                CustomData: !Sub "Approve deployment of ${ProjectName} to ECS?"
                # NotificationArn: arn:aws:sns:...   # <-- CHANGE THIS: SNS topic for approval emails

        # --- Deploy Stage ---
        # Note 88: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
        - Name: Deploy
          Actions:
            - Name: DeployToECS
              # Note 89: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
              ActionTypeId:
                Category: Deploy
                Owner: AWS
                # Note 90: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
                Provider: ECS
                Version: "1"
              Configuration:
                # Note 91: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
                ClusterName: !Ref EcsClusterName
                ServiceName: !Ref EcsServiceName
                FileName: imagedefinitions.json
              # Note 92: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
              InputArtifacts:
                - Name: BuildArtifact

      Tags:
        # Note 93: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
        - Key: Project
          Value: !Ref ProjectName
        - Key: ManagedBy
          Value: cloudformation

# ============================================================
# OUTPUTS
# ============================================================
Outputs:
  PipelineUrl:
    Description: "CodePipeline console URL"
    Value: !Sub "https://${AWS::Region}.console.aws.amazon.com/codesuite/codepipeline/pipelines/${ProjectName}-pipeline/view"

  CodeBuildProjectName:
    Description: "CodeBuild project name"
    Value: !Ref CodeBuildProject

  ArtifactBucketName:
    Description: "S3 bucket for pipeline artifacts"
    Value: !Ref ArtifactBucket

# ============================================================
# TEMPLATE: GitHub Actions — Deploy to AWS ECS
# WHEN TO USE: Deploying containerised apps to ECS Fargate/EC2
# PREREQUISITES: ECR repository, ECS cluster & service, task definition
# SECRETS NEEDED: AWS_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN
# WHAT TO CHANGE: ECR repository, ECS cluster/service names, Dockerfile path
# RELATED FILES: docker/dotnet/Dockerfile.api
# MATURITY: Stable
# ============================================================

# Note 1: Resource identity and metadata drive automation, selectors, and operational traceability.
name: Deploy to AWS ECS

on:
  # Note 2: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
  push:
    branches: [main]

# Note 3: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
env:
  AWS_REGION: us-east-1
  # Note 4: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
  ECR_REPOSITORY: my-app
  ECS_SERVICE: my-service
  # Note 5: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
  ECS_CLUSTER: my-cluster
  CONTAINER_NAME: my-app

# Note 6: Pipeline structure separates concerns, helping teams test, deploy, and recover with smaller blast radius.
jobs:
  deploy:
    # Note 7: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      # Note 8: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
      id-token: write
      contents: read

    # Note 9: Pipeline structure separates concerns, helping teams test, deploy, and recover with smaller blast radius.
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      # Note 10: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
      - name: Configure AWS credentials
        uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v4
        # Note 11: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
        with:
          role-to-assume: ${{ secrets.AWS_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN }}
          # Note 12: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
          aws-region: ${{ env.AWS_REGION }}

      - name: Login to ECR
        # Note 13: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
        id: login-ecr
        uses: aws-actions/amazon-ecr-login@v2

      # Note 14: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
      - name: Build and push to ECR
        id: build
        # Note 15: Pipeline structure separates concerns, helping teams test, deploy, and recover with smaller blast radius.
        run: |
          IMAGE_URI=${{ steps.login-ecr.outputs.registry }}/${{ env.ECR_REPOSITORY }}:${{ github.sha }}
          # Note 16: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
          docker build -t $IMAGE_URI -f docker/dotnet/Dockerfile.api .
          docker push $IMAGE_URI
          # Note 17: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
          echo "image=$IMAGE_URI" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

      - name: Download task definition
        # Note 18: Pipeline structure separates concerns, helping teams test, deploy, and recover with smaller blast radius.
        run: aws ecs describe-task-definition --task-definition my-task --query taskDefinition > task-definition.json

      - name: Update ECS task definition
        id: task-def
        uses: aws-actions/amazon-ecs-render-task-definition@v1
        with:
          task-definition: task-definition.json
          container-name: ${{ env.CONTAINER_NAME }}
          image: ${{ steps.build.outputs.image }}

      - name: Deploy to ECS
        uses: aws-actions/amazon-ecs-deploy-task-definition@v1
        with:
          task-definition: ${{ steps.task-def.outputs.task-definition }}
          service: ${{ env.ECS_SERVICE }}
          cluster: ${{ env.ECS_CLUSTER }}
          wait-for-service-stability: true

---
# ============================================================
# TEMPLATE: GitHub Actions — Deploy to AWS EKS
# WHEN TO USE: Deploying to Amazon EKS via OIDC
# PREREQUISITES: EKS cluster, IAM role for OIDC
# SECRETS NEEDED: AWS_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN
# WHAT TO CHANGE: Cluster name, region, and Kustomize overlay path
# RELATED FILES: cd/kubernetes/_overlays/prod/kustomization.yaml
# MATURITY: Stable
# ============================================================

# Note 1: Resource identity and metadata drive automation, selectors, and operational traceability.
name: Deploy to AWS EKS

on:
  # Note 2: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
  workflow_run:
    workflows: ["CI"]
    # Note 3: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
    types: [completed]
    branches: [main]

# Note 4: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
env:
  AWS_REGION: us-east-1
  # Note 5: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
  EKS_CLUSTER: my-eks-cluster
  HEALTHCHECK_URL: https://app.example.com/health/ready

concurrency:
  group: deploy-aws-eks-production
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  # Note 6: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
  deploy:
    if: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'success' }}
    # Note 7: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      # Note 8: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
      id-token: write
      contents: read
    environment: production

    # Note 9: Pipeline structure separates concerns, helping teams test, deploy, and recover with smaller blast radius.
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      # Note 10: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
      - name: Configure AWS credentials (OIDC)
        uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v4
        # Note 11: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
        with:
          role-to-assume: ${{ secrets.AWS_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN }}
          # Note 12: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
          aws-region: ${{ env.AWS_REGION }}

      - name: Update kubeconfig
        # Note 13: Pipeline structure separates concerns, helping teams test, deploy, and recover with smaller blast radius.
        run: aws eks update-kubeconfig --name ${{ env.EKS_CLUSTER }} --region ${{ env.AWS_REGION }}

      - name: Login to ECR
        uses: aws-actions/amazon-ecr-login@v2

      - name: Deploy with Kustomize
        run: |
          kubectl apply -k cd/kubernetes/_overlays/prod
          kubectl rollout status deployment/app -n production --timeout=5m

      - name: Smoke test
        run: |
          for i in {1..12}; do
            if curl -fsS "$HEALTHCHECK_URL" >/dev/null; then
              echo "Smoke test passed"
              exit 0
            fi
            sleep 5
          done
          echo "Smoke test failed"
          exit 1

  rollback:
    if: ${{ failure() }}
    needs: deploy
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      id-token: write
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Configure AWS credentials (OIDC)
        uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v4
        with:
          role-to-assume: ${{ secrets.AWS_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN }}
          aws-region: ${{ env.AWS_REGION }}

      - name: Update kubeconfig

# WHAT TO CHANGE: ACR name, App Service name, Dockerfile path
# RELATED FILES: docker/dotnet/Dockerfile.api
# MATURITY: Stable
# ============================================================

# Note 1: Resource identity and metadata drive automation, selectors, and operational traceability.
name: Deploy to Azure App Service

on:
  # Note 2: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
  push:
    branches: [main]

concurrency:
  group: deploy-azure-app-service-production
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  APP_RESOURCE_GROUP: my-resource-group                  # <-- CHANGE THIS
  APP_HEALTHCHECK_URL: https://app.example.com/health   # <-- CHANGE THIS

# Note 3: Pipeline structure separates concerns, helping teams test, deploy, and recover with smaller blast radius.
jobs:
  deploy:
    # Note 4: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      id-token: write
      contents: read
    environment: production
    outputs:
      previous-image: ${{ steps.capture-current-image.outputs.image }}

    steps:
      # Note 5: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Azure Login
        # Note 6: Pipeline structure separates concerns, helping teams test, deploy, and recover with smaller blast radius.
        uses: azure/login@v2
        with:
          client-id: ${{ secrets.AZURE_CLIENT_ID }}
          tenant-id: ${{ secrets.AZURE_TENANT_ID }}
          subscription-id: ${{ secrets.AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID }}

      - name: Capture current App Service image
        id: capture-current-image
        run: |
          current_image=$(az webapp config container show \
            --name "${{ vars.APP_SERVICE_NAME }}" \
            --resource-group "$APP_RESOURCE_GROUP" \
            --query "linuxFxVersion" \
            --output tsv)
          current_image=${current_image#DOCKER|}
          echo "image=$current_image" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Build and push Docker image
        # Note 8: Pipeline structure separates concerns, helping teams test, deploy, and recover with smaller blast radius.
        run: |
          az acr build \
            # Note 9: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
            --registry ${{ vars.ACR_NAME }} \
            --image my-app:${{ github.sha }} \
            # Note 10: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
            --file docker/dotnet/Dockerfile.api \
            .

      - name: Deploy to App Service
        run: |
          az webapp config container set \
            --name "${{ vars.APP_SERVICE_NAME }}" \
            --resource-group "$APP_RESOURCE_GROUP" \
            --docker-custom-image-name "${{ vars.ACR_NAME }}.azurecr.io/my-app:${{ github.sha }}"
          az webapp restart \
            --name "${{ vars.APP_SERVICE_NAME }}" \
            --resource-group "$APP_RESOURCE_GROUP"

      - name: Smoke test
        run: |
          for i in {1..12}; do
            if curl -fsS "$APP_HEALTHCHECK_URL" >/dev/null; then
              echo "Smoke test passed"
              exit 0
            fi
            sleep 5
          done
          echo "Smoke test failed"
          exit 1

  rollback:
    if: ${{ failure() && needs.deploy.outputs.previous-image != '' }}
    needs: deploy
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      id-token: write
      contents: read
    steps:
      - name: Azure Login
        uses: azure/login@v2
        with:
          client-id: ${{ secrets.AZURE_CLIENT_ID }}
          tenant-id: ${{ secrets.AZURE_TENANT_ID }}
          subscription-id: ${{ secrets.AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID }}

      - name: Roll back to previous App Service image
        run: |
          az webapp config container set \
            --name "${{ vars.APP_SERVICE_NAME }}" \
            --resource-group "$APP_RESOURCE_GROUP" \
            --docker-custom-image-name "${{ needs.deploy.outputs.previous-image }}"
          az webapp restart \
            --name "${{ vars.APP_SERVICE_NAME }}" \
            --resource-group "$APP_RESOURCE_GROUP"

  notify-failure:
    if: ${{ failure() }}
    needs: [deploy, rollback]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Notify Slack on deployment failure
        uses: slackapi/slack-github-action@v1
        with:
          payload: |
            {
              "blocks": [
                {
                  "type": "section",
                  "text": {
                    "type": "mrkdwn",
                    "text": ":x: *${{ github.repository }}* deployment *failed*\n*Target:* `azure-app-service`\n*Environment:* `production`"
                  }
                },
                {
                  "type": "actions",
                  "elements": [
                    {
                      "type": "button",
                      "text": { "type": "plain_text", "text": "View Run" },
                      "url": "${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}"
                    }
                  ]
                }
              ]
            }
        env:
          SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL: ${{ secrets.SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL }}
          SLACK_WEBHOOK_TYPE: INCOMING_WEBHOOK

  notify-failure:
    if: ${{ failure() }}
    needs: [deploy, rollback]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Notify Slack on deployment failure
        uses: slackapi/slack-github-action@v1
        with:
          payload: |
            {
              "blocks": [
                {
                  "type": "section",
                  "text": {
                    "type": "mrkdwn",
                    "text": ":x: *${{ github.repository }}* deployment *failed*\n*Target:* `gcp-gke`\n*Environment:* `production`"
                  }
                },
                {
                  "type": "actions",
                  "elements": [
                    {
                      "type": "button",
                      "text": { "type": "plain_text", "text": "View Run" },
                      "url": "${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}"
                    }
                  ]
                }
              ]
            }
        env:
          SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL: ${{ secrets.SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL }}
          SLACK_WEBHOOK_TYPE: INCOMING_WEBHOOK

# Note 1: Resource identity and metadata drive automation, selectors, and operational traceability.
name: Deploy to OpenShift

on:

  workflow_run:
    workflows: ["CI"]
    # Note 3: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
    types: [completed]
    branches: [main]

# Note 4: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
env:
  OPENSHIFT_NAMESPACE: production
  # Note 5: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
  APP_NAME: my-app
  IMAGE: image-registry.openshift-image-registry.svc:5000/production/my-app

# Note 6: Pipeline structure separates concerns, helping teams test, deploy, and recover with smaller blast radius.
jobs:
  deploy:
    # Note 7: Control flow should stay readable; predictable branches reduce defects and simplify troubleshooting.
    if: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'success' }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Note 8: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
    permissions:
      id-token: write
      # Note 9: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
      contents: read

    steps:
      # Note 10: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Log in to OpenShift
        # Note 11: Pipeline structure separates concerns, helping teams test, deploy, and recover with smaller blast radius.

          # Note 13: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
          insecure_skip_tls_verify: false

      - name: Set project
        run: oc project ${{ env.OPENSHIFT_NAMESPACE }}

      - name: Deploy with Kustomize
        run: |
          kubectl apply -k cd/kubernetes/_overlays/prod
          kubectl rollout status deployment/${{ env.APP_NAME }} -n ${{ env.OPENSHIFT_NAMESPACE }}

      - name: Verify rollout
        run: oc get pods -n ${{ env.OPENSHIFT_NAMESPACE }} -l app=${{ env.APP_NAME }}

# GitHub Actions — Environment Protection Rules

## What is a GitHub Environment?

A GitHub Environment is a named deployment target you configure in **Settings → Environments**.
Workflows reference it with `environment: <name>`, which makes the job pause and wait for the
protection rules to be satisfied before it runs.

The **key value**: your `secrets.PROD_DB_PASSWORD` in a job that references `environment: production`
is only available if all protection gates pass. Secrets are scoped to the environment, not the repo.

---

## How to configure (one-time, per repo)

1. Go to **Settings → Environments → New environment**
2. Name it to match exactly what workflows use (`production`, `staging`, etc.)
3. Configure protection rules:

| Rule | What it does | Recommended setting |
|------|-------------|---------------------|
| **Required reviewers** | Pause until N people approve the deployment | 1–2 (prod), 0 (dev/staging) |
| **Wait timer** | Delay start N minutes after approval | 0–5 min (gives you time to cancel) |
| **Deployment branches** | Which branches can deploy to this env | `main` only for production |
| **Deployment tags** | Which tag patterns can deploy | `v*` for prod release tags |
| **Prevent self-review** | Reviewer cannot be the same person who triggered | Enable on production |

---

## Recommended environment matrix

```
┌─────────────┬──────────────┬───────────┬─────────────────────────┐
│ Environment │ Branch/Tag   │ Reviewers │ Notes                   │
├─────────────┼──────────────┼───────────┼─────────────────────────┤
│ development │ Any          │ 0         │ Auto-deploy on PR        │
│ staging     │ main         │ 0         │ Auto-deploy after merge  │
│ production  │ main / v*.*  │ 1–2       │ Manual approval required │
│ dr-failover │ main         │ 2         │ Ops team only            │
└─────────────┴──────────────┴───────────┴─────────────────────────┘
```

---

## Workflow template with environment gate

See the example below. The `environment:` key on a job is all that is needed in the YAML —
the protection rules are enforced server-side by GitHub.

```yaml
# ============================================================
# TEMPLATE: GitHub Actions — Staged deployment with environment gates
# WHEN TO USE: Any workflow that deploys to staging and production
# PREREQUISITES: Environments configured in Settings → Environments
# WHAT TO CHANGE: Lines marked  # <-- CHANGE THIS
# RELATED FILES: ci/github-actions/_strategies/matrix-build.yml
# MATURITY: Stable
# ============================================================

name: Deploy

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:           # allow manual trigger with environment selection
    inputs:
      target:
        description: "Target environment"
        required: true
        default: staging
        type: choice
        options: [staging, production]

jobs:
  # ── Build once, deploy everywhere ─────────────────────────────────
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      packages: write
      id-token: write
    outputs:
      image-digest: ${{ steps.build.outputs.digest }}
      image-tag:    ${{ steps.meta.outputs.version }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Docker metadata
        id: meta
        uses: docker/metadata-action@v5
        with:
          images: ghcr.io/${{ github.repository }}    # <-- CHANGE THIS
          tags: |
            type=sha,prefix=sha-
            type=semver,pattern={{version}}

      - name: Build and push
        id: build
        uses: docker/build-push-action@v6
        with:
          push: true
          tags: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.tags }}
          cache-from: type=gha
          cache-to:   type=gha,mode=max

  # ── Deploy to staging (no approval required) ──────────────────────
  deploy-staging:
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: staging           # <-- matches environment name in Settings → Environments
    concurrency:
      group: staging-deploy
      cancel-in-progress: false    # never cancel an in-flight deployment

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Deploy to staging
        run: |
          echo "Deploying ${{ needs.build.outputs.image-tag }} to staging"
          # kubectl set image ... or helm upgrade ...   # <-- CHANGE THIS

  # ── Deploy to production (requires approval) ──────────────────────
  deploy-production:
    needs: deploy-staging
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    # Note 1: The 'environment' key is what connects this job to the protection rules
    # configured in Settings → Environments. GitHub will pause the job here and
    # notify required reviewers before releasing the job to run.
    environment:
      name: production
      url: https://app.example.com   # <-- CHANGE THIS: shown in the deployment summary

    concurrency:
      group: production-deploy
      cancel-in-progress: false      # NEVER cancel in-progress production deploys

    permissions:
      contents: read
      id-token: write                # needed if using OIDC to cloud

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      # Note 2: Secrets scoped to the 'production' environment are ONLY available
      # inside a job that references environment: production. They are not accessible
      # to any other job, including deploy-staging.
      - name: Authenticate to cloud
        run: |
          echo "Using OIDC token to authenticate"
          # aws configure or az login --federated-token   # <-- CHANGE THIS

      - name: Deploy to production
        run: |
          echo "Deploying ${{ needs.build.outputs.image-tag }} to production"
          # kubectl set image ... or helm upgrade ...   # <-- CHANGE THIS

      - name: Notify on success
        if: success()
        uses: ./.github/workflows/notify-slack.yml    # <-- CHANGE THIS or remove
```

---

## Protecting secrets per environment

1. In **Settings → Environments → production**, add secrets (e.g. `KUBECONFIG`, `PROD_DB_URL`).
2. These secrets are NOT available to jobs targeting other environments.
3. Repository secrets are available everywhere — only use them for non-sensitive values.

```
Hierarchy (most to least restricted):
  Environment secrets   → only in jobs with matching environment:
  Repository secrets    → any job in any workflow
  Organization secrets  → any repo in the org (if policy allows)
```

---

## API / Terraform equivalent (for IaC teams)

GitHub Environments can be managed via the REST API or third-party Terraform providers.
The `github` Terraform provider supports `github_repository_environment` and
`github_repository_environment_deployment_policy` resources for GitOps-style environment config.

```hcl
resource "github_repository_environment" "production" {
  repository  = "my-repo"              # <-- CHANGE THIS
  environment = "production"

  reviewers {
    teams = [data.github_team.ops.id]  # <-- CHANGE THIS
  }

  deployment_branch_policy {
    protected_branches     = true
    custom_branch_policies = false
  }
}
```

# ============================================================
# TEMPLATE: GitHub Actions — PR Quality Gate
#   1. Conventional commit enforcer (commitlint)
#   2. PR size checker (blocks XL PRs, warns on L)
# WHEN TO USE: Add to every repo that uses release-please or
#   semantic-release. Run on every pull_request event.
# PREREQUISITES:
#   - commitlint.config.js at repo root (template in comments below)
#   - See docs/guides/conventional-commits.md for the commit format
# WHAT TO CHANGE: Lines marked  # <-- CHANGE THIS
# RELATED FILES:
#   - ci/github-actions/_strategies/release-please.yml
#   - ci/github-actions/_strategies/semantic-release.yml
#   - docs/guides/conventional-commits.md
# MATURITY: Stable
# ============================================================

name: PR Quality Gate

on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened, edited]
    branches: [main, develop]      # <-- CHANGE THIS: branches you merge into

# Note 1: Only read access is needed — this workflow never writes back to the repo.
permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: read

jobs:
  # ── Job 1: Conventional commit check ────────────────────────────────────
  # Validates every commit in the PR individually, plus the PR title
  # (useful when squash-merging — the PR title becomes the merge commit).
  commit-lint:
    name: Commit Convention Check
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          # Note 2: fetch-depth 0 gives access to all commits in the PR branch
          # so commitlint can inspect every commit, not just the latest.
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Set up Node (for commitlint)
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: "lts/*"

      - name: Install commitlint
        run: |
          npm install --no-save \
            @commitlint/cli \
            @commitlint/config-conventional

      # Note 3: We lint from the base branch to HEAD so every commit
      # in the PR is checked, not just the last one.
      - name: Lint commits in this PR
        run: |
          npx commitlint \
            --from ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }} \
            --to   ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }} \
            --verbose

      # Also lint the PR title — used when squash-merging.
      # The PR title becomes the single merge commit message.
      - name: Lint PR title
        env:
          PR_TITLE: ${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}
        run: |
          echo "$PR_TITLE" | npx commitlint --verbose

  # ── Job 2: PR size check ────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Blocks PRs that change too many lines, encourages incremental work.
  # Adjust thresholds to match your team's preference.
  pr-size:
    name: PR Size Check
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Calculate changed lines
        id: size
        env:
          BASE_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
        run: |
          # Count insertions + deletions, exclude generated/vendored files
          CHANGED=$(git diff --stat "$BASE_SHA" "$HEAD_SHA" \
            -- ':!*.lock' ':!**/vendor/**' ':!**/__generated__/**' ':!*.min.*' \
            | tail -1 \
            | grep -oP '\d+(?= insertion)' || echo 0)

          DELETED=$(git diff --stat "$BASE_SHA" "$HEAD_SHA" \
            -- ':!*.lock' ':!**/vendor/**' ':!**/__generated__/**' ':!*.min.*' \
            | tail -1 \
            | grep -oP '\d+(?= deletion)' || echo 0)

          TOTAL=$((CHANGED + DELETED))
          echo "total=$TOTAL" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "PR changes $TOTAL lines (additions + deletions, excluding generated files)"

      # Note 4: Size thresholds — adjust to your team's norms.
      #   XS  <  50 lines  — config tweak, doc update
      #   S   < 200 lines  — typical bug fix
      #   M   < 500 lines  — feature
      #   L   < 800 lines  — large feature (warn)
      #   XL  ≥ 800 lines  — block and require justification  # <-- CHANGE THIS threshold
      - name: Enforce size limit
        env:
          TOTAL: ${{ steps.size.outputs.total }}
          WARN_THRESHOLD: 500      # <-- CHANGE THIS
          FAIL_THRESHOLD: 800      # <-- CHANGE THIS
        run: |
          echo "Changed lines: $TOTAL"

          if [ "$TOTAL" -ge "$FAIL_THRESHOLD" ]; then
            echo ""
            echo "❌ PR is too large ($TOTAL lines ≥ $FAIL_THRESHOLD limit)."
            echo ""
            echo "Large PRs are hard to review safely and increase merge risk."
            echo "Please split this PR into smaller, focused changes."
            echo "If this is unavoidable (e.g. a migration), add the label"
            echo "'large-pr-approved' and a comment explaining why."
            exit 1
          fi

          if [ "$TOTAL" -ge "$WARN_THRESHOLD" ]; then
            echo ""
            echo "⚠️  PR is large ($TOTAL lines ≥ $WARN_THRESHOLD warning threshold)."
            echo "Consider splitting into smaller PRs for easier review."
          fi

          echo "✅ PR size is acceptable ($TOTAL lines)"

      # Note 5: Override gate — if the PR has the 'large-pr-approved' label,
      # skip the size check. Useful for migrations and large refactors.
      - name: Check for large-pr-approved label override
        if: failure()
        env:
          LABELS: ${{ toJson(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name) }}
        run: |
          if echo "$LABELS" | grep -q "large-pr-approved"; then
            echo "Label 'large-pr-approved' found — overriding size check."
            exit 0
          fi
          exit 1

# ============================================================
# TEMPLATE: GitHub Actions — Reusable Artifact Attestation
#   Provides SLSA provenance + SBOM + cosign image signing
#   for any container image built in this repo.
#
# WHEN TO USE: Call from any workflow that builds and pushes
#   a Docker image. Replaces the inline SBOM step that only
#   some workflows had, giving consistent coverage everywhere.
#
# WHAT THIS PROVIDES:
#   1. SBOM (SPDX-JSON) — attached as OCI referrer and uploaded
#      as a workflow artifact. Satisfies supply-chain audit requirements.
#   2. SLSA provenance attestation — signed by GitHub's OIDC token
#      via actions/attest-build-provenance. Meets SLSA Build L2.
#   3. cosign keyless signing — signs the image digest in Sigstore's
#      transparency log (Rekor). Verifiable without managing keys.
#
# SLSA levels in this template:
#   L1: Provenance exists (attestation written)
#   L2: Provenance is signed (GitHub OIDC token, Sigstore Rekor)
#   L3: Requires hermetic builds on GitHub-hosted runners with no
#       network access — not covered here; needs slsa-framework/slsa-github-generator
#
# PREREQUISITES:
#   - Image already built and pushed (pass the digest as input)
#   - Calling job needs: id-token: write, attestations: write, packages: write
# WHAT TO CHANGE: Lines marked  # <-- CHANGE THIS
# RELATED FILES:
#   - ci/github-actions/dotnet/docker-publish.yml
#   - ci/github-actions/_shared/reusable-docker-build.yml
# MATURITY: Stable
# ============================================================

name: Reusable Artifact Attestation

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      image-ref:
        description: "Full image reference including digest, e.g. ghcr.io/org/app@sha256:abc123"
        required: true
        type: string
      image-digest:
        description: "Image digest (sha256:...) returned by docker/build-push-action"
        required: true
        type: string
      sbom-artifact-name:
        description: "Name for the uploaded SBOM artifact"
        required: false
        type: string
        default: sbom-${{ github.sha }}.spdx.json
    secrets:
      registry-token:
        description: "Token with push access to the registry (for cosign)"
        required: true

jobs:
  attest:
    name: Sign & Attest
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    # Note 1: These three permissions are ALL required.
    # id-token: write   — lets cosign get an OIDC token from GitHub, no keys needed
    # attestations: write — lets actions/attest-build-provenance write attestations
    # packages: write   — lets cosign push the signature/attestation to GHCR
    permissions:
      id-token: write
      attestations: write
      packages: write

    steps:
      # ── SBOM ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
      # Note 2: anchore/sbom-action scans the image layers and produces an SPDX
      # JSON SBOM. It attaches it to the image as an OCI referrer (so it stays
      # with the image in the registry) AND uploads it as a workflow artifact.
      - name: Generate SBOM
        uses: anchore/sbom-action@v0
        with:
          image:         ${{ inputs.image-ref }}
          format:        spdx-json
          output-file:   sbom.spdx.json
          upload-artifact: true
          artifact-name: ${{ inputs.sbom-artifact-name }}

      # ── SLSA provenance attestation ────────────────────────────────────────
      # Note 3: actions/attest-build-provenance writes a signed SLSA provenance
      # attestation that records: the workflow that triggered the build, the
      # git ref + SHA, the repository, and the build runner. It is signed using
      # the job's OIDC token so no secrets are needed.
      # Verify with: gh attestation verify <image> --repo <owner/repo>
      - name: Attest build provenance
        uses: actions/attest-build-provenance@v1
        with:
          subject-name:   ${{ inputs.image-ref }}
          subject-digest: ${{ inputs.image-digest }}
          push-to-registry: true  # attaches attestation as OCI referrer in registry

      # ── cosign keyless image signing ────────────────────────────────────────
      # Note 4: cosign signs the image digest using Sigstore's keyless flow:
      #   1. Gets an OIDC token from GitHub (the job's id-token)
      #   2. Exchanges it for a short-lived certificate from Fulcio (Sigstore CA)
      #   3. Creates a signature and records it in Rekor (public transparency log)
      # No private keys are stored anywhere. The identity claim in the cert is
      # the GitHub Actions workflow URL, making it auditable.
      - name: Install cosign
        uses: sigstore/cosign-installer@v3

      - name: Log in to registry for cosign
        uses: docker/login-action@v3
        with:
          registry: ghcr.io                         # <-- CHANGE THIS if using ACR/ECR/Artifact Registry
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.registry-token }}

      - name: Sign image with cosign (keyless)
        env:
          COSIGN_EXPERIMENTAL: "1"   # enables keyless (OIDC) signing
        run: |
          cosign sign --yes \
            ${{ inputs.image-ref }}

          echo ""
          echo "Image signed. To verify on any machine:"
          echo "  cosign verify \\"
          echo "    --certificate-identity-regexp 'https://github.com/${{ github.repository }}' \\"
          echo "    --certificate-oidc-issuer     'https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com' \\"
          echo "    ${{ inputs.image-ref }}"

      # ── Verify (self-check) ────────────────────────────────────────────────
      # Note 5: Verify the signature immediately after signing as a sanity check.
      # This catches registry connectivity issues and misconfigured OIDC issuers
      # before the image is deployed.
      - name: Verify cosign signature
        env:
          COSIGN_EXPERIMENTAL: "1"
        run: |
          cosign verify \
            --certificate-identity-regexp "https://github.com/${{ github.repository }}" \
            --certificate-oidc-issuer     "https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com" \
            ${{ inputs.image-ref }}

# ============================================================
# HOW TO CALL THIS WORKFLOW

# ============================================================
# TEMPLATE: GitHub Actions — Reusable Docker Build & Push
# WHEN TO USE: Call from any workflow that needs to build and push images
# PREREQUISITES: Container registry accessible from GitHub Actions
# SECRETS NEEDED: registry-token (e.g., GITHUB_TOKEN for GHCR)
# WHAT TO CHANGE: Inputs when calling this workflow
# RELATED FILES: ci/github-actions/dotnet/docker-publish.yml
# MATURITY: Stable
# ============================================================

# Note 1: Resource identity and metadata drive automation, selectors, and operational traceability.
name: Reusable Docker Build

on:
  # Note 2: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      # Note 3: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
      image-name:
        required: true
        # Note 4: This declaration defines a reusable unit, which supports composition and makes behavior easier to test.
        type: string
      dockerfile:
        # Note 5: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
        required: false
        type: string
        # Note 6: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
        default: Dockerfile
      context:
        # Note 7: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
        required: false
        type: string
        # Note 8: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
        default: .
    secrets:
      # Note 9: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
      registry-token:
        required: true
    outputs:
      # Note 10: Expose the image digest so callers can pass it to the attest
      # reusable workflow (reusable-attest.yml) for SBOM + cosign signing.
      image-digest:
        description: "sha256 digest of the pushed image"
        value: ${{ jobs.docker-build.outputs.image-digest }}

# Note 11: Pipeline structure separates concerns, helping teams test, deploy, and recover with smaller blast radius.
jobs:
  docker-build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      image-digest: ${{ steps.build-push.outputs.digest }}
    permissions:
      # Note 12: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
      contents: read
      packages: write

    # Note 13: Pipeline structure separates concerns, helping teams test, deploy, and recover with smaller blast radius.
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      # Note 14: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
      - name: Log in to GHCR
        uses: docker/login-action@v3
        # Note 15: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
        with:
          registry: ghcr.io
          # Note 16: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.registry-token }}

      # Note 17: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
      - name: Set up Buildx
        uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3

      # Note 18: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
      - name: Docker metadata
        id: meta
        uses: docker/metadata-action@v5
        with:
          images: ghcr.io/${{ inputs.image-name }}
          tags: |
            type=sha
            type=ref,event=branch

      - name: Build and push
        id: build-push          # id required so outputs.digest is accessible
        uses: docker/build-push-action@v6
        with:
          context: ${{ inputs.context }}
          file: ${{ inputs.dockerfile }}
          push: true
          tags: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.tags }}
          cache-from: type=gha
          cache-to: type=gha,mode=max

        type: string
    # Note 6: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
    secrets:
      slack-webhook:
        # Note 7: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
        required: true

jobs:
  # Note 8: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
  notify:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Note 9: Pipeline structure separates concerns, helping teams test, deploy, and recover with smaller blast radius.
    steps:
      - name: Send Slack notification
        # Note 10: Pipeline structure separates concerns, helping teams test, deploy, and recover with smaller blast radius.
        uses: slackapi/slack-github-action@v1
        with:
          # Note 11: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
          payload: |
            {
              # Note 12: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
              "text": "${{ inputs.status == 'success' && '✅' || '❌' }} *${{ github.repository }}* — ${{ inputs.message || github.workflow }} (${{ github.ref_name }})",

        env:

# ============================================================
# TEMPLATE: GitHub Actions - Reusable Supply Chain Verify
# WHEN TO USE: Pull request check to verify a referenced image is already signed
# PREREQUISITES: OIDC issuer and expected certificate identity pattern are known
# SECRETS NEEDED: None
# WHAT TO CHANGE: Inputs passed from caller pipeline
# RELATED FILES: secops/supply-chain/cosign-verify-policy.yaml
# MATURITY: Stable
# ============================================================

name: Reusable Supply Chain Verify

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      image-ref:
        description: Fully qualified image reference to verify.
        required: true
        type: string
      certificate-identity-regexp:
        description: Expected identity regex in cosign certificate.
        required: true
        type: string
      certificate-oidc-issuer:
        description: Expected OIDC issuer in cosign certificate.
        required: false
        type: string
        default: https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com
      soft-fail:
        description: When true, keep PR green while still surfacing verification failure.
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false

jobs:
  verify-image-signature:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      id-token: write
    steps:
      - name: Install cosign
        uses: sigstore/cosign-installer@v3.8.2 # <-- UPDATE QUARTERLY

      - name: Verify image signature
        id: verify
        continue-on-error: true
        run: |
          # CI verification is a shift-left check; Kyverno admission policies are the
          # enforcement gate at deploy time and should still remain enabled.
          # Risk note: never run bare `cosign verify <image>` because it does not restrict
          # trusted identity scope without explicit certificate checks.
          cosign verify \
            --certificate-identity-regexp "${{ inputs.certificate-identity-regexp }}" \
            --certificate-oidc-issuer "${{ inputs.certificate-oidc-issuer }}" \
            "${{ inputs.image-ref }}"

      - name: Fail if signature verification failed
        if: steps.verify.outcome == 'failure' && !inputs.soft-fail
        run: |
          echo "Image signature verification failed for ${{ inputs.image-ref }}"
          exit 1

      - name: Audit-only warning when soft-fail is enabled
        if: steps.verify.outcome == 'failure' && inputs.soft-fail
        run: |
          echo "[AUDIT MODE] Signature verification failed for ${{ inputs.image-ref }}"
          echo "Enable hard fail by setting soft-fail to false in the caller workflow."

# ============================================================
# TEMPLATE: GitHub Actions - Reusable Supply Chain Security
# WHEN TO USE: Call after Docker build/push to sign image and attach attestations
# PREREQUISITES: Image already pushed to registry and OIDC federation configured
# SECRETS NEEDED: registry-token (for registry login if required)
# WHAT TO CHANGE: Inputs when calling this workflow and identity regex defaults
# RELATED FILES: ci/github-actions/_shared/reusable-docker-build.yml
# MATURITY: Stable
# ============================================================

name: Reusable Supply Chain Security

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      image-name:
        description: Repository/image name, matching reusable-docker-build input.
        required: true
        type: string
      image-tag:
        description: Immutable tag or digest selector to attest, matching caller convention.
        required: true
        type: string
      registry:
        description: OCI registry hostname.
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ghcr.io
      certificate-identity-regexp:
        description: Expected GitHub workflow identity pattern for keyless verification.
        required: false
        type: string
        default: "https://github.com/.*/.github/workflows/.*"
      certificate-oidc-issuer:
        description: Expected OIDC issuer for keyless certificates.
        required: false
        type: string
        default: "https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com"
    secrets:
      registry-token:
        required: true

env:
  IMAGE_REF: ${{ inputs.registry }}/${{ inputs.image-name }}:${{ inputs.image-tag }}

jobs:
  sign-image:
    name: sign-image
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      id-token: write
      packages: write
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4.2.2 # <-- UPDATE QUARTERLY

      - name: Install cosign
        uses: sigstore/cosign-installer@v3.8.2 # <-- UPDATE QUARTERLY

      - name: Log in to registry
        uses: docker/login-action@v3.3.0 # <-- UPDATE QUARTERLY
        with:
          registry: ${{ inputs.registry }}
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.registry-token }}

      - name: Sign image with keyless OIDC and Rekor transparency log
        env:
          COSIGN_EXPERIMENTAL: "1"
        run: |
          # Keyless signing means no private key is stored anywhere; a short-lived cert
          # is minted from this workflow's OIDC identity and recorded in Rekor.
          cosign sign --yes "${IMAGE_REF}"

      - name: Verify signature as CI self-check
        env:
          COSIGN_EXPERIMENTAL: "1"
        run: |
          # Risk note: bare `cosign verify <image>` can trust unexpected identities;
          # always pin expected identity and issuer to prevent confused-deputy trust.
          cosign verify \
            --certificate-identity-regexp "${{ inputs.certificate-identity-regexp }}" \
            --certificate-oidc-issuer "${{ inputs.certificate-oidc-issuer }}" \
            "${IMAGE_REF}"

  generate-sbom:
    name: generate-sbom
    needs: sign-image
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      id-token: write
      packages: write
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4.2.2 # <-- UPDATE QUARTERLY

      - name: Install cosign
        uses: sigstore/cosign-installer@v3.8.2 # <-- UPDATE QUARTERLY

      - name: Generate SBOM in SPDX-JSON format
        uses: anchore/sbom-action@v0.17.1 # <-- UPDATE QUARTERLY
        with:
          image: ${{ env.IMAGE_REF }}
          format: spdx-json
          output-file: sbom.spdx.json

      - name: Upload raw SBOM artifact
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4.4.3 # <-- UPDATE QUARTERLY
        with:
          name: sbom-${{ github.run_id }}
          path: sbom.spdx.json

      - name: Attach SBOM attestation with cosign
        env:
          COSIGN_EXPERIMENTAL: "1"
        run: |
          # SPDX-JSON is used instead of CycloneDX because Kyverno SBOM verification
          # in secops/supply-chain/sbom-policy.yaml expects predicate type https://spdx.dev/Document.
          cosign attest --yes \
            --predicate sbom.spdx.json \
            --type spdx \
            "${IMAGE_REF}"

  generate-slsa-provenance:
    name: generate-slsa-provenance
    needs: generate-sbom
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      id-token: write
      packages: write
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4.2.2 # <-- UPDATE QUARTERLY

      - name: Install cosign
        uses: sigstore/cosign-installer@v3.8.2 # <-- UPDATE QUARTERLY

      - name: Generate SLSA provenance predicate
        id: slsa-generator
        uses: slsa-framework/slsa-github-generator/actions/generator@3a9d8b6a5f1f72a806d4dc7b8d47f8f8f9ab2c10 # <-- UPDATE QUARTERLY
        with:
          base64-subjects: "${{ env.IMAGE_REF }}"
          upload-assets: false

      - name: Write provenance to file
        run: |
          echo '${{ steps.slsa-generator.outputs.provenance }}' > provenance.intoto.jsonl

      - name: Attach SLSA provenance attestation
        env:
          COSIGN_EXPERIMENTAL: "1"
        run: |
          # Supply chain tools must be pinned to immutable SHAs to prevent workflow drift
          # and dependency substitution attacks from floating tags.
          cosign attest --yes \
            --predicate provenance.intoto.jsonl \
            --type slsaprovenance \
            "${IMAGE_REF}"

# ============================================================
# TEMPLATE: GitHub Actions — Matrix Build Strategy
# WHEN TO USE: Testing across multiple OS / runtime versions

# RELATED FILES: None

# Note 1: Resource identity and metadata drive automation, selectors, and operational traceability.
name: Matrix Build Example

on:
  # Note 2: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
  push:
    branches: [main]

# Note 3: Pipeline structure separates concerns, helping teams test, deploy, and recover with smaller blast radius.
jobs:
  build:
    # Note 4: Resource identity and metadata drive automation, selectors, and operational traceability.
    name: Build (${{ matrix.os }} / ${{ matrix.node }})
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}

    # Note 5: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false  # Don't cancel other matrix jobs on failure
      # Note 6: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-latest, windows-latest, macos-latest]
        # Note 7: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
        node: ["18", "20"]
        exclude:
          # Note 8: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
          - os: macos-latest
            node: "18"  # Skip this combination

    # Note 9: Pipeline structure separates concerns, helping teams test, deploy, and recover with smaller blast radius.
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      # Note 10: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
      - name: Setup Node ${{ matrix.node }}
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        # Note 11: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
        with:
          node-version: ${{ matrix.node }}

      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm test

# TEMPLATE: GitHub Actions — Monorepo Affected Services
# WHEN TO USE: Monorepos with multiple services in subdirectories
# PREREQUISITES: dorny/paths-filter action, per-service workflows
# SECRETS NEEDED: None
