# Note 1: Resource identity and metadata drive automation, selectors, and operational traceability.
name: Monorepo — Build Affected Services

on:
  # Note 2: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
  push:
    branches: [main]
  # Note 3: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]

# Note 4: Pipeline structure separates concerns, helping teams test, deploy, and recover with smaller blast radius.
jobs:
  detect-changes:
    # Note 5: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      # Note 6: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
      user-service: ${{ steps.filter.outputs.user-service }}
      order-service: ${{ steps.filter.outputs.order-service }}
      # Note 7: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
      api-gateway: ${{ steps.filter.outputs.api-gateway }}

    steps:
      # Note 8: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: dorny/paths-filter@v3
        # Note 9: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
        id: filter
        with:
          # Note 10: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
          filters: |
            user-service:
              # Note 11: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
              - 'services/user-service/**'
            order-service:
              # Note 12: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
              - 'services/order-service/**'
            api-gateway:
              # Note 13: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
              - 'services/api-gateway/**'
              - 'shared/**'  # Shared changes affect gateway

  # Note 14: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
  build-user-service:
    needs: detect-changes
    if: needs.detect-changes.outputs.user-service == 'true'
    uses: ./.github/workflows/build-service.yml
    with:
      service: user-service

  build-order-service:
    needs: detect-changes
    if: needs.detect-changes.outputs.order-service == 'true'
    uses: ./.github/workflows/build-service.yml
    with:
      service: order-service

    steps:

        # Note 7: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.

        with:
          # Note 8: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.

          # Reads conventional commits to bump version automatically

      # Only run on release (not on every push)
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        # Note 9: Control flow should stay readable; predictable branches reduce defects and simplify troubleshooting.
        if: ${{ steps.release.outputs.release_created }}

      - name: Publish to npm
        # Note 10: Control flow should stay readable; predictable branches reduce defects and simplify troubleshooting.
        if: ${{ steps.release.outputs.release_created }}
        run: |
          # Note 11: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.

# ============================================================
# TEMPLATE: GitHub Actions — semantic-release (non-Node stacks)
# WHEN TO USE: Automated versioning + changelog for Python, Go,
#              .NET, Java, or Ruby repos where release-please is
#              not a natural fit. semantic-release runs on every
#              push to main and cuts a release directly (no PR).
# PREREQUISITES:
#   - Conventional Commits in every commit (see docs/guides/conventional-commits.md)
#   - .releaserc.json at repo root (example provided below)
#   - Node.js available in the runner (only for running semantic-release itself)
# SECRETS NEEDED: GITHUB_TOKEN (automatic), NPM_TOKEN only if publishing to npm
# WHAT TO CHANGE: Lines marked  # <-- CHANGE THIS
# RELATED FILES:
#   - ci/github-actions/_strategies/release-please.yml (alternative)
#   - ci/github-actions/_shared/pr-conventional-commit.yml (enforcer)
#   - docs/guides/conventional-commits.md
# MATURITY: Stable
# ============================================================

name: Semantic Release

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main             # <-- CHANGE THIS: add 'beta' or 'next' for pre-release channels

# Note 1: semantic-release needs write access to push the release commit,
# create the tag, and post the GitHub Release. id-token is only required
# if you add an OIDC-based cloud publish step below.
permissions:
  contents: write
  issues: write
  pull-requests: write
  id-token: write

jobs:
  release:
    name: Cut Release
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Note 2: Concurrency ensures only one release runs at a time on main.
    # cancel-in-progress: false is intentional — we never want to drop a release mid-flight.
    concurrency:
      group: semantic-release
      cancel-in-progress: false

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0          # full history needed for changelog generation
          persist-credentials: false  # use GITHUB_TOKEN from env, not git credential store

      # ── Language-specific build/test step ─────────────────────────────────
      # Run your existing build before cutting the release so a broken build
      # cannot produce a new version tag.

      # Python example
      - name: Set up Python
        if: false                 # <-- CHANGE THIS: remove this 'if: false' to enable
        uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:

        uses: actions/setup-go@v5
        with:
          go-version: "1.22"      # <-- CHANGE THIS

        uses: actions/setup-dotnet@v4
        with:

      - name: .NET build & test
        if: false                 # <-- CHANGE THIS
        run: |
          dotnet build --configuration Release
          dotnet test --no-build --verbosity normal
      # ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

      # semantic-release is a Node package, but it works for any language repo.
      # It reads .releaserc.json, parses commits, and creates the GitHub Release.
      - name: Set up Node (for semantic-release only)
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: "lts/*"

      - name: Install semantic-release
        run: |
          npm install --no-save \
            semantic-release \
            @semantic-release/commit-analyzer \
            @semantic-release/release-notes-generator \
            @semantic-release/changelog \
            @semantic-release/git \
            @semantic-release/github
          # Optional extras:                                  # <-- CHANGE THIS

          # @semantic-release/npm             — bump package.json version
          # semantic-release-pypi             — publish to PyPI
          # @semantic-release/slack-notify    — post Slack message on release

      - name: Run semantic-release

          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          # NPM_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}              # <-- CHANGE THIS: uncomment for npm publish
          # PYPI_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.PYPI_TOKEN }}            # <-- CHANGE THIS: uncomment for PyPI
        run: npx semantic-release

# ============================================================
# TEMPLATE: GitHub Actions — .NET Docker Build & Publish
# WHEN TO USE: Publishing .NET container images to GHCR or ACR
# PREREQUISITES: Dockerfile in the repository
# SECRETS NEEDED: GITHUB_TOKEN (automatic for GHCR)
# WHAT TO CHANGE: Lines marked with # <-- CHANGE THIS
# RELATED FILES: docker/dotnet/Dockerfile.api
# MATURITY: Stable
# ============================================================

# Note 1: Resource identity and metadata drive automation, selectors, and operational traceability.
name: .NET Docker Build & Publish

on:
  # Note 2: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
  push:
    branches: [main]
    # Note 3: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
    tags: ["v*.*.*"]

env:
  # Note 4: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
  REGISTRY: ghcr.io
  IMAGE_NAME: ${{ github.repository }}

# Note 5: Pipeline structure separates concerns, helping teams test, deploy, and recover with smaller blast radius.
jobs:
  docker:
    # Note 6: Resource identity and metadata drive automation, selectors, and operational traceability.
    name: Build & Push Docker Image
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Note 7: Pass the image digest forward so the attest job can sign the exact
    # immutable digest rather than a mutable tag.
    outputs:
      image-digest: ${{ steps.build-push.outputs.digest }}
    # Note 8: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
    permissions:
      contents: read
      packages: write

    steps:
      # Note 9: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Log in to Container Registry
        # Note 10: Pipeline structure separates concerns, helping teams test, deploy, and recover with smaller blast radius.
        uses: docker/login-action@v3
        with:
          # Note 11: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
          registry: ${{ env.REGISTRY }}
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          # Note 12: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      - name: Extract Docker metadata
        # Note 13: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
        id: meta
        uses: docker/metadata-action@v5
        # Note 14: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
        with:
          images: ${{ env.REGISTRY }}/${{ env.IMAGE_NAME }}
          # Note 15: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
          tags: |
            type=semver,pattern={{version}}
            type=semver,pattern={{major}}.{{minor}}
            type=sha,prefix=sha-
            type=raw,value=latest,enable=${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' }}

      - name: Set up Docker Buildx
        uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3

      - name: Build and push
        id: build-push
        uses: docker/build-push-action@v6
        with:
          context: .
          file: docker/dotnet/Dockerfile.api                 # <-- CHANGE THIS: path to your Dockerfile
          push: true
          tags: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.tags }}
          labels: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.labels }}
          cache-from: type=gha
          cache-to: type=gha,mode=max

  # ── Attestation job — SBOM + SLSA provenance + cosign signing ──────────────
  # Note 9: Runs after the build job completes. Uses the reusable workflow that
  # consistently applies SBOM generation, SLSA provenance attestation, and
  # cosign keyless signing across all images in this repo.
  attest:
    name: Sign & Attest
    needs: docker
    uses: ./.github/workflows/reusable-attest.yml      # <-- CHANGE THIS to your workflow path
    permissions:
      id-token:     write
      attestations: write
      packages:     write
    with:
      image-ref:    ghcr.io/${{ github.repository }}@${{ needs.docker.outputs.image-digest }}
      image-digest: ${{ needs.docker.outputs.image-digest }}
      sbom-artifact-name: sbom-dotnet-${{ github.sha }}.spdx.json
    secrets:
      registry-token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

# Note 1: Resource identity and metadata drive automation, selectors, and operational traceability.

jobs:

    # Note 5: Resource identity and metadata drive automation, selectors, and operational traceability.
    name: Build & Test
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    # Note 6: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
    strategy:
      matrix:
        # Note 7: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
        go-version: ["1.23", "1.24"]            # <-- CHANGE THIS: your supported Go versions

    steps:
      # Note 8: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up Go ${{ matrix.go-version }}
        # Note 9: Pipeline structure separates concerns, helping teams test, deploy, and recover with smaller blast radius.
        uses: actions/setup-go@v5
        with:
          # Note 10: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
          go-version: ${{ matrix.go-version }}
          cache: true                            # Caches ~/go/pkg/mod and ~/.cache/go-build

      # Note 11: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
      - name: Download dependencies
        run: go mod download

      # Note 12: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
      - name: Verify dependencies
        run: go mod verify

      # Note 13: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
      - name: Lint with golangci-lint
        uses: golangci/golangci-lint-action@v6
        # Note 14: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
        with:
          version: latest
          # Note 15: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
          args: --timeout=5m

      - name: Vet
        # Note 16: Pipeline structure separates concerns, helping teams test, deploy, and recover with smaller blast radius.
        run: go vet ./...

      - name: Test with coverage
        # Note 17: Pipeline structure separates concerns, helping teams test, deploy, and recover with smaller blast radius.
        run: go test -v -race -coverprofile=coverage.out -covermode=atomic ./...

      - name: Check coverage threshold
        # Note 18: Pipeline structure separates concerns, helping teams test, deploy, and recover with smaller blast radius.
        run: |
          COVERAGE=$(go tool cover -func=coverage.out | grep total | awk '{print $3}' | sed 's/%//')
          # Note 19: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
          echo "Total coverage: ${COVERAGE}%"
          THRESHOLD=70                           # <-- CHANGE THIS: your minimum coverage
          # Note 20: Control flow should stay readable; predictable branches reduce defects and simplify troubleshooting.
          if (( $(echo "$COVERAGE < $THRESHOLD" | bc -l) )); then
            echo "::error::Coverage ${COVERAGE}% is below threshold ${THRESHOLD}%"
            # Note 21: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
            exit 1
          fi

      # Note 22: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
      - name: Upload coverage

        # Note 23: Pipeline structure separates concerns, helping teams test, deploy, and recover with smaller blast radius.
        uses: codecov/codecov-action@v5

          file: coverage.out

      - name: Build
        # Note 25: Pipeline structure separates concerns, helping teams test, deploy, and recover with smaller blast radius.
        run: go build -v ./...

  # Build Docker image on main branch

    permissions:

          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      - name: Set up Docker Buildx
        uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3

      - name: Extract Docker metadata
        id: meta
        uses: docker/metadata-action@v5
        with:
          images: ghcr.io/${{ github.repository }}
          tags: |

# ============================================================
# TEMPLATE: Terraform Cost Estimation with Infracost
# WHEN TO USE: On every pull request that changes Terraform files.
#   Posts a monthly cost diff table as a PR comment so the team
#   can review cost impact before merging.
#
# PREREQUISITES:
#   - Infracost API key from https://www.infracost.io/docs/
#   - Add INFRACOST_API_KEY to GitHub repository secrets
#   - Cloud credentials (AWS/Azure/GCP) available as GitHub secrets or OIDC role
#
# WHAT TO CHANGE: Lines marked  # <-- CHANGE THIS
# RELATED FILES: ci/github-actions/terraform/plan-apply.yml
#                terraform/aws-eks/, terraform/azure-aks/
# MATURITY: Stable
# ============================================================

name: Terraform Cost Estimation

on:
  pull_request:
    branches:
      - main        # <-- CHANGE THIS
    paths:
      - "terraform/**"   # <-- CHANGE THIS: adjust to your Terraform root

# Note 1: Read access to contents and write access to pull-requests are the minimum
# permissions needed: read code + post the cost comment on the PR.
permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: write

# Note 2: One concurrent cost estimation job per branch avoids comment spam on
# rapidly-updated PRs. If a new push arrives while the previous run is in progress,
# the in-progress run is cancelled and the new one starts fresh.
concurrency:
  group: infracost-${{ github.head_ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  cost-estimation:
    name: Cost Estimation
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20

    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      # Note 3: Infracost is a free, open-source CLI that reads a Terraform plan (or
      # HCL directly with --path) and prices each resource using cloud provider APIs.
      # The API key is used to pull up-to-date pricing data from infracost.io.
      # Without a key the job runs in degraded mode: known prices are used but
      # the comment will note which resources have estimated costs.
      - name: Setup Infracost
        uses: infracost/actions/setup@v3
        with:
          api-key: ${{ secrets.INFRACOST_API_KEY }}   # <-- CHANGE THIS: add to GitHub secrets

      # Note 4: We run Infracost against the base branch first so we can compute
      # the DIFF (cost change introduced by this PR) rather than the total cost.
      # This is far more useful in reviews: "this PR adds $12/month" is actionable;
      # "the infrastructure costs $3,400/month" is just noise.
      - name: Generate cost estimate for base branch
        run: |
          infracost breakdown \
            --path="${{ env.TF_WORKING_DIR }}" \
            --terraform-var-file="${{ env.TF_VAR_FILE }}" \
            --format=json \
            --out-file=/tmp/infracost-base.json
        env:
          TF_WORKING_DIR: terraform/aws-eks    # <-- CHANGE THIS: path to your Terraform module
          TF_VAR_FILE: environments/production.tfvars   # <-- CHANGE THIS: or remove if unused
          # Note 5: Cloud credentials for Infracost to call pricing APIs.
          # For AWS: provide AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID + AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY or use OIDC.
          # For Azure: provide ARM_CLIENT_ID + ARM_CLIENT_SECRET + ARM_TENANT_ID + ARM_SUBSCRIPTION_ID.
          # For GCP: provide GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS pointing to a service account key file.
          AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID: ${{ secrets.AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID }}        # <-- CHANGE THIS
          AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY: ${{ secrets.AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY }} # <-- CHANGE THIS
          AWS_DEFAULT_REGION: us-east-1                               # <-- CHANGE THIS

      - name: Checkout PR branch
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}

      - name: Generate cost estimate for PR branch
        run: |
          infracost breakdown \
            --path="${{ env.TF_WORKING_DIR }}" \
            --terraform-var-file="${{ env.TF_VAR_FILE }}" \
            --format=json \
            --out-file=/tmp/infracost-pr.json
        env:
          TF_WORKING_DIR: terraform/aws-eks              # <-- CHANGE THIS: same as above
          TF_VAR_FILE: environments/production.tfvars   # <-- CHANGE THIS: same as above
          AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID: ${{ secrets.AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID }}
          AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY: ${{ secrets.AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY }}
          AWS_DEFAULT_REGION: us-east-1                  # <-- CHANGE THIS

      # Note 6: `infracost diff` computes the delta between base and PR estimates.
      # It outputs a markdown table with:
      #   - Resources that will be added (green +)
      #   - Resources that will be removed (red -)
      #   - Existing resources whose cost changes (e.g., instance resize)
      #   - A total monthly cost change (+/- $X/month)
      - name: Generate cost diff
        run: |
          infracost diff \
            --path=/tmp/infracost-pr.json \
            --compare-to=/tmp/infracost-base.json \
            --format=json \
            --out-file=/tmp/infracost-diff.json

      # Note 7: Post the diff as a PR comment. Infracost will update the comment
      # if the workflow runs again on the same PR (identified by the comment header).
      # The `--policy-path` flag lets you enforce cost gates (e.g., fail if diff > $500/month);
      # see infracost.io/docs/features/cost_policies for details.
      - name: Post cost diff to PR
        uses: infracost/actions/comment@v3
        with:
          path: /tmp/infracost-diff.json
          behavior: update    # Note 8: 'update' replaces the previous comment; 'new' posts a new one each time

      # Note 9: soft_fail: true means a missing API key or pricing error does NOT
      # fail the PR. Cost estimation is advisory; teams should not block deploys
      # purely on cost failures. If you want to enforce a budget gate, remove this
      # line and add --policy-path to the infracost diff command above.
      - name: Check cost policy (optional gate)
        run: |
          infracost comment github \
            --path=/tmp/infracost-diff.json \
            --repo=${{ github.repository }} \
            --pull-request=${{ github.event.pull_request.number }} \
            --github-token=${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }} \
            --behavior=update \
            --log-level=warn || true   # <-- Remove '|| true' to make cost overruns block the PR

---
# ============================================================
# TEMPLATE: GitHub Actions — Terraform Drift Detection
# WHEN TO USE: Detect when live infrastructure diverges from the
#   Terraform state (someone applied changes outside Terraform, a
#   cloud provider changed defaults, etc.). Runs daily on a schedule.
#   Opens a GitHub Issue automatically when drift is found.
# PREREQUISITES:
#   - Terraform state in a remote backend (S3, Azure, GCS)
#   - Cloud credentials as GitHub Actions OIDC secrets
#   - GitHub token with Issues write permission
# WHAT TO CHANGE: Lines marked  # <-- CHANGE THIS
# RELATED FILES:
#   ci/github-actions/terraform/plan-apply.yml
#   terraform/aws-eks/main.tf  (or whichever module to monitor)
# MATURITY: Stable
# ============================================================

name: Terraform Drift Detection

on:
  # Note 1: Schedule runs at 06:00 UTC daily — adjust to match your team's
  # working hours so the issue appears when someone is online to triage it.
  schedule:
    - cron: "0 6 * * 1-5"   # <-- CHANGE THIS: Mon-Fri 06:00 UTC (skip weekends)
  # Note 2: workflow_dispatch lets you trigger a manual drift check without
  # waiting for the schedule — useful after an incident or bulk change.
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      environment:
        description: "Environment to check for drift"
        required: true
        default: "production"
        type: choice
        options:
          - production
          - staging
          - development

env:
  TF_VERSION:     "1.10.0"          # <-- CHANGE THIS: keep in sync with plan-apply.yml
  TF_WORKING_DIR: "terraform/aws-eks"  # <-- CHANGE THIS: module under drift check
  TF_VAR_FILE:    "envs/prod.tfvars"   # <-- CHANGE THIS: or leave empty if not using var files
  AWS_REGION:     "us-east-1"          # <-- CHANGE THIS: cloud-specific, used for display only

permissions:
  contents: read
  issues:   write   # Note 3: Required to open a drift issue automatically
  id-token: write   # Note 4: Required for OIDC cloud authentication

# Note 5: Concurrency prevents two drift checks running simultaneously
# (e.g., manual trigger during scheduled run). The cancel-in-progress=false
# ensures the scheduled run finishes rather than being killed by a manual one.
concurrency:
  group: terraform-drift-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  # =============================================
  # DRIFT CHECK — plan with -detailed-exitcode
  # =============================================
  detect-drift:
    name: Detect Terraform Drift
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Note 6: output the drift status so the notify job can check it
    outputs:
      drift-detected: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.drift }}
      plan-output:    ${{ steps.plan.outputs.plan_text }}

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      # ── Cloud Authentication (uncomment ONE) ──────────────────────────
      # - name: Azure Login (OIDC)
      #   uses: azure/login@v2
      #   with:
      #     client-id:       ${{ secrets.AZURE_CLIENT_ID }}    # <-- CHANGE THIS
      #     tenant-id:       ${{ secrets.AZURE_TENANT_ID }}
      #     subscription-id: ${{ secrets.AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID }}

      # - name: AWS Login (OIDC)
      #   uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v4
      #   with:
      #     role-to-assume: ${{ secrets.AWS_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN }} # <-- CHANGE THIS
      #     aws-region: ${{ env.AWS_REGION }}

      # - name: GCP Auth (Workload Identity)
      #   uses: google-github-actions/auth@v2
      #   with:
      #     workload_identity_provider: ${{ secrets.GCP_WORKLOAD_IDENTITY_PROVIDER }} # <-- CHANGE THIS
      #     service_account: ${{ secrets.GCP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT }}

      - name: Setup Terraform
        uses: hashicorp/setup-terraform@v3
        with:
          terraform_version: ${{ env.TF_VERSION }}
          # Note 7: wrapper=false gives us the raw exit code from terraform plan.
          # With wrapper=true, Terraform exit code 2 (drift) would be swallowed.
          terraform_wrapper: false

      - name: Terraform Init
        working-directory: ${{ env.TF_WORKING_DIR }}
        run: terraform init -input=false

      - name: Terraform Plan (drift check)
        id: plan
        working-directory: ${{ env.TF_WORKING_DIR }}
        # Note 8: Exit codes from `terraform plan -detailed-exitcode`:
        #   0 = no changes (no drift)
        #   1 = error
        #   2 = changes present (DRIFT DETECTED)
        # We capture the exit code manually and set step outputs.
        run: |
          PLAN_ARGS="-detailed-exitcode -input=false -no-color"
          if [ -n "${{ env.TF_VAR_FILE }}" ]; then
            PLAN_ARGS="${PLAN_ARGS} -var-file=${{ env.TF_VAR_FILE }}"
          fi

          set +e
          terraform plan ${PLAN_ARGS} 2>&1 | tee /tmp/plan.txt
          EXIT_CODE=${PIPESTATUS[0]}
          set -e

          # Store plan output in step output (truncated to 65535 chars — GH limit)
          PLAN_TEXT=$(cat /tmp/plan.txt | tail -c 60000)
          echo "plan_text<<EOF" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "${PLAN_TEXT}"   >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "EOF"            >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

          if [ "$EXIT_CODE" -eq 2 ]; then
            echo "drift=true"  >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::warning::Drift detected in ${{ env.TF_WORKING_DIR }}"
            exit 0   # Note 9: Don't fail the step — let the notify job open the issue
          elif [ "$EXIT_CODE" -eq 1 ]; then
            echo "drift=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::error::terraform plan failed"
            exit 1
          else
            echo "drift=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "No drift detected."
          fi

  # =============================================
  # NOTIFY — open (or update) a GitHub Issue when drift is found
  # =============================================
  open-drift-issue:
    name: Open Drift Issue
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: detect-drift
    if: needs.detect-drift.outputs.drift-detected == 'true'

    steps:
      - uses: actions/github-script@v7
        with:
          github-token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          script: |
            const title = `[Drift] Terraform drift detected in ${{ env.TF_WORKING_DIR }}`;
            const body = [
              "## :warning: Terraform Drift Detected",
              "",
              `**Module:** \`${{ env.TF_WORKING_DIR }}\``,
              `**Detected at:** ${new Date().toISOString()}`,
              `**Triggered by:** \`${{ github.event_name }}\``,
              `**Run:** ${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}`,
              "",
              "### What this means",
              "The live infrastructure no longer matches the Terraform state.",
              "This typically happens when:",
              "- Someone applied changes directly via the cloud console or CLI",
              "- A cloud provider changed default values or resource behaviour",
              "- A resource was manually deleted or recreated",
              "",
              "### How to resolve",
              "1. Review the plan output below",
              "2. Determine if the live change should be **imported** (`terraform import`) or **reverted** (re-run plan-apply)",
              "3. Apply the fix and close this issue",
              "",
              "### Plan output",
              "```",
              `${{ needs.detect-drift.outputs.plan-output }}`,
              "```",
            ].join("\n");

            // Note 10: Check for an existing open drift issue so we don't spam.
            // If one already exists, add a comment instead of opening a duplicate.
            const { data: issues } = await github.rest.issues.listForRepo({
              owner: context.repo.owner,
              repo:  context.repo.repo,
              state: "open",
              labels: "terraform-drift",
            });

            const existing = issues.find(i => i.title === title);

            if (existing) {
              await github.rest.issues.createComment({
                owner:    context.repo.owner,
                repo:     context.repo.repo,
                issue_number: existing.number,
                body: `Drift still present as of ${new Date().toISOString()}.\n\nRun: ${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}`,
              });
              console.log(`Updated existing drift issue #${existing.number}`);
            } else {
              const { data: issue } = await github.rest.issues.create({
                owner:  context.repo.owner,
                repo:   context.repo.repo,
                title,
                body,
                labels: ["terraform-drift", "infrastructure"],   // <-- CHANGE THIS: labels must exist in your repo
              });
              console.log(`Opened drift issue #${issue.number}: ${issue.html_url}`);
            }

  # =============================================
  # CLOSE ISSUE — auto-close drift issue when drift is resolved
  # =============================================
  close-drift-issue:
    name: Close Resolved Drift Issue
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: detect-drift
    if: needs.detect-drift.outputs.drift-detected == 'false'

    steps:
      - uses: actions/github-script@v7
        with:
          github-token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          script: |
            const title = `[Drift] Terraform drift detected in ${{ env.TF_WORKING_DIR }}`;

            const { data: issues } = await github.rest.issues.listForRepo({
              owner: context.repo.owner,
              repo:  context.repo.repo,
              state: "open",
              labels: "terraform-drift",
            });

            const existing = issues.find(i => i.title === title);

            if (existing) {
              await github.rest.issues.createComment({
                owner:    context.repo.owner,
                repo:     context.repo.repo,
                issue_number: existing.number,
                body: `Drift resolved as of ${new Date().toISOString()}. Closing automatically.\n\nRun: ${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}`,
              });
              await github.rest.issues.update({
                owner:  context.repo.owner,
                repo:   context.repo.repo,
                issue_number: existing.number,
                state:  "closed",
              });
              console.log(`Closed drift issue #${existing.number}`);
            } else {
              console.log("No open drift issue to close.");
            }

# ============================================================
# TEMPLATE: GitHub Actions — Terraform Module Tests
# WHEN TO USE: Run native `terraform test` on every PR that touches
#   Terraform code. Fast plan-only tests run on PR; integration
#   tests (apply) are gated on manual trigger.
# PREREQUISITES:
#   - Terraform >= 1.6 (native test framework)
#   - test files in terraform/aws-eks/tests/*.tftest.hcl
#   - For integration tests: cloud credentials as Actions secrets
# WHAT TO CHANGE: Lines marked  # <-- CHANGE THIS
# RELATED FILES:
#   terraform/aws-eks/tests/unit.tftest.hcl
#   terraform/_testing/terratest/aws_eks_test.go
#   ci/github-actions/terraform/plan-apply.yml
# MATURITY: Stable
# ============================================================

name: Terraform Module Tests

on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - "terraform/**"
      - ".github/workflows/terraform-module-test.yml"
  # Note 1: workflow_dispatch lets you trigger integration tests on demand
  # without waiting for a PR. Pass integration_test=true to run apply tests.
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      integration_test:
        description: "Run integration tests (creates real cloud resources)"
        required: false
        default: "false"
        type: choice
        options:
          - "false"
          - "true"

env:
  TF_VERSION: "1.10.0"         # <-- CHANGE THIS: keep in sync with plan-apply.yml
  GO_VERSION:  "1.22"          # <-- CHANGE THIS: Go version for Terratest

jobs:
  # =============================================
  # UNIT TESTS — native terraform test, no cloud creds needed
  # =============================================
  terraform-unit-test:
    name: Terraform Unit Tests (${{ matrix.module }})
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        # Note 2: Add one entry per module that has a tests/ directory.
        # Each entry maps to a subdirectory under terraform/
        module:
          - aws-eks        # <-- CHANGE THIS: list your modules
          # - azure-aks
          # - gcp-gke

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Setup Terraform
        uses: hashicorp/setup-terraform@v3
        with:
          terraform_version: ${{ env.TF_VERSION }}

      - name: Terraform Init — ${{ matrix.module }}
        working-directory: terraform/${{ matrix.module }}
        run: terraform init -input=false

      - name: Terraform Test (unit) — ${{ matrix.module }}
        working-directory: terraform/${{ matrix.module }}
        # Note 3: `terraform test` discovers all *.tftest.hcl files in the
        # tests/ directory automatically. The -filter flag can target one file.
        run: terraform test
        env:
          # Note 4: mock_provider handles auth for unit tests, but some modules
          # still need these env vars to initialise remote state backends.
          TF_CLI_ARGS_init: "-backend=false"

  # =============================================
  # INTEGRATION TESTS — Terratest + Go, creates real resources
  # Only on workflow_dispatch with integration_test=true
  # =============================================
  terratest-integration:
    name: Terratest Integration Tests
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && github.event.inputs.integration_test == 'true'
    environment: test-account   # <-- CHANGE THIS: GitHub environment for cloud test credentials
    permissions:
      id-token: write   # OIDC
      contents: read

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      # Note 5: Uncomment ONE cloud auth block — same pattern as plan-apply.yml.
      # - name: AWS Login (OIDC)
      #   uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v4
      #   with:
      #     role-to-assume: ${{ secrets.AWS_TEST_ROLE_ARN }}   # <-- CHANGE THIS
      #     aws-region: us-east-1                              # <-- CHANGE THIS

      # - name: Azure Login (OIDC)
      #   uses: azure/login@v2
      #   with:
      #     client-id:       ${{ secrets.AZURE_CLIENT_ID }}
      #     tenant-id:       ${{ secrets.AZURE_TENANT_ID }}
      #     subscription-id: ${{ secrets.AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID }}

      - name: Setup Go
        uses: actions/setup-go@v5
        with:
          go-version: ${{ env.GO_VERSION }}
          cache-dependency-path: terraform/_testing/terratest/go.sum

      - name: Install Terraform
        uses: hashicorp/setup-terraform@v3
        with:
          terraform_version: ${{ env.TF_VERSION }}
          terraform_wrapper: false  # Note 6: Must be false for Terratest to capture output

      - name: Run Terratest
        working-directory: terraform/_testing/terratest
        # Note 7: -timeout 60m keeps the job alive during the ~25 min cluster creation.
        # -run selects only the integration tests (not the fast plan-only ones).
        run: go test -v -timeout 60m -run TestEKSCluster ./...
        env:
          AWS_DEFAULT_REGION: us-east-1   # <-- CHANGE THIS

      - name: Upload test results
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: terratest-results
          path: terraform/_testing/terratest/test-results.xml
          retention-days: 30
          if-no-files-found: ignore

            *Pushed by: @${{ github.actor }}, Action: \`${{ github.event_name }}\`*`;

            github.rest.issues.createComment({
              issue_number: context.issue.number,
              owner: context.repo.owner,
              repo: context.repo.repo,
              body: output
            })

      - name: Fail if Plan Failed
        if: steps.plan.outcome == 'failure'
        run: exit 1

  # =============================================
  # APPLY — runs only on push to main (after PR merge)
  # =============================================
  apply:
    name: Terraform Apply
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    if: github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    environment: production   # <-- CHANGE THIS: requires environment approval in GitHub settings

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      # --- Cloud Authentication (uncomment ONE — same as plan job) ---
      # - name: Azure Login (OIDC)
      #   uses: azure/login@v2
      #   with:
      #     client-id: ${{ secrets.AZURE_CLIENT_ID }}
      #     tenant-id: ${{ secrets.AZURE_TENANT_ID }}
      #     subscription-id: ${{ secrets.AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID }}

      # - name: AWS Login (OIDC)
      #   uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v4
      #   with:
      #     role-to-assume: ${{ secrets.AWS_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN }}
      #     aws-region: ${{ env.AWS_REGION }}

      # - name: GCP Auth (Workload Identity)
      #   uses: google-github-actions/auth@v2
      #   with:
      #     workload_identity_provider: ${{ secrets.GCP_WORKLOAD_IDENTITY_PROVIDER }}
      #     service_account: ${{ secrets.GCP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT }}

      - name: Setup Terraform
        uses: hashicorp/setup-terraform@v3
        with:
          terraform_version: ${{ env.TF_VERSION }}

      - name: Terraform Init
        working-directory: ${{ env.TF_WORKING_DIR }}
        run: terraform init -input=false

      - name: Terraform Apply
        working-directory: ${{ env.TF_WORKING_DIR }}
        run: |
          APPLY_ARGS="-input=false -auto-approve"
          if [ -n "${{ env.TF_VAR_FILE }}" ]; then
            APPLY_ARGS="${APPLY_ARGS} -var-file=${{ env.TF_VAR_FILE }}"
          fi
          terraform apply ${APPLY_ARGS}

  # =============================================
  # INFRACOST — posts cloud cost diff on every PR
  # Requires: INFRACOST_API_KEY secret (free at infracost.io)
  # =============================================
  infracost:
    name: Cost Estimation (Infracost)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
    needs: plan
    permissions:
      contents:      read
      pull-requests: write   # Note 1: Required to post the cost comment on the PR

    steps:
      - name: Checkout PR branch
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Setup Infracost
        uses: infracost/actions/setup@v3
        with:
          # Note 2: Get a free API key at https://www.infracost.io/docs/#2-get-api-key
          api-key: ${{ secrets.INFRACOST_API_KEY }}   # <-- CHANGE THIS: add to repo secrets

      - name: Ensure jq is available
        run: jq --version

      # Note 3: We generate cost breakdowns for both the base branch and the PR
      # branch, then diff them so the comment shows only what CHANGED in this PR.
      - name: Generate cost breakdown — base branch
        run: |
          git fetch origin ${{ github.base_ref }}
          git checkout ${{ github.base_ref }}
          INFRACOST_ARGS="--path ${{ env.TF_WORKING_DIR }} --format json --out-file /tmp/infracost-base.json"
          if [ -n "${{ env.TF_VAR_FILE }}" ]; then
            INFRACOST_ARGS="${INFRACOST_ARGS} --terraform-var-file ${{ env.TF_WORKING_DIR }}/${{ env.TF_VAR_FILE }}"
          fi
          infracost breakdown ${INFRACOST_ARGS}

      - name: Generate cost breakdown — PR branch
        run: |
          git checkout ${{ github.head_ref }}
          INFRACOST_ARGS="--path ${{ env.TF_WORKING_DIR }} --format json --out-file /tmp/infracost-pr.json"
          if [ -n "${{ env.TF_VAR_FILE }}" ]; then
            INFRACOST_ARGS="${INFRACOST_ARGS} --terraform-var-file ${{ env.TF_WORKING_DIR }}/${{ env.TF_VAR_FILE }}"
          fi
          infracost breakdown ${INFRACOST_ARGS}

      - name: Generate cost diff JSON
        run: |
          infracost diff \
            --path /tmp/infracost-pr.json \
            --compare-to /tmp/infracost-base.json \
            --format json \
            --out-file /tmp/infracost-diff.json

      - name: Post cost diff as PR comment
        # Note 4: --behavior=update replaces a previous Infracost comment rather than
        # posting a new one on each commit push, keeping PR threads clean.
        run: |
          infracost diff \
            --path /tmp/infracost-pr.json \
            --compare-to /tmp/infracost-base.json \
            --format github-comment \
            --github-token ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }} \
            --pull-request ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }} \
            --repo ${{ github.repository }} \
            --behavior update

      - name: Fail if monthly cost increase exceeds threshold
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          monthly_diff=$(jq -r '(.totalMonthlyCostDiff // .diffTotalMonthlyCost // 0) | tonumber' /tmp/infracost-diff.json)
          printf 'Infracost monthly diff: $%s\n' "$monthly_diff"

          if jq -e --argjson threshold "${INFRACOST_DIFF_THRESHOLD}" '((.totalMonthlyCostDiff // .diffTotalMonthlyCost // 0) | tonumber) > $threshold' /tmp/infracost-diff.json > /dev/null; then
            printf 'Monthly cost increase exceeds threshold of $%s.\n' "${INFRACOST_DIFF_THRESHOLD}"
            exit 1
          fi

# ============================================================
# TEMPLATE: GitHub Actions — TruffleHog Verified Secret Detection
# WHEN TO USE: Deep pull request secret scanning with live credential verification
# PREREQUISITES: Pull requests opened from branches with accessible base and head commits
# SECRETS NEEDED: None
# WHAT TO CHANGE: Pull request branch filters, TruffleHog CLI version, and summary detail level
# RELATED FILES: security/secret-detection/gitleaks.yml, security/README.md
# MATURITY: Stable
# ============================================================

# Note 1: Resource identity and metadata drive automation, selectors, and operational traceability.
name: TruffleHog Verified Secret Detection

on:
  # Note 2: PR-only is intentional here because deep history and verification are more expensive than fast push-time pattern scans.
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]  # <-- CHANGE THIS: match your protected review branch

# Note 3: Comment updates need issue or PR write access; checkout only needs contents read.
permissions:
  contents: read
  issues: write
  pull-requests: write

jobs:
  # Note 4: Keep TruffleHog separate from Gitleaks so teams can tune expensive verified scanning independently.
  trufflehog:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        # Note 5: Base and head SHAs may sit outside a shallow clone, so full history avoids false negatives on PR diffs.
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Run TruffleHog enforcement scan
        # Note 6: Pinning a security action to a full SHA prevents an upstream branch move from silently changing scanner behaviour.
        uses: trufflesecurity/trufflehog@5474feb15b332595dd00d83b71f4689ab1860a1d
        with:
          path: ./
          # Note 7: The action maps base/head to --since-commit and --branch so only the PR diff is scanned instead of full history.
          base: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          head: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          version: v3.95.2  # <-- CHANGE THIS: pin the TruffleHog CLI version instead of relying on latest
          # IMPORTANT: --only-verified reduces false positives, but it can miss secrets that cannot be live-verified such as internal APIs.
          extra_args: --only-verified  # Pair with Gitleaks for broader pattern coverage across unverifiable secret types.

      - name: Build job summary
        # Note 8: Re-running the same bounded diff in JSON mode gives reviewers a concise summary without re-scanning full repository history.
        if: always()
        id: summary
        shell: bash
        env:
          BASE_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
        run: |
          results_file="$(mktemp)"
          summary_file="$(mktemp)"

          docker run --rm -v "$PWD:/tmp" -w /tmp \
            ghcr.io/trufflesecurity/trufflehog:v3.95.2 \
            git file:///tmp/ \
            --since-commit "$BASE_SHA" \
            --branch "$HEAD_SHA" \
            --only-verified \
            --json \
            --no-update > "$results_file" || true

          finding_count="$(jq -s 'length' "$results_file")"

          {
            echo "## TruffleHog PR Secret Scan"
            echo
            echo "- Base commit: \`$BASE_SHA\`"
            echo "- Head commit: \`$HEAD_SHA\`"
            echo "- Verified findings: **$finding_count**"
            echo

            if [ "$finding_count" -gt 0 ]; then
              echo "| Detector | Location |"
              echo "|---|---|"
              jq -r '[.DetectorName // "unknown", .SourceMetadata.Data.Git.file // .SourceMetadata.Data.Filesystem.file // .SourceMetadata.Data.Git.path // "unknown"] | @tsv' "$results_file" \
                | sort -u \
                | head -n 20 \
                | while IFS=$'\t' read -r detector location; do
                    printf '| %s | %s |\n' "$detector" "$location"
                  done
              echo
              echo "Verified secrets were detected in the PR diff. Review the workflow logs for the full scanner output and rotate any exposed credentials immediately."
            else
              echo "No verified secrets were found in the pull request diff."
            fi
          } | tee "$summary_file" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

          {
            echo "comment_body<<EOF"
            cat "$summary_file"
            echo "EOF"
          } >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Comment on pull request
        # Note 9: Reusing the same markdown in the PR comment and job summary keeps reviewer context consistent.
        if: always() && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository
        uses: actions/github-script@v7
        env:
          COMMENT_BODY: ${{ steps.summary.outputs.comment_body }}
        with:
          github-token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          script: |
            const marker = '<!-- trufflehog-pr-scan -->';
            const body = `${marker}\n${process.env.COMMENT_BODY}`;
            const { owner, repo } = context.repo;
            const issue_number = context.issue.number;
            const comments = await github.paginate(github.rest.issues.listComments, {
              owner,
              repo,
              issue_number,
            });
            const existing = comments.find((comment) => comment.user.type === 'Bot' && comment.body.includes(marker));

            if (existing) {
              await github.rest.issues.updateComment({
                owner,
                repo,
                comment_id: existing.id,
                body,
              });
            } else {
              await github.rest.issues.createComment({
                owner,
                repo,
                issue_number,
                body,
              });
            }

"""
AWS Secrets Manager — Single-User Database Rotation Lambda
===========================================================
WHEN TO USE : Rotate a database password stored in AWS Secrets Manager.
              Works for PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB.  Adapt the DB_ENGINE
              constant and the SQL statements for other engines.

HOW IT WORKS: Secrets Manager calls this Lambda at four lifecycle steps
              (createSecret → setSecret → testSecret → finishSecret).
              Each step is idempotent so a retry is safe.

PREREQUISITES:
  - The secret JSON must contain:
      { "username": "...", "password": "...",
        "host": "...", "port": 5432, "dbname": "..." }
  - Lambda must have network access to the database (VPC + SG rules).
  - Lambda execution role needs:
      secretsmanager:GetSecretValue
      secretsmanager:PutSecretValue
      secretsmanager:DescribeSecret
      secretsmanager:UpdateSecretVersionStage

WHAT TO CHANGE: Variables marked  # <-- CHANGE THIS
"""

import boto3
import json
import logging
import os
import secrets
import string
import psycopg2  # pip install psycopg2-binary  # <-- CHANGE THIS: use pymysql for MySQL

logger = logging.getLogger()
logger.setLevel(logging.INFO)

# --- Configuration -------------------------------------------------------
DB_ENGINE = "postgresql"  # <-- CHANGE THIS: "mysql" | "postgresql" | "mariadb"
PASSWORD_LEN = 32  # <-- CHANGE THIS: minimum 20 recommended
# Exclude characters that break DSN strings or shell quoting
EXCLUDED = "\"'@/\\"
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------


def lambda_handler(event, context):
    """Entry point called by Secrets Manager at each rotation step."""
    arn = event["SecretId"]
    token = event["ClientRequestToken"]
    step = event["Step"]

    client = boto3.client("secretsmanager", region_name=os.environ["AWS_REGION"])

    metadata = client.describe_secret(SecretId=arn)
    if not metadata.get("RotationEnabled"):
        raise ValueError(f"Rotation is not enabled for secret {arn}")

    versions = metadata.get("VersionIdsToStages", {})
    if token not in versions:
        raise ValueError(f"Token {token} is not associated with secret {arn}")

    if "AWSCURRENT" in versions[token]:
        logger.info("Token is already AWSCURRENT — nothing to do")
        return
    if "AWSPENDING" not in versions[token]:
        raise ValueError(f"Token {token} is not in AWSPENDING stage")

    dispatch = {
        "createSecret": _create_secret,
        "setSecret": _set_secret,
        "testSecret": _test_secret,
        "finishSecret": _finish_secret,
    }
    if step not in dispatch:
        raise ValueError(f"Unknown step: {step}")

    dispatch[step](client, arn, token)


# ── Step 1: generate and store a new password in AWSPENDING ──────────────
def _create_secret(client, arn, token):
    try:
        client.get_secret_value(SecretId=arn, VersionStage="AWSPENDING", VersionId=token)
        logger.info("createSecret: AWSPENDING already exists — skipping")
        return
    except client.exceptions.ResourceNotFoundException:
        pass

    current = _get_secret(client, arn, "AWSCURRENT")
    current["password"] = _generate_password()

    client.put_secret_value(
        SecretId=arn,
        ClientRequestToken=token,
        SecretString=json.dumps(current),
        VersionStages=["AWSPENDING"],
    )
    logger.info("createSecret: stored new password in AWSPENDING")


# ── Step 2: apply the new password in the actual database ────────────────
def _set_secret(client, arn, token):
    pending = _get_secret(client, arn, "AWSPENDING", token)
    current = _get_secret(client, arn, "AWSCURRENT")

    conn = _db_connect(current)
    try:
        with conn.cursor() as cur:
            if DB_ENGINE == "postgresql":
                cur.execute(
                    "ALTER USER %s WITH PASSWORD %s",
                    (pending["username"], pending["password"]),
                )
            else:
                # MySQL / MariaDB
                cur.execute(
                    "ALTER USER %s@'%%' IDENTIFIED BY %s",
                    (pending["username"], pending["password"]),
                )
        conn.commit()
        logger.info("setSecret: password updated in database")
    finally:
        conn.close()


# ── Step 3: verify the new credentials actually work ─────────────────────
def _test_secret(client, arn, token):
    pending = _get_secret(client, arn, "AWSPENDING", token)
    conn = _db_connect(pending)
    try:
        with conn.cursor() as cur:
            cur.execute("SELECT 1")
        logger.info("testSecret: new credentials verified")
    finally:
        conn.close()


# ── Step 4: promote AWSPENDING to AWSCURRENT ─────────────────────────────
def _finish_secret(client, arn, token):
    metadata = client.describe_secret(SecretId=arn)
    current_version = next(
        (v for v, stages in metadata["VersionIdsToStages"].items() if "AWSCURRENT" in stages),
        None,
    )
    if current_version == token:
        logger.info("finishSecret: already AWSCURRENT — nothing to do")
        return

    client.update_secret_version_stage(
        SecretId=arn,
        VersionStage="AWSCURRENT",
        MoveToVersionId=token,
        RemoveFromVersionId=current_version,
    )
    logger.info("finishSecret: promoted AWSPENDING to AWSCURRENT")


# ── Helpers ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
def _get_secret(client, arn, stage, version_id=None):
    kwargs = {"SecretId": arn, "VersionStage": stage}
    if version_id:
        kwargs["VersionId"] = version_id
    value = client.get_secret_value(**kwargs)
    return json.loads(value["SecretString"])


def _generate_password(length: int = PASSWORD_LEN) -> str:
    alphabet = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + string.punctuation
    safe = "".join(c for c in alphabet if c not in EXCLUDED)
    # Guarantee at least one of each required character class
    pwd = [
        secrets.choice(string.ascii_uppercase),
        secrets.choice(string.ascii_lowercase),
        secrets.choice(string.digits),
        secrets.choice("!#$%^&*()-_=+[]{}|;:,.<>?"),
    ]
    pwd += [secrets.choice(safe) for _ in range(length - len(pwd))]
    secrets.SystemRandom().shuffle(pwd)
    return "".join(pwd)


def _db_connect(secret: dict):
    if DB_ENGINE == "postgresql":
        return psycopg2.connect(
            host=secret["host"],
            port=secret.get("port", 5432),
            dbname=secret["dbname"],
            user=secret["username"],
            password=secret["password"],
            connect_timeout=5,
            sslmode="require",  # always require TLS in production
        )
    # MySQL / MariaDB
    import pymysql  # noqa: PLC0415

    return pymysql.connect(
        host=secret["host"],
        port=secret.get("port", 3306),
        db=secret["dbname"],
        user=secret["username"],
        password=secret["password"],
        connect_timeout=5,
        ssl={"ssl": True},
    )

# WHEN TO USE: Automatically rotate a secret in Azure Key Vault
#              before it expires, triggered by an EventGrid event.
# PREREQUISITES:
#   - Azure Key Vault with an existing secret that has an expiry date set.
#   - Azure Function App (Consumption or Flex) with system-assigned identity.
#   - Function app identity must have "Key Vault Secrets Officer" on the vault.
# WHAT TO CHANGE: Lines marked  # <-- CHANGE THIS
# RELATED FILES: security/secret-rotation/external-secrets-operator.yaml
# MATURITY: Stable
# ============================================================

# ---------------------------------------------
# 1. EventGrid System Topic — Key Vault events
# ---------------------------------------------
resource "azurerm_eventgrid_system_topic" "keyvault" {
  name                   = "evgt-kv-rotation"       # <-- CHANGE THIS
  resource_group_name    = var.resource_group_name
  location               = var.location
  source_arm_resource_id = var.key_vault_id
  topic_type             = "Microsoft.KeyVault.vaults"
  tags                   = var.common_tags
}

# ---------------------------------------------
# 2. EventGrid Subscription → Azure Function
# ---------------------------------------------
resource "azurerm_eventgrid_system_topic_event_subscription" "near_expiry" {
  name                = "sub-kv-secret-near-expiry"
  system_topic        = azurerm_eventgrid_system_topic.keyvault.name
  resource_group_name = var.resource_group_name

  # Fire when a secret is about to expire (30-day warning)
  included_event_types = [
    "Microsoft.KeyVault.SecretNearExpiry",
    "Microsoft.KeyVault.SecretExpired",
  ]

  azure_function_endpoint {
    function_id = "${var.function_app_id}/functions/RotateSecret"
    # Ensure the function endpoint uses the same auth as the Event Grid topic
    max_events_per_batch              = 1
    preferred_batch_size_in_kilobytes = 64
  }

  retry_policy {
    max_delivery_attempts = 10
    event_time_to_live    = 1440 # 24 hours
  }
}

# Grant EventGrid permission to invoke the function
resource "azurerm_role_assignment" "eventgrid_to_function" {
  scope                = var.function_app_id
  role_definition_name = "Website Contributor"
  principal_id         = azurerm_eventgrid_system_topic.keyvault.identity[0].principal_id
}

# Grant Function identity access to Key Vault
resource "azurerm_role_assignment" "function_kv_secrets_officer" {
  scope                = var.key_vault_id
  role_definition_name = "Key Vault Secrets Officer"
  principal_id         = var.function_identity_principal_id # <-- CHANGE THIS: system-assigned MI principal
}

# ============================================================
# TEMPLATE: Docker Compose — Annotated Base Template
# WHEN TO USE: Starting point for any new local dev environment
# PREREQUISITES: Docker and Docker Compose v2+
# SECRETS NEEDED: None (uses .env file)
# WHAT TO CHANGE: Adapt services, ports, and volumes to your stack
# RELATED FILES: compose/dotnet-sqlserver/, compose/python-postgres-redis/
# MATURITY: Stable
# ============================================================
#
# NOTE: The top-level 'version:' key is obsolete in Docker Compose v2+
# and has been intentionally omitted. See:
# https://docs.docker.com/compose/compose-file/04-version-and-name/

# Extension fields: define anchors to reuse across services
# Note 1: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
x-logging: &default-logging
  driver: "json-file"
  # Note 2: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
  options:
    max-size: "10m"
    # Note 3: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
    max-file: "3"

x-restart-policy: &restart-policy
  # Note 4: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
  restart: unless-stopped

services:
  # Note 5: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
  app:
    # Build from local Dockerfile
    build:
      # Note 6: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
      context: .          # Build context (directory sent to Docker daemon)
      dockerfile: Dockerfile
      # Note 7: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
      args:
        - BUILD_ENV=development  # ARGs available during build only
      # Note 8: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
      target: runtime     # Stop at a specific multi-stage target

    # Or pull a pre-built image:
    # image: myregistry.io/my-app:1.2.3

    container_name: my-app  # Avoid auto-generated names in dev

    # Note 9: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
    ports:
      - "3000:3000"     # host:container — only expose what you need

    # Note 10: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
    environment:
      - NODE_ENV=development
      # Note 11: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
      - DB_HOST=db      # Container names resolve as DNS on the same network

    # Load from .env file (never commit secrets)
    env_file:
      # Note 12: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
      - .env

    volumes:
      # Named volume: managed by Docker, persists between restarts
      # Note 13: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
      - app-data:/app/data
      # Bind mount: reflects local file changes instantly (great for dev)
      - ./src:/app/src:ro   # :ro = read-only inside container

    # Note 14: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
    depends_on:
      db:
        # Note 15: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
        condition: service_healthy  # Wait for healthcheck to pass

    healthcheck:
      # Note 16: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
      test: ["CMD", "wget", "-qO-", "http://localhost:3000/health"]
      interval: 30s
      # Note 17: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 3
      # Note 18: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
      start_period: 20s  # Grace period before first check

    networks:
      # Note 19: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
      - app-net

    logging: *default-logging
    # Note 20: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
    <<: *restart-policy

  db:
    # Note 21: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
    image: postgres:16-alpine
    environment:
      # Note 22: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
      - POSTGRES_USER=${DB_USER:-appuser}
      - POSTGRES_PASSWORD=${DB_PASSWORD:?DB_PASSWORD must be set}  # Fails if not set
      # Note 23: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
      - POSTGRES_DB=${DB_NAME:-appdb}
    volumes:
      # Note 24: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
      - db-data:/var/lib/postgresql/data
      - ./db/init.sql:/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d/init.sql:ro  # Run on first start
    # Note 25: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U ${DB_USER:-appuser}"]
      # Note 26: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5
    networks:
      - app-net
    logging: *default-logging
    <<: *restart-policy

volumes:
  app-data:     # Persists across container restarts
  db-data:

networks:
  app-net:
    driver: bridge
    # For external network (e.g., shared across compose files):
    # external: true

# ============================================================
# TEMPLATE: Docker Compose — .NET API + SQL Server + Seq
# WHEN TO USE: Local development for .NET applications with SQL Server
# PREREQUISITES: Docker and Docker Compose v2+
# SECRETS NEEDED: SQL_PASSWORD (in .env file)
# WHAT TO CHANGE: Lines marked with # <-- CHANGE THIS
# RELATED FILES: docker/dotnet/Dockerfile.api
# MATURITY: Stable
# ============================================================

# .NET API + SQL Server + Seq (structured logging UI) — Local Dev Stack

# Note 1: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
services:
  api:
    # Note 2: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
    build:
      context: ../../
      # Note 3: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
      dockerfile: docker/dotnet/Dockerfile.api               # <-- CHANGE THIS: path to your Dockerfile
    ports:
      # Note 4: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
      - "5000:8080"                                          # <-- CHANGE THIS: host:container port
    environment:
      # Note 5: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
      - ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT=Development
      - ConnectionStrings__DefaultConnection=Server=sqlserver;Database=AppDb;User Id=sa;Password=${SQL_PASSWORD};TrustServerCertificate=True
      # Note 6: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
      - Serilog__WriteTo__Seq__ServerUrl=http://seq:5341
    depends_on:
      # Note 7: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
      sqlserver:
        condition: service_healthy
    # Note 8: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
    networks:
      - app-net

  # Note 9: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
  sqlserver:
    image: mcr.microsoft.com/mssql/server:2022-latest
    # Note 10: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
    environment:
      - ACCEPT_EULA=Y
      # Note 11: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
      - SA_PASSWORD=${SQL_PASSWORD:-Dev@Password123!}
    ports:
      # Note 12: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
      - "1433:1433"
    volumes:
      # Note 13: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
      - sqlserver-data:/var/opt/mssql
    healthcheck:
      # Note 14: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
      test: /opt/mssql-tools18/bin/sqlcmd -S localhost -U sa -P "$$SA_PASSWORD" -C -Q "SELECT 1" || exit 1
      interval: 15s
      # Note 15: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5
      # Note 16: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
      start_period: 30s
    networks:
      # Note 17: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
      - app-net

  # Seq — structured logging UI (view .NET Serilog logs)
  seq:
    image: datalust/seq:latest
    environment:
      - ACCEPT_EULA=Y
    ports:
      - "5341:5341"   # Ingestion API
      - "8081:80"     # Web UI — open http://localhost:8081
    volumes:
      - seq-data:/data
    networks:
      - app-net

volumes:
  sqlserver-data:
  seq-data:

networks:
  app-net:
    driver: bridge

# MATURITY: Stable

# Spring Boot API + PostgreSQL — Local Dev Stack

services:
  api:
    build:
      context: ../../
      dockerfile: docker/java/Dockerfile.gradle
      target: build
    command: gradle bootRun --no-daemon
    ports:
      - "8080:8080"
    environment:
      - SPRING_DATASOURCE_URL=jdbc:postgresql://postgres:5432/${POSTGRES_DB}
      - SPRING_DATASOURCE_USERNAME=${SPRING_DATASOURCE_USERNAME}
      - SPRING_DATASOURCE_PASSWORD=${SPRING_DATASOURCE_PASSWORD}
      - SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE=local
      - JAVA_OPTS=-Xmx512m
    depends_on:
      postgres:
        condition: service_healthy
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- http://localhost:8080/actuator/health || exit 1"]
      interval: 15s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5
      start_period: 45s
    volumes:
      - ../../src/main:/app/src/main   # <-- CHANGE THIS if your Spring Boot sources live elsewhere
    networks:
      - app-net

  postgres:
    image: postgres:16-alpine
    environment:
      - POSTGRES_DB=${POSTGRES_DB}
      - POSTGRES_USER=${POSTGRES_USER}
      - POSTGRES_PASSWORD=${POSTGRES_PASSWORD}
    ports:
      - "5432:5432"
    volumes:
      - postgres-data:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U $$POSTGRES_USER -d $$POSTGRES_DB"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5
      start_period: 10s
    networks:
      - app-net

volumes:
  postgres-data:

networks:
  app-net:
    driver: bridge

# Microservices Example — Local Dev Stack
# Demonstrates: shared network, service discovery, API gateway pattern

# Note 1: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
services:
  # API Gateway / reverse proxy
  gateway:
    image: nginx:1.27-alpine
    # Note 2: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
    ports:
      - "8080:80"
    volumes:
      # Note 3: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
      - ./gateway/nginx.conf:/etc/nginx/conf.d/default.conf:ro
    depends_on:
      - user-service
      # Note 4: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
      - order-service
    networks:
      - app-net

  # Note 5: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
  user-service:
    build:
      context: ./user-service
    # Note 6: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
    environment:
      - DATABASE_URL=postgresql://postgres:devpassword@postgres:5432/usersdb
    depends_on:
      # Note 7: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
      postgres:
        condition: service_healthy
    networks:
      # Note 8: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
      - app-net

  order-service:
    build:
      # Note 9: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
      context: ./order-service
    environment:
      - DATABASE_URL=postgresql://postgres:devpassword@postgres:5432/ordersdb
      # Note 10: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
      - MESSAGE_BROKER=amqp://guest:guest@rabbitmq:5672/
    depends_on:
      postgres:
        # Note 11: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
        condition: service_healthy
      rabbitmq:
        condition: service_healthy
    # Note 12: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
    networks:
      - app-net

  postgres:
    # Note 13: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
    image: postgres:16-alpine
    environment:
      - POSTGRES_USER=postgres
      # Note 14: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
      - POSTGRES_PASSWORD=devpassword
      - POSTGRES_MULTIPLE_DATABASES=usersdb,ordersdb
    volumes:
      # Note 15: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
      - postgres-data:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U postgres"]
      # Note 16: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5
    # Note 17: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
    networks:
      - app-net

  rabbitmq:
    # Note 18: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
    image: rabbitmq:3.13-management-alpine
    ports:
      - "15672:15672"  # management UI
    # Note 19: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
    healthcheck:
      test: rabbitmq-diagnostics -q ping
      interval: 15s
      # Note 20: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 5
    networks:
      # Note 21: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
      - app-net

volumes:
  postgres-data:

# Note 22: This line contributes to the system's declarative intent, helping future readers reason about behavior and change impact.
networks:
  app-net:
    driver: bridge

# ============================================================
# TEMPLATE: Annotated Multi-stage Dockerfile — Teaching Example
# WHEN TO USE: Learning reference for multi-stage Docker builds
# PREREQUISITES: Node.js project with package.json and build script
# SECRETS NEEDED: None
# WHAT TO CHANGE: Adapt patterns to your stack
# RELATED FILES: docker/_base/security-hardened.Dockerfile
# MATURITY: Stable
# ============================================================
# A multi-stage build separates build-time tools from the final runtime image.
# Only the last stage is used when you run `docker build` with no --target flag.

# ── Stage 1: Dependencies ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Use a full SDK image for building — this stage will NOT be shipped
# Note 1: Imports make dependencies explicit, which keeps module boundaries clear and simplifies maintenance.
FROM node:22-alpine AS deps
# Note 2: Docker instructions are layer-based; ordering these commands intentionally can improve cache reuse and build speed.
