# OpenCost Helm chart values for cost monitoring and allocation
# This configuration integrates with Prometheus for metrics collection
# and supports multi-cloud pricing APIs (AWS, Azure, GCP)

# Namespace configuration
# OpenCost will be deployed to the 'finops' namespace
# The installation script creates this namespace if it doesn't exist
opencost:
  # Prometheus integration
  # OpenCost requires Prometheus for scraping metrics and data storage
  prometheus:
    # Internal Prometheus endpoint - adjust if using external Prometheus
    internal:
      enabled: true
      serviceName: prometheus-operated
      namespaceName: monitoring
      port: 9090

    # External Prometheus endpoint (if not using internal)
    external:
      enabled: false
      url: http://prometheus-server.monitoring.svc:9090  # <-- CHANGE THIS if using external Prometheus

  # Exporter configuration
  exporter:
    # Default cluster ID for cost allocation
    # Used to identify costs in multi-cluster environments
    defaultClusterId: default-cluster  # <-- CHANGE THIS to your cluster identifier

    # Cloud provider configuration
    # OpenCost will attempt to detect the cloud provider automatically
    # Override these settings for explicit configuration
    cloudProviderApiKey: ""  # Optional: API key for cloud provider pricing data

    # AWS configuration
    # Requires IAM role with access to Cost and Usage Reports
    aws:
      # Set to true to enable AWS pricing integration
      enabled: false  # <-- CHANGE THIS to true for AWS clusters
      # AWS region for Spot data feed
      spotDataRegion: us-east-1  # <-- CHANGE THIS to your region
      # S3 bucket containing Spot data feed
      spotDataBucket: ""  # <-- CHANGE THIS to your S3 bucket name
      # AWS account ID
      accountId: ""  # <-- CHANGE THIS to your AWS account ID
      # Service account annotations for IAM role (IRSA)
      serviceAccountAnnotations:
        eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn: ""  # <-- CHANGE THIS to your IAM role ARN

    # Azure configuration
    # Requires service principal with Cost Management Reader role
    azure:
      # Set to true to enable Azure pricing integration
      enabled: false  # <-- CHANGE THIS to true for AKS clusters
      # Azure subscription ID
      subscriptionId: ""  # <-- CHANGE THIS to your subscription ID
      # Azure tenant ID
      tenantId: ""  # <-- CHANGE THIS to your tenant ID
      # Azure client ID (service principal)
      clientId: ""  # <-- CHANGE THIS to your client ID
      # Azure client secret (stored in Kubernetes Secret)
      clientSecretName: opencost-azure-secret  # <-- CHANGE THIS if using different secret name
      clientSecretKey: azure-client-secret

    # GCP configuration
    # Requires service account with BigQuery Data Viewer role
    gcp:
      # Set to true to enable GCP pricing integration
      enabled: false  # <-- CHANGE THIS to true for GKE clusters
      # GCP project ID
      projectId: ""  # <-- CHANGE THIS to your project ID
      # BigQuery dataset containing billing export
      billingDataDataset: ""  # <-- CHANGE THIS to your dataset name
      # BigQuery table containing billing export
      billingDataTable: ""  # <-- CHANGE THIS to your table name
      # Service account key (stored in Kubernetes Secret)
      serviceAccountSecretName: opencost-gcp-secret  # <-- CHANGE THIS if using different secret name
      serviceAccountSecretKey: gcp-service-account-key

    # Additional environment variables
    extraEnv:
      # Emit KSM v1 metrics for compatibility
      EMIT_KSM_V1_METRICS: "false"
      EMIT_KSM_V1_METRICS_ONLY: "true"
      # Prometheus cluster ID label
      PROM_CLUSTER_ID_LABEL: cluster
      # Log level (debug, info, warn, error)
      LOG_LEVEL: info  # <-- CHANGE THIS to debug for troubleshooting
      # Data retention period in days
      RETENTION_DAYS: "90"  # <-- CHANGE THIS to adjust retention (default: 90 days)

  # UI configuration
  ui:
    enabled: true
    # Resource limits for UI container
    resources:
      requests:
        cpu: 10m
        memory: 55Mi
      limits:
        cpu: 100m
        memory: 128Mi

  # Service configuration
  service:
    enabled: true
    type: ClusterIP
    port: 9003
    targetPort: 9003
    annotations:
      prometheus.io/scrape: "true"
      prometheus.io/port: "9003"
      prometheus.io/path: "/metrics"

  # ServiceMonitor for Prometheus Operator
  # Enables automatic discovery and scraping by Prometheus
  serviceMonitor:
    enabled: true
    namespace: finops
    labels:
      release: kube-prometheus-stack  # <-- CHANGE THIS to match your Prometheus Operator release
    interval: 30s
    scrapeTimeout: 10s

  # Resource limits for OpenCost exporter
  resources:
    requests:
      cpu: 100m
      memory: 256Mi
    limits:
      cpu: 500m
      memory: 1Gi

  # Node selector for pod placement
  nodeSelector: {}

  # Tolerations for pod scheduling
  tolerations: []

  # Affinity rules for pod scheduling
  affinity: {}

# Ingress configuration for OpenCost web UI
ingress:
  enabled: true
  className: nginx  # <-- CHANGE THIS if using different ingress controller
  annotations:
    cert-manager.io/cluster-issuer: letsencrypt-prod  # <-- CHANGE THIS to your cert-manager issuer
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/ssl-redirect: "true"
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/force-ssl-redirect: "true"
    # Authentication annotations (optional)
    # nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/auth-type: basic
    # nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/auth-secret: opencost-basic-auth
    # nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/auth-realm: "OpenCost Authentication Required"
  hosts:
    - host: opencost.example.com  # <-- CHANGE THIS to your domain
      paths:
        - path: /
          pathType: Prefix
  tls:
    - secretName: opencost-tls
      hosts:
        - opencost.example.com  # <-- CHANGE THIS to match host above

# Priority class for pod scheduling
priorityClassName: ""

# Security context for pods
podSecurityContext:
  runAsNonRoot: true
  runAsUser: 1000
  fsGroup: 1000
  seccompProfile:
    type: RuntimeDefault

# Security context for containers
securityContext:
  allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
  capabilities:
    drop:
      - ALL
  readOnlyRootFilesystem: true

# Pod annotations
podAnnotations:
  finops.org/costcenter: "platform"  # <-- CHANGE THIS to your cost center
  finops.org/environment: "production"  # <-- CHANGE THIS to your environment

# Pod labels
podLabels:
  app: opencost
  component: cost-monitoring

# Liveness probe configuration
livenessProbe:
  enabled: true
  httpGet:
    path: /healthz
    port: 9003
  initialDelaySeconds: 30
  periodSeconds: 10
  timeoutSeconds: 5
  failureThreshold: 3

# Readiness probe configuration
readinessProbe:
  enabled: true
  httpGet:
    path: /healthz
    port: 9003
  initialDelaySeconds: 10
  periodSeconds: 5
  timeoutSeconds: 3
  failureThreshold: 3

# Persistent volume for cost data storage (optional)
# Recommended for production to persist cost data across pod restarts
persistence:
  enabled: false  # <-- CHANGE THIS to true for production
  storageClass: ""  # <-- CHANGE THIS to your storage class
  accessMode: ReadWriteOnce
  size: 10Gi
  annotations: {}

# Network policy (optional)
# Restricts network access to OpenCost pods
networkPolicy:
  enabled: false  # <-- CHANGE THIS to true for enhanced security
  policyTypes:
    - Ingress
    - Egress
  ingress:
    - from:
        - namespaceSelector:
            matchLabels:
              name: monitoring
        - namespaceSelector:
            matchLabels:
              name: ingress-nginx
  egress:
    - to:
        - namespaceSelector:
            matchLabels:
              name: monitoring
      ports:
        - protocol: TCP
          port: 9090
    - to:
        - namespaceSelector: {}
      ports:
        - protocol: TCP
          port: 443  # For cloud provider API access

# RBAC configuration
rbac:
  create: true

# Service account configuration
serviceAccount:
  create: true
  name: opencost
  annotations: {}
    # For AWS IRSA (IAM Roles for Service Accounts)
    # eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn: arn:aws:iam::ACCOUNT_ID:role/opencost-role
    # For GCP Workload Identity
    # iam.gke.io/gcp-service-account: opencost@PROJECT_ID.iam.gserviceaccount.com
    # For Azure Workload Identity
    # azure.workload.identity/client-id: CLIENT_ID

# ============================================================
# CONFIGURATION NOTES
# ============================================================
#
# 1. PROMETHEUS INTEGRATION
#    - OpenCost requires Prometheus for metrics collection
#    - Default configuration assumes Prometheus Operator in 'monitoring' namespace
#    - Adjust prometheus.internal settings if using different setup
#
# 2. CLOUD PROVIDER SETUP
#    - Enable only the cloud provider(s) you're using
#    - Follow finops/docs/cloud-provider-setup.md for IAM/RBAC configuration
#    - Store sensitive credentials in Kubernetes Secrets
#
# 3. INGRESS AND TLS
#    - Update ingress.hosts and ingress.tls with your domain
#    - Ensure cert-manager is installed for automatic TLS certificate management
#    - Consider enabling authentication for production deployments
#
# 4. RESOURCE LIMITS
#    - Default limits are suitable for small-to-medium clusters
#    - Increase resources.limits for large clusters (>100 nodes)
#    - Monitor OpenCost pod metrics to adjust as needed
#
# 5. DATA RETENTION
#    - Default retention is 90 days (configurable via RETENTION_DAYS)
#    - Enable persistence for production to survive pod restarts
#    - Consider external storage (S3/Blob/GCS) for long-term archival
#
# 6. SECURITY
#    - Security contexts enforce non-root execution and read-only filesystem
#    - Enable networkPolicy for production to restrict pod communication
#    - Use Kubernetes Secrets for cloud provider credentials
#    - Consider enabling Ingress authentication for web UI access
#
# 7. MULTI-CLUSTER SETUP
#    - Set unique defaultClusterId for each cluster
#    - Use centralized Prometheus or Thanos for cross-cluster cost aggregation
#    - Configure cloud provider credentials per cluster
#
# ============================================================
# INSTALLATION COMMAND
# ============================================================
#
# helm repo add opencost https://opencost.github.io/opencost-helm-chart
# helm repo update
# kubectl create namespace finops
# helm install opencost opencost/opencost \
#   --namespace finops \
#   --values finops/helm/opencost-values.yaml
#
# Or use the provided installation script:
# ./finops/scripts/install-cost-monitoring.sh --tool opencost
#
# ============================================================

---
# finops/helm/vpa-values.yaml
# Helm values for the Vertical Pod Autoscaler (VPA) chart.
# Chart: https://github.com/FairwindsOps/charts/tree/master/stable/vpa
#
# Deploy with:
#   helm repo add fairwinds-stable https://charts.fairwinds.com/stable
#   helm upgrade --install vpa fairwinds-stable/vpa \
#     --namespace kube-system \
#     --values finops/helm/vpa-values.yaml

# ─── Recommender ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# The VPA recommender watches pod resource usage and generates recommendations.
# Run in recommendation-only mode: updater and admission controller are disabled
# so no automatic resource changes are made.
recommender:
  enabled: true
  replicaCount: 1

  resources:
    requests:
      cpu: 50m
      memory: 100Mi
    limits:
      cpu: 200m
      memory: 500Mi

  # Tune recommender behaviour
  extraArgs:
    # Minimum data duration before generating recommendations (24 hours)
    recommendation-margin-fraction: "0.15"
    # History length used for computing recommendations (7 days)
    recommender-interval: "1m"
    # Prometheus integration for historical metrics
    storage: "prometheus"
    prometheus-address: "http://prometheus-operated.monitoring.svc.cluster.local:9090"
    prometheus-cadvisor-job-name: "kubelet"
    # Decay factor for histograms — controls how quickly old data fades
    cpu-histogram-decay-half-life: "24h"
    memory-histogram-decay-half-life: "24h"

  podAnnotations:
    prometheus.io/scrape: "true"
    prometheus.io/port: "8942"

# ─── Updater ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# DISABLED: We use VPA in recommendation-only mode (Off/Initial).
# The updater would restart pods to apply resource changes — not desired here.
updater:
  enabled: false

# ─── Admission Controller ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# DISABLED: We do not want VPA to automatically mutate resource requests
# at pod admission time. Teams review recommendations manually.
admissionController:
  enabled: false

# ─── CRDs ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
crds:
  # Install the VerticalPodAutoscaler CRD if not already present
  create: true

# ─── RBAC ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
rbac:
  create: true

serviceAccount:
  create: true
  name: vpa-recommender

# ─── Metrics ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# ServiceMonitor for Prometheus scraping (requires kube-prometheus-stack)
metrics:
  serviceMonitor:
    enabled: true
    namespace: monitoring
    labels:
      release: kube-prometheus-stack
    interval: 60s

# ─── Pod Security ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
podSecurityContext:
  runAsNonRoot: true
  runAsUser: 65534
  fsGroup: 65534

securityContext:
  allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
  readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
  capabilities:
    drop: ["ALL"]

---
# finops/infracost/.infracost.yml
# Per-repository Infracost configuration template.
# Copy this file to the root of your Terraform repository as .infracost.yml
# and customize the paths and thresholds.
#
# Documentation: finops/docs/infracost-integration.md

version: 0.1

# ─── Projects ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# List each Terraform root module to be estimated.
projects:
  - path: terraform/
    name: production-infrastructure
    # Optional: Terraform workspace (if using workspaces)
    # terraform_workspace: production
    # Optional: Terraform var files to apply
    # terraform_var_files:
    #   - terraform/production.tfvars

  # Add additional modules if needed:
  # - path: terraform/networking/
  #   name: networking-module

# ─── Cost Thresholds ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# CI pipelines (GitHub Actions, Azure Pipelines, GitLab CI) will fail
# the PR/MR check if either threshold is exceeded.
cost_thresholds:
  # Fail if monthly cost increases by more than this percentage
  percentage_increase: 20    # 20% is a reasonable default for most teams

  # Fail if monthly cost increases by more than this absolute USD amount
  absolute_increase_usd: 500  # $500/month hard cap on surprise increases

# ─── Currency ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
currency: USD

# ─── Usage Data ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Uncomment to provide usage estimates for resources Infracost cannot infer.
# This improves estimate accuracy significantly.
# usage_file: infracost-usage.yml

# ─── Custom Prices ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Uncomment to override pricing with negotiated enterprise discount rates.
# custom_price_overrides: {}

---
# finops/kubernetes/cost-report-cronjob.yaml
# CronJob that generates and exports monthly FinOps cost reports.
# Runs on the 1st of each month at 02:00 UTC.
#
# Apply: kubectl apply -f finops/kubernetes/cost-report-cronjob.yaml -n finops

apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: finops
  labels:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: finops
    finops.org/component: cost-reporting

---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: cost-report-sa
  namespace: finops
  labels:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: cost-report-cronjob
    finops.org/component: cost-reporting

---
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: ClusterRole
metadata:
  name: finops-cost-reader
  labels:
    finops.org/component: cost-reporting
rules:
  - apiGroups: [""]
    resources: ["namespaces", "pods", "persistentvolumes", "persistentvolumeclaims"]
    verbs: ["get", "list"]
  - apiGroups: ["apps"]
    resources: ["deployments", "statefulsets", "daemonsets"]
    verbs: ["get", "list"]

---
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: ClusterRoleBinding
metadata:
  name: finops-cost-reader
  labels:
    finops.org/component: cost-reporting
subjects:
  - kind: ServiceAccount
    name: cost-report-sa
    namespace: finops
roleRef:
  kind: ClusterRole
  name: finops-cost-reader
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io

---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: cost-report-scripts
  namespace: finops
  labels:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: cost-report-cronjob
data:
  # The scripts are mounted from the repository; this ConfigMap holds the
  # entrypoint wrapper that orchestrates report generation + export.
  entrypoint.sh: |
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail

    MONTH="${REPORT_MONTH:-$(date -u +'%Y-%m' -d '1 month ago')}"
    PROVIDER="${CLOUD_PROVIDER:-aws}"
    BUCKET="${REPORT_BUCKET:-}"
    KUBECOST_URL="${KUBECOST_URL:-http://kubecost.finops.svc.cluster.local:9090}"
    CLUSTER_NAME="${CLUSTER_NAME:-production}"

    echo "==> Generating cost report for $MONTH ..."
    python /scripts/generate-cost-report.py \
      --month "$MONTH" \
      --kubecost-url "$KUBECOST_URL" \
      --cluster "$CLUSTER_NAME" \
      --provider "$PROVIDER" \
      --format json \
      --output "/tmp/cost-report-${MONTH}.json"

    python /scripts/generate-cost-report.py \
      --month "$MONTH" \
      --kubecost-url "$KUBECOST_URL" \
      --cluster "$CLUSTER_NAME" \
      --provider "$PROVIDER" \
      --format csv \
      --output "/tmp/cost-report-${MONTH}.csv"

    echo "==> Exporting reports to cloud storage ..."
    if [ -n "$BUCKET" ]; then
      /scripts/export-cost-report.sh \
        --provider "$PROVIDER" \
        --bucket "$BUCKET" \
        --cluster "$CLUSTER_NAME" \
        --file "/tmp/cost-report-${MONTH}.json"

      /scripts/export-cost-report.sh \
        --provider "$PROVIDER" \
        --bucket "$BUCKET" \
        --cluster "$CLUSTER_NAME" \
        --file "/tmp/cost-report-${MONTH}.csv"
    else
      echo "WARNING: REPORT_BUCKET not set — skipping cloud export."
      echo "Reports generated locally:"
      ls -la /tmp/cost-report-${MONTH}.*
    fi

    echo "==> Cost report job complete."

---
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: finops-cost-report
  namespace: finops
  labels:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: cost-report-cronjob
    finops.org/component: cost-reporting
spec:
  # Run at 02:00 UTC on the 1st of every month
  schedule: "0 2 1 * *"
  concurrencyPolicy: Forbid
  successfulJobsHistoryLimit: 3
  failedJobsHistoryLimit: 3
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      backoffLimit: 2
      activeDeadlineSeconds: 1800  # 30 minutes max
      template:
        metadata:
          labels:
            app.kubernetes.io/name: cost-report-cronjob
            finops.org/costcenter: platform-infra
            finops.org/environment: production
        spec:
          serviceAccountName: cost-report-sa
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
          securityContext:
            runAsNonRoot: true
            runAsUser: 65534
            fsGroup: 65534

          containers:
            - name: cost-report
              image: python:3.12-slim
              imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
              command: ["/bin/bash", "/config/entrypoint.sh"]

              env:
                - name: CLOUD_PROVIDER
                  valueFrom:
                    configMapKeyRef:
                      name: finops-config
                      key: cloud_provider
                      optional: true
                - name: REPORT_BUCKET
                  valueFrom:
                    secretKeyRef:
                      name: finops-export-credentials
                      key: report_bucket
                      optional: true
                - name: CLUSTER_NAME
                  valueFrom:
                    configMapKeyRef:
                      name: finops-config
                      key: cluster_name
                      optional: true
                - name: KUBECOST_URL
                  value: "http://kubecost.finops.svc.cluster.local:9090"

              resources:
                requests:
                  cpu: 100m
                  memory: 256Mi
                limits:
                  cpu: 500m
                  memory: 512Mi

              volumeMounts:
                - name: scripts
                  mountPath: /config
                - name: tmp
                  mountPath: /tmp

          volumes:
            - name: scripts
              configMap:
                name: cost-report-scripts
                defaultMode: 0755
            - name: tmp
              emptyDir: {}

---
# finops/policies/enforce-resource-limits.yaml
# Kyverno ClusterPolicy: enforce maximum resource limits per namespace based on
# team budget. Blocks Pods that request resources exceeding configured limits.
#
# Apply:  kubectl apply -f finops/policies/enforce-resource-limits.yaml

apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: enforce-resource-limits
  annotations:
    policies.kyverno.io/title: Enforce Resource Limits for Cost Control
    policies.kyverno.io/category: FinOps Cost Governance
    policies.kyverno.io/severity: medium
    policies.kyverno.io/subject: Pod
    policies.kyverno.io/description: >-
      Ensures all containers have CPU and memory resource limits defined, and
      that requests do not exceed team-budget-based maximums per container.
      This prevents uncontrolled cost growth from resource-hungry workloads.
    finops.org/policy-id: "CP-002"
spec:
  validationFailureAction: Enforce
  background: true
  rules:
    - name: require-cpu-limits
      match:
        any:
          - resources:
              kinds: ["Pod"]
      exclude:
        any:
          - resources:
              namespaces: ["kube-system", "kube-public", "kube-node-lease", "cert-manager"]
      validate:
        message: |
          Policy: enforce-resource-limits | Rule: require-cpu-limits

          Container '{{ request.object.spec.containers[0].name }}' in Pod '{{ request.object.metadata.name }}'
          does not have a CPU limit defined.

          Remediation: Add resources.limits.cpu to every container:
            resources:
              requests:
                cpu: "100m"
              limits:
                cpu: "2"

          See: https://github.com/your-org/cicd-reference/blob/main/finops/docs/cost-tagging-schema.md
        pattern:
          spec:
            containers:
              - resources:
                  limits:
                    cpu: "?*"

    - name: require-memory-limits
      match:
        any:
          - resources:
              kinds: ["Pod"]
      exclude:
        any:
          - resources:
              namespaces: ["kube-system", "kube-public", "kube-node-lease", "cert-manager"]
      validate:
        message: |
          Policy: enforce-resource-limits | Rule: require-memory-limits

          Container in Pod '{{ request.object.metadata.name }}' does not have a memory limit defined.

          Remediation: Add resources.limits.memory to every container:
            resources:
              limits:
                memory: "512Mi"
        pattern:
          spec:
            containers:
              - resources:
                  limits:
                    memory: "?*"

    - name: max-cpu-per-container
      match:
        any:
          - resources:
              kinds: ["Pod"]
      exclude:
        any:
          - resources:
              namespaces: ["kube-system", "kube-public", "kube-node-lease", "cert-manager"]
          # Exclude GPU-approved workloads which may need more resources
          - resources:
              selector:
                matchLabels:
                  finops.org/gpu-approved: "true"
      validate:
        message: |
          Policy: enforce-resource-limits | Rule: max-cpu-per-container

          Container in Pod '{{ request.object.metadata.name }}' requests CPU exceeding the maximum
          allowed per container (8 cores).

          Current request: {{ request.object.spec.containers[0].resources.requests.cpu }}
          Maximum allowed: 8 cores (8000m)

          Remediation:
          1. Reduce CPU request/limit to <= 8 cores
          2. If this workload genuinely needs more than 8 cores, contact the platform team
             to review your budget allocation.
        deny:
          conditions:
            any:
              - key: "{{ request.object.spec.containers[].resources.requests.cpu | to_number(@) }}"
                operator: GreaterThan
                value: 8

    - name: max-memory-per-container
      match:
        any:
          - resources:
              kinds: ["Pod"]
      exclude:
        any:
          - resources:
              namespaces: ["kube-system", "kube-public", "kube-node-lease", "cert-manager"]
          - resources:
              selector:
                matchLabels:
                  finops.org/gpu-approved: "true"
      validate:
        message: |
          Policy: enforce-resource-limits | Rule: max-memory-per-container

          Container in Pod '{{ request.object.metadata.name }}' requests memory exceeding the maximum
          allowed per container (32Gi).

          Maximum allowed: 32Gi
          To request an exemption, contact the platform team.
        deny:
          conditions:
            any:
              - key: "{{ divide(request.object.spec.containers[0].resources.requests.memory || '0', '1073741824') }}"
                operator: GreaterThan
                value: 32

---
# finops/policies/gpu-approval-gate.yaml
# Kyverno ClusterPolicy: require explicit cost-center approval annotation
# for any workload that requests GPU resources (nvidia.com/gpu or amd.com/gpu).
#
# GPU workloads are extremely expensive. This policy gates them behind an
# explicit approval annotation to prevent accidental GPU provisioning.
#
# To allow a GPU workload, add:
#   metadata:
#     annotations:
#       finops.org/gpu-approved: "true"
#       finops.org/gpu-approved-by: "john.doe@company.com"
#       finops.org/gpu-approved-date: "2025-01-15"
#       finops.org/gpu-justification: "ML training job for Q1 model"
#
# Apply:  kubectl apply -f finops/policies/gpu-approval-gate.yaml

apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: gpu-approval-gate
  annotations:
    policies.kyverno.io/title: GPU Workload Approval Gate
    policies.kyverno.io/category: FinOps Cost Governance
    policies.kyverno.io/severity: high
    policies.kyverno.io/subject: Pod
    policies.kyverno.io/description: >-
      Blocks deployment of workloads requesting GPU resources unless they have
      the explicit approval annotation finops.org/gpu-approved: "true".
      GPU instances (p3, p4, A100 etc.) can cost $3-$30/hour each.
      This gate prevents accidental GPU provisioning.
    finops.org/policy-id: "CP-003"
spec:
  validationFailureAction: Enforce
  background: true
  rules:
    - name: require-gpu-approval-annotation
      match:
        any:
          - resources:
              kinds: ["Pod"]
      preconditions:
        any:
          # Only apply to pods that actually request GPU resources
          - key: "{{ request.object.spec.containers[].resources.limits.\"nvidia.com/gpu\" | length(@) }}"
            operator: GreaterThan
            value: 0
          - key: "{{ request.object.spec.containers[].resources.limits.\"amd.com/gpu\" | length(@) }}"
            operator: GreaterThan
            value: 0
      validate:
        message: |
          Policy: gpu-approval-gate | Rule: require-gpu-approval-annotation

          Pod '{{ request.object.metadata.name }}' requests GPU resources but lacks the required
          approval annotation: finops.org/gpu-approved: "true"

          GPU instances are expensive ($3–$30/hour). Approval is required before provisioning.

          Remediation: Obtain approval and add the following annotations to your Pod/Deployment:
            metadata:
              annotations:
                finops.org/gpu-approved: "true"
                finops.org/gpu-approved-by: "manager@company.com"
                finops.org/gpu-approved-date: "YYYY-MM-DD"
                finops.org/gpu-justification: "Brief description of the business need"

          Approval process: https://github.com/your-org/cicd-reference/blob/main/finops/docs/finops-workflow.md#gpu-approval
        pattern:
          metadata:
            annotations:
              finops.org/gpu-approved: "true"

    - name: require-gpu-approval-metadata
      match:
        any:
          - resources:
              kinds: ["Pod"]
      preconditions:
        any:
          - key: "{{ request.object.spec.containers[].resources.limits.\"nvidia.com/gpu\" | length(@) }}"
            operator: GreaterThan
            value: 0
          - key: "{{ request.object.spec.containers[].resources.limits.\"amd.com/gpu\" | length(@) }}"
            operator: GreaterThan
            value: 0
          - key: "{{ request.object.metadata.annotations.\"finops.org/gpu-approved\" }}"
            operator: Equals
            value: "true"
      validate:
        message: |
          Policy: gpu-approval-gate | Rule: require-gpu-approval-metadata

          Pod '{{ request.object.metadata.name }}' has gpu-approved: "true" but is missing
          required approval metadata annotations.

          Required annotations:
            finops.org/gpu-approved-by    — Email of approving manager
            finops.org/gpu-approved-date  — Date of approval (YYYY-MM-DD)
            finops.org/gpu-justification  — Business justification for GPU usage
        pattern:
          metadata:
            annotations:
              finops.org/gpu-approved-by: "?*"
              finops.org/gpu-approved-date: "?*"
              finops.org/gpu-justification: "?*"

---
# finops/policies/require-cost-labels.yaml
# Kyverno ClusterPolicy: require finops.org/costcenter and finops.org/environment
# labels on all Pods. Violations block pod creation with a descriptive error.
#
# Apply:  kubectl apply -f finops/policies/require-cost-labels.yaml
# Test:   kyverno test finops/policies/ --test-case require-cost-labels

apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: require-cost-labels
  annotations:
    policies.kyverno.io/title: Require FinOps Cost Labels
    policies.kyverno.io/category: FinOps Cost Governance
    policies.kyverno.io/severity: medium
    policies.kyverno.io/subject: Pod
    policies.kyverno.io/description: >-
      Validates that all Pods have the required FinOps cost allocation labels:
      finops.org/costcenter and finops.org/environment. These labels are
      mandatory for accurate chargeback reporting and cost tracking.
    finops.org/policy-id: "CP-001"
    finops.org/remediation: >-
      Add the labels finops.org/costcenter and finops.org/environment to your
      Pod spec or the owning controller (Deployment, StatefulSet, etc.).
spec:
  validationFailureAction: Enforce
  background: true
  rules:
    - name: validate-costcenter-label
      match:
        any:
          - resources:
              kinds: ["Pod"]
      exclude:
        any:
          - resources:
              namespaces:
                - kube-system
                - kube-public
                - kube-node-lease
                - cert-manager
      validate:
        message: |
          Policy: require-cost-labels | Rule: validate-costcenter-label

          Pod '{{ request.object.metadata.name }}' in namespace '{{ request.object.metadata.namespace }}'
          is missing the required label 'finops.org/costcenter'.

          Remediation: Add the label to your Pod/Deployment spec:
            metadata:
              labels:
                finops.org/costcenter: "your-cost-center"

          Valid cost center values: engineering, data-science, frontend, platform-infra
          See: https://github.com/your-org/cicd-reference/blob/main/finops/docs/cost-tagging-schema.md
        pattern:
          metadata:
            labels:
              finops.org/costcenter: "?*"

    - name: validate-environment-label
      match:
        any:
          - resources:
              kinds: ["Pod"]
      exclude:
        any:
          - resources:
              namespaces:
                - kube-system
                - kube-public
                - kube-node-lease
                - cert-manager
      validate:
        message: |
          Policy: require-cost-labels | Rule: validate-environment-label

          Pod '{{ request.object.metadata.name }}' in namespace '{{ request.object.metadata.namespace }}'
          is missing the required label 'finops.org/environment'.

          Remediation: Add the label to your Pod/Deployment spec:
            metadata:
              labels:
                finops.org/environment: "production"  # dev | staging | production

          See: https://github.com/your-org/cicd-reference/blob/main/finops/docs/cost-tagging-schema.md
        pattern:
          metadata:
            labels:
              finops.org/environment: "dev | staging | production"

---
# finops/policies/require-pdb-large-workloads.yaml
# Kyverno ClusterPolicy: require a PodDisruptionBudget for workloads that
# request more than 4 CPU cores OR more than 8Gi of memory.
# Large workloads without PDBs risk unnecessary downtime during node maintenance,
# which can also cause unexpected cost spikes from emergency scaling.
#
# Apply:  kubectl apply -f finops/policies/require-pdb-large-workloads.yaml

apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: require-pdb-large-workloads
  annotations:
    policies.kyverno.io/title: Require PodDisruptionBudget for Large Workloads
    policies.kyverno.io/category: FinOps Cost Governance
    policies.kyverno.io/severity: medium
    policies.kyverno.io/subject: Deployment,StatefulSet
    policies.kyverno.io/description: >-
      Validates that Deployments and StatefulSets requesting more than 4 CPU cores
      or 8Gi memory have a corresponding PodDisruptionBudget in the same namespace.
      Without a PDB, large workloads can be entirely evicted during maintenance,
      causing service disruption and emergency scaling costs.
    finops.org/policy-id: "CP-004"
spec:
  validationFailureAction: Audit
  background: true
  rules:
    - name: check-pdb-exists-for-large-deployment
      match:
        any:
          - resources:
              kinds: ["Deployment"]
      exclude:
        any:
          - resources:
              namespaces: ["kube-system", "kube-public", "kube-node-lease", "cert-manager"]
      preconditions:
        any:
          # Only run for large workloads: > 4 CPU cores or > 8Gi memory (8589934592 bytes)
          - key: "{{ request.object.spec.template.spec.containers[].resources.requests.cpu | sum_of_integers(@) }}"
            operator: GreaterThan
            value: 4
          - key: "{{ request.object.spec.template.spec.containers[].resources.requests.memory | sum_of_integers(@) }}"
            operator: GreaterThan
            value: 8589934592
      validate:
        message: |
          Policy: require-pdb-large-workloads | Rule: check-pdb-exists-for-large-deployment

          Deployment '{{ request.object.metadata.name }}' in namespace '{{ request.object.metadata.namespace }}'
          requests significant resources (>4 CPU cores or >8Gi memory) but no PodDisruptionBudget
          was found in the same namespace.

          Large workloads without PDBs risk complete eviction during node maintenance, causing:
          - Service downtime and potential SLA violations
          - Emergency scaling costs
          - Potential data corruption for stateful workloads

          Remediation: Create a PodDisruptionBudget for your workload:
            apiVersion: policy/v1
            kind: PodDisruptionBudget
            metadata:
              name: {{ request.object.metadata.name }}-pdb
              namespace: {{ request.object.metadata.namespace }}
            spec:
              minAvailable: 1   # Keep at least 1 replica running
              selector:
                matchLabels:
                  app: {{ request.object.metadata.name }}

          See: https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/run-application/configure-pdb/
          Reference: https://github.com/your-org/cicd-reference/blob/main/cd/kubernetes/_base/pdb.yaml
        deny:
          conditions:
            all:
              # Check if a PDB exists for this workload in the same namespace
              # This uses the cluster-wide resource context
              - key: "{{ request.object.metadata.name }}"
                operator: AnyNotIn
                value: "{{ policycontext.namespaceLabels.\"finops.org/pdb-exempt\" || '' }}"

    - name: check-pdb-exists-for-large-statefulset
      match:
        any:
          - resources:
              kinds: ["StatefulSet"]
      exclude:
        any:
          - resources:
              namespaces: ["kube-system", "kube-public", "kube-node-lease", "cert-manager"]
      preconditions:
        any:
          - key: "{{ request.object.spec.template.spec.containers[].resources.requests.cpu | sum_of_integers(@) }}"
            operator: GreaterThan
            value: 4
          - key: "{{ request.object.spec.template.spec.containers[].resources.requests.memory | sum_of_integers(@) }}"
            operator: GreaterThan
            value: 8589934592
      validate:
        message: |
          Policy: require-pdb-large-workloads | Rule: check-pdb-exists-for-large-statefulset

          StatefulSet '{{ request.object.metadata.name }}' in namespace '{{ request.object.metadata.namespace }}'
          requests significant resources (>4 CPU or >8Gi memory) but no PodDisruptionBudget exists.

          Remediation: Add a PDB matching your StatefulSet's pod selector labels.
          See: https://github.com/your-org/cicd-reference/blob/main/cd/kubernetes/_base/pdb.yaml

          To temporarily exempt this workload, add the namespace label:
            kubectl label namespace {{ request.object.metadata.namespace }} \
              finops.org/pdb-exempt={{ request.object.metadata.name }}
        deny:
          conditions:
            all:
              - key: "{{ request.object.metadata.name }}"
                operator: AnyNotIn
                value: "{{ policycontext.namespaceLabels.\"finops.org/pdb-exempt\" || '' }}"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# finops/policies/test-policies.sh
# Validates all Kyverno ClusterPolicy files using the Kyverno CLI test framework.
# Tests both valid and invalid Pod manifests to verify enforcement and error messages.
#
# Prerequisites:
#   kyverno CLI installed: https://kyverno.io/docs/kyverno-cli/#installation
#
# Usage:
#   ./finops/policies/test-policies.sh
#   ./finops/policies/test-policies.sh --policy require-cost-labels.yaml
#   ./finops/policies/test-policies.sh --help

set -euo pipefail

POLICIES_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
TEMP_DIR="$(mktemp -d)"
FAILURES=0
POLICY_FILTER=""

cleanup() { rm -rf "$TEMP_DIR"; }
trap cleanup EXIT

while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case "$1" in
    --policy) POLICY_FILTER="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --help)
      echo "Usage: $0 [--policy <filename>]"
      echo "  Runs kyverno validate + kyverno test on all FinOps ClusterPolicies."
      exit 0 ;;
    *) echo "Unknown argument: $1"; exit 1 ;;
  esac
done

# ─── Check kyverno CLI ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
if ! command -v kyverno &>/dev/null; then
  echo "ERROR: kyverno CLI not found."
  echo "Install: https://kyverno.io/docs/kyverno-cli/#installation"
  exit 1
fi
echo "==> kyverno CLI: $(kyverno version 2>/dev/null | head -1)"

# ─── Validate YAML syntax ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
echo ""
echo "==> Validating policy YAML syntax ..."
for policy in "$POLICIES_DIR"/*.yaml; do
  [[ -z "$POLICY_FILTER" || "$(basename "$policy")" == "$POLICY_FILTER" ]] || continue
  [[ "$(basename "$policy")" == "README.md" ]] && continue
  echo -n "  Validating $(basename "$policy") ... "
  if kyverno validate "$policy" &>/dev/null; then
    echo "OK"
  else
    echo "FAIL"
    kyverno validate "$policy" || true
    FAILURES=$((FAILURES + 1))
  fi
done

# ─── Create test fixture Pod manifests ───────────────────────────────────────
echo ""
echo "==> Creating test fixtures ..."

# Valid pod — all required labels present, resource limits set
cat > "$TEMP_DIR/pod-valid.yaml" <<'EOF'
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: valid-pod
  namespace: test-ns
  labels:
    app: myapp
    finops.org/costcenter: "engineering"
    finops.org/environment: "production"
  annotations:
    finops.org/gpu-approved: "true"
spec:
  containers:
    - name: app
      image: nginx:1.25
      resources:
        requests:
          cpu: "250m"
          memory: "256Mi"
        limits:
          cpu: "500m"
          memory: "512Mi"
EOF

# Invalid pod — missing cost labels
cat > "$TEMP_DIR/pod-no-labels.yaml" <<'EOF'
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: no-label-pod
  namespace: test-ns
  labels:
    app: myapp
spec:
  containers:
    - name: app
      image: nginx:1.25
      resources:
        requests:
          cpu: "250m"
          memory: "256Mi"
        limits:
          cpu: "500m"
          memory: "512Mi"
EOF

# Invalid pod — missing resource limits
cat > "$TEMP_DIR/pod-no-limits.yaml" <<'EOF'
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: no-limits-pod
  namespace: test-ns
  labels:
    finops.org/costcenter: "engineering"
    finops.org/environment: "production"
spec:
  containers:
    - name: app
      image: nginx:1.25
      resources:
        requests:
          cpu: "250m"
          memory: "256Mi"
EOF

# Invalid pod — GPU without approval
cat > "$TEMP_DIR/pod-gpu-unapproved.yaml" <<'EOF'
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: gpu-pod
  namespace: test-ns
  labels:
    finops.org/costcenter: "engineering"
    finops.org/environment: "production"
spec:
  containers:
    - name: trainer
      image: nvidia/cuda:12.0-runtime
      resources:
        requests:
          nvidia.com/gpu: "1"
        limits:
          cpu: "4"
          memory: "8Gi"
          nvidia.com/gpu: "1"
EOF

# Valid GPU pod — with approval annotation
cat > "$TEMP_DIR/pod-gpu-approved.yaml" <<'EOF'
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: gpu-pod-approved
  namespace: test-ns
  labels:
    finops.org/costcenter: "data-science"
    finops.org/environment: "production"
  annotations:
    finops.org/gpu-approved: "true"
    finops.org/gpu-cost-center: "data-science"
    finops.org/gpu-justification: "ML model training"
spec:
  containers:
    - name: trainer
      image: nvidia/cuda:12.0-runtime
      resources:
        requests:
          nvidia.com/gpu: "1"
        limits:
          cpu: "4"
          memory: "8Gi"
          nvidia.com/gpu: "1"
EOF

echo "  Fixtures created in $TEMP_DIR"

# ─── Run kyverno apply tests ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
echo ""
echo "==> Testing require-cost-labels policy ..."

run_test() {
  local policy="$1"
  local resource="$2"
  local expect_pass="$3"   # "pass" or "fail"
  local description="$4"

  [[ -z "$POLICY_FILTER" || "$(basename "$policy")" == "$POLICY_FILTER" ]] || return 0
  [[ -f "$POLICIES_DIR/$(basename "$policy")" ]] || return 0

  echo -n "  [$description] "
  OUTPUT=$(kyverno apply "$POLICIES_DIR/$(basename "$policy")" --resource="$resource" 2>&1 || true)

  if [[ "$expect_pass" == "pass" ]]; then
    if echo "$OUTPUT" | grep -q "pass: 1"; then
      echo "PASS ✓"
    else
      echo "FAIL ✗ (expected pass)"
      echo "    Output: $(echo "$OUTPUT" | tail -5)"
      FAILURES=$((FAILURES + 1))
    fi
  else
    if echo "$OUTPUT" | grep -q "fail: 1\|violations found"; then
      echo "PASS ✓ (correctly rejected)"
    else
      echo "FAIL ✗ (expected rejection)"
      echo "    Output: $(echo "$OUTPUT" | tail -5)"
      FAILURES=$((FAILURES + 1))
    fi
  fi
}

# require-cost-labels tests
run_test "require-cost-labels.yaml" "$TEMP_DIR/pod-valid.yaml"         "pass" "Valid pod with all labels → allowed"
run_test "require-cost-labels.yaml" "$TEMP_DIR/pod-no-labels.yaml"     "fail" "Pod without labels → blocked"

# enforce-resource-limits tests
echo ""
echo "==> Testing enforce-resource-limits policy ..."
run_test "enforce-resource-limits.yaml" "$TEMP_DIR/pod-valid.yaml"     "pass" "Pod with limits → allowed"
run_test "enforce-resource-limits.yaml" "$TEMP_DIR/pod-no-limits.yaml" "fail" "Pod without limits → blocked"

# gpu-approval-gate tests
echo ""
echo "==> Testing gpu-approval-gate policy ..."
run_test "gpu-approval-gate.yaml" "$TEMP_DIR/pod-gpu-approved.yaml"    "pass" "GPU pod with approval → allowed"
run_test "gpu-approval-gate.yaml" "$TEMP_DIR/pod-gpu-unapproved.yaml"  "fail" "GPU pod without approval → blocked"

# ─── Results ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
echo ""
echo "=========================="
if [[ $FAILURES -eq 0 ]]; then
  echo "  All policy tests PASSED ✅"
else
  echo "  $FAILURES test(s) FAILED ❌"
  exit 1
fi

---
# finops/prometheus/alertmanager-anomaly-config.yaml
# Dedicated Alertmanager configuration for cost anomaly alerts.
# Routes anomaly alerts to appropriate channels based on severity and namespace.
#
# Apply as a patch to the existing Alertmanager configuration, or use standalone:
#   kubectl create secret generic alertmanager-finops-anomaly \
#     --from-file=alertmanager.yaml=finops/prometheus/alertmanager-anomaly-config.yaml \
#     -n monitoring

global:
  resolve_timeout: 5m

# ─── Notification templates ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
templates:
  - /etc/alertmanager/templates/finops-anomaly.tmpl

# ─── Routing ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
route:
  group_by: ["alertname", "namespace", "anomaly_type"]
  group_wait: 1m
  group_interval: 10m
  repeat_interval: 6h
  receiver: "default-anomaly"

  routes:
    # Critical anomaly (>100% spike) — PagerDuty + Slack
    - matchers:
        - name: alertname
          value: CostAnomalyCritical
      receiver: "pagerduty-anomaly-critical"
      continue: true

    - matchers:
        - name: alertname
          value: CostAnomalyCritical
      receiver: "slack-anomaly-critical"

    # Spike warning (>50% over 7d baseline)
    - matchers:
        - name: alertname
          value: CostAnomalySpike
      receiver: "slack-anomaly-warning"

    # New namespace with high spend
    - matchers:
        - name: alertname
          value: NewNamespaceHighCost
      receiver: "slack-anomaly-new-namespace"

    # Tag compliance degradation
    - matchers:
        - name: alertname
          value: CostTagComplianceLow
      receiver: "slack-tag-compliance"

# ─── Receivers ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
receivers:
  - name: "default-anomaly"
    slack_configs:
      - api_url: "${SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL_FINOPS}"
        channel: "#finops-anomalies"
        title: "FinOps Anomaly: {{ .GroupLabels.alertname }}"
        text: "{{ range .Alerts }}{{ .Annotations.description }}\n{{ end }}"
        send_resolved: true

  - name: "pagerduty-anomaly-critical"
    pagerduty_configs:
      - routing_key: "${PAGERDUTY_INTEGRATION_KEY_PLATFORM}"
        severity: "critical"
        summary: "Cost Spike >100%: {{ .GroupLabels.namespace }}"
        description: |
          {{ range .Alerts }}
          Namespace: {{ .Labels.namespace }}
          Current cost: {{ .Annotations.current_cost }}
          Baseline (7d avg): {{ .Annotations.baseline_cost }}
          Increase: {{ .Annotations.percent_increase }}%
          {{ end }}
        details:
          namespace: "{{ .GroupLabels.namespace }}"
          runbook: "https://github.com/your-org/cicd-reference/blob/main/finops/docs/runbooks/investigate-cost-spike.md"

  - name: "slack-anomaly-critical"
    slack_configs:
      - api_url: "${SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL_PLATFORM}"
        channel: "#platform-emergency"
        title: "🔴 CRITICAL Cost Spike: {{ .GroupLabels.namespace }}"
        color: "danger"
        text: |
          @oncall — Cost anomaly requires immediate attention.
          {{ range .Alerts }}
          *Namespace:* {{ .Labels.namespace }}
          *Current hourly cost:* {{ .Annotations.current_cost }}
          *7-day baseline:* {{ .Annotations.baseline_cost }}
          *Increase:* {{ .Annotations.percent_increase }}%
          <{{ .Annotations.dashboard_url }}|📊 Investigate in Grafana>
          <{{ .Annotations.runbook_url }}|📖 Runbook>
          {{ end }}
        send_resolved: true

  - name: "slack-anomaly-warning"
    slack_configs:
      - api_url: "${SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL_FINOPS}"
        channel: "#finops-anomalies"
        title: "⚠️ Cost Spike Detected: {{ .GroupLabels.namespace }}"
        color: "warning"
        text: |
          {{ range .Alerts }}
          *Namespace:* {{ .Labels.namespace }}
          *Current hourly cost:* {{ .Annotations.current_cost }}
          *7-day baseline:* {{ .Annotations.baseline_cost }}
          *Increase:* {{ .Annotations.percent_increase }}%
          *Anomaly type:* {{ .Labels.anomaly_type }}
          <{{ .Annotations.dashboard_url }}|📊 View in Grafana> | <{{ .Annotations.runbook_url }}|📖 Runbook>
          {{ end }}
        send_resolved: true

  - name: "slack-anomaly-new-namespace"
    slack_configs:
      - api_url: "${SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL_FINOPS}"
        channel: "#finops-anomalies"
        title: "🆕 New High-Cost Namespace: {{ .GroupLabels.namespace }}"
        color: "warning"
        text: |
          A new namespace has appeared with significant spend within 24h.
          {{ range .Alerts }}
          *Namespace:* {{ .Labels.namespace }}
          *Cost (last 24h):* {{ .Annotations.current_cost }}
          *Threshold:* $100/day
          Check if this workload has the required FinOps cost labels.
          <{{ .Annotations.dashboard_url }}|📊 View Cost Dashboard>
          {{ end }}
        send_resolved: false

  - name: "slack-tag-compliance"
    slack_configs:
      - api_url: "${SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL_FINOPS}"
        channel: "#finops-alerts"
        title: "🏷️ Tag Compliance Below 95%: {{ .GroupLabels.namespace }}"
        color: "warning"
        text: |
          {{ range .Alerts }}
          *Namespace:* {{ .Labels.namespace }}
          *Compliance:* {{ .Annotations.compliance_pct }}%
          *Non-compliant pods:* {{ .Annotations.non_compliant_count }}
          Run: `python finops/scripts/validate-cost-tags.py --namespace {{ .Labels.namespace }}`
          {{ end }}
        send_resolved: true

# ─── Inhibition rules ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
inhibit_rules:
  # Suppress spike warning when critical is already firing for the same namespace
  - source_matchers:
      - name: alertname
        value: CostAnomalyCritical
    target_matchers:
      - name: alertname
        value: CostAnomalySpike
    equal: ["namespace"]

---
# finops/prometheus/alertmanager-budget-config.yaml
# Alertmanager configuration for routing FinOps budget and anomaly alerts.
# Integrates with Slack, Microsoft Teams, and PagerDuty.
#
# Apply as a Secret:
#   kubectl create secret generic alertmanager-finops \
#     --from-file=alertmanager.yaml=finops/prometheus/alertmanager-budget-config.yaml \
#     -n monitoring

global:
  resolve_timeout: 5m

# ─── Notification templates ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
templates:
  - /etc/alertmanager/templates/finops.tmpl

# ─── Routing ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
route:
  group_by: ["alertname", "cost_center", "namespace"]
  group_wait: 30s
  group_interval: 5m
  repeat_interval: 4h
  receiver: "default-receiver"

  routes:
    # Emergency budget alerts — PagerDuty + Slack
    - matchers:
        - name: escalation
          value: emergency
      receiver: "pagerduty-emergency"
      continue: true

    - matchers:
        - name: escalation
          value: emergency
      receiver: "slack-emergency"

    # Critical budget alerts
    - matchers:
        - name: severity
          value: critical
        - name: type
          value: budget
      receiver: "slack-critical-budget"
      continue: true

    - matchers:
        - name: severity
          value: critical
        - name: type
          value: budget
        - name: cost_center
          value: data-science
      receiver: "pagerduty-data-science"

    # Warning budget alerts — Slack only
    - matchers:
        - name: severity
          value: warning
        - name: type
          value: budget
      receiver: "slack-warning-budget"

    # Cost anomaly alerts
    - matchers:
        - name: type
          value: cost-anomaly
      receiver: "slack-anomaly"
      continue: true

    - matchers:
        - name: severity
          value: critical
        - name: type
          value: cost-anomaly
      receiver: "pagerduty-platform"

# ─── Receivers ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
receivers:
  - name: "default-receiver"
    slack_configs:
      - api_url: "${SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL_FINOPS}"
        channel: "#finops-alerts"
        title: "FinOps Alert: {{ .GroupLabels.alertname }}"
        text: "{{ range .Alerts }}{{ .Annotations.description }}\n{{ end }}"
        send_resolved: true

  - name: "slack-warning-budget"
    slack_configs:
      - api_url: "${SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL_FINOPS}"
        channel: "#finops-budget-warnings"
        title: "⚠️ Budget Warning: {{ .GroupLabels.cost_center }}"
        color: "warning"
        text: |
          {{ range .Alerts }}
          *Cost Center:* {{ .Labels.cost_center }}
          *Severity:* {{ .Labels.severity }}
          {{ .Annotations.description }}
          <{{ .Annotations.dashboard_url }}|View Dashboard>
          {{ end }}
        send_resolved: true

  - name: "slack-critical-budget"
    slack_configs:
      - api_url: "${SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL_FINOPS}"
        channel: "#finops-budget-critical"
        title: "🚨 Budget EXCEEDED: {{ .GroupLabels.cost_center }}"
        color: "danger"
        text: |
          {{ range .Alerts }}
          *Cost Center:* {{ .Labels.cost_center }}
          {{ .Annotations.description }}
          <{{ .Annotations.runbook_url }}|Runbook> | <{{ .Annotations.dashboard_url }}|Dashboard>
          {{ end }}
        send_resolved: true

  - name: "slack-emergency"
    slack_configs:
      - api_url: "${SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL_PLATFORM}"
        channel: "#platform-emergency"
        title: "🔴 EMERGENCY: {{ .GroupLabels.cost_center }} — 120%+ Budget"
        color: "danger"
        text: |
          @oncall EMERGENCY budget breach detected!
          {{ range .Alerts }}{{ .Annotations.description }}{{ end }}
        send_resolved: true

  - name: "slack-anomaly"
    slack_configs:
      - api_url: "${SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL_FINOPS}"
        channel: "#finops-anomalies"
        title: "📊 Cost Anomaly: {{ .GroupLabels.namespace }}"
        color: "warning"
        text: |
          {{ range .Alerts }}
          *Namespace:* {{ .Labels.namespace }}
          *Type:* {{ .Labels.anomaly_type }}
          {{ .Annotations.description }}
          <{{ .Annotations.dashboard_url }}|Investigate>
          {{ end }}
        send_resolved: true

  - name: "pagerduty-platform"
    pagerduty_configs:
      - routing_key: "${PAGERDUTY_INTEGRATION_KEY_PLATFORM}"
        severity: "critical"
        summary: "FinOps: {{ .GroupLabels.alertname }} — {{ .GroupLabels.namespace }}"
        description: "{{ range .Alerts }}{{ .Annotations.description }}\n{{ end }}"
        details:
          cost_center: "{{ .GroupLabels.cost_center }}"
          namespace: "{{ .GroupLabels.namespace }}"
          runbook: "{{ (index .Alerts 0).Annotations.runbook_url }}"

  - name: "pagerduty-emergency"
    pagerduty_configs:
      - routing_key: "${PAGERDUTY_INTEGRATION_KEY_PLATFORM}"
        severity: "critical"
        summary: "EMERGENCY Budget: {{ .GroupLabels.cost_center }} > 120%"
        description: "{{ range .Alerts }}{{ .Annotations.description }}\n{{ end }}"

  - name: "pagerduty-data-science"
    pagerduty_configs:
      - routing_key: "${PAGERDUTY_INTEGRATION_KEY_DATA_SCIENCE}"
        severity: "critical"
        summary: "FinOps Budget Alert: data-science {{ .GroupLabels.alertname }}"
        description: "{{ range .Alerts }}{{ .Annotations.description }}\n{{ end }}"

# ─── Inhibition rules ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
inhibit_rules:
  # Suppress warning when critical is already firing for the same cost center
  - source_matchers:
      - name: severity
        value: critical
    target_matchers:
      - name: severity
        value: warning
    equal: ["cost_center", "alertname"]

  # Suppress anomaly warning when critical anomaly is firing
  - source_matchers:
      - name: anomaly_type
        value: critical-spike
    target_matchers:
      - name: anomaly_type
        value: spike
    equal: ["namespace"]

---
# finops/prometheus/anomaly-alerts.yaml
# Prometheus alerting rules for cost anomaly detection.
# Triggers when costs spike >50% vs 7-day average or new namespaces exceed $100/24h.
#
# Apply: kubectl apply -f finops/prometheus/anomaly-alerts.yaml -n monitoring

apiVersion: monitoring.coreos.com/v1
kind: PrometheusRule
metadata:
  name: finops-anomaly-alerts
  namespace: monitoring
  labels:
    app: kube-prometheus-stack
    release: kube-prometheus-stack
    finops.org/component: anomaly-detection
spec:
  groups:
    - name: finops.cost.anomalies
      interval: 5m
      rules:
        # ── Cost spike: >50% above 7-day rolling average ─────────────────────
        - alert: CostAnomalySpike
          expr: |
            (
              sum by (namespace, cost_center) (kubecost_namespace_cost_hourly)
              -
              sum by (namespace, cost_center) (avg_over_time(kubecost_namespace_cost_hourly[7d]))
            )
            /
            sum by (namespace, cost_center) (avg_over_time(kubecost_namespace_cost_hourly[7d]))
            > 0.50
          for: 30m
          labels:
            severity: warning
            component: finops
            type: cost-anomaly
            anomaly_type: spike
          annotations:
            summary: "Cost spike detected in namespace {{ $labels.namespace }}"
            description: |
              Namespace {{ $labels.namespace }} (cost center: {{ $labels.cost_center }}) has a
              cost spike of {{ printf "%.1f" (mulf $value 100) }}% above its 7-day baseline.

              Current hourly cost : ${{ printf "%.2f" (query "sum(kubecost_namespace_cost_hourly{namespace=\"" $labels.namespace "\"})" | first | value) }}/hr
              7-day average       : ${{ printf "%.2f" (query "sum(avg_over_time(kubecost_namespace_cost_hourly{namespace=\"" $labels.namespace "\"}[7d]))" | first | value) }}/hr

              Investigate at: {{ $externalURL }}/d/finops-anomaly-detection?var-namespace={{ $labels.namespace }}
            runbook_url: "https://github.com/your-org/cicd-reference/blob/main/finops/docs/runbooks/investigate-cost-spike.md"
            dashboard_url: "{{ $externalURL }}/d/finops-anomaly-detection?var-namespace={{ $labels.namespace }}"

        # ── Critical: >100% above 7-day average ─────────────────────────────
        - alert: CostAnomalyCritical
          expr: |
            (
              sum by (namespace, cost_center) (kubecost_namespace_cost_hourly)
              -
              sum by (namespace, cost_center) (avg_over_time(kubecost_namespace_cost_hourly[7d]))
            )
            /
            sum by (namespace, cost_center) (avg_over_time(kubecost_namespace_cost_hourly[7d]))
            > 1.00
          for: 15m
          labels:
            severity: critical
            component: finops
            type: cost-anomaly
            anomaly_type: critical-spike
          annotations:
            summary: "CRITICAL cost spike in namespace {{ $labels.namespace }} — doubled vs baseline"
            description: |
              Namespace {{ $labels.namespace }} costs have more than DOUBLED vs the 7-day baseline.
              Spike: {{ printf "%.1f" (mulf $value 100) }}% above baseline.
              Immediate investigation required.
            runbook_url: "https://github.com/your-org/cicd-reference/blob/main/finops/docs/runbooks/investigate-cost-spike.md"
            dashboard_url: "{{ $externalURL }}/d/finops-anomaly-detection?var-namespace={{ $labels.namespace }}"

        # ── New namespace: >$100 cost within 24 hours of creation ────────────
        - alert: CostAnomalyNewNamespace
          expr: |
            sum by (namespace) (
              increase(kubecost_namespace_cost_hourly[24h])
            ) > 100
            and on (namespace) (
              (time() - kube_namespace_created) < 86400
            )
          for: 10m
          labels:
            severity: warning
            component: finops
            type: cost-anomaly
            anomaly_type: new-namespace-high-cost
          annotations:
            summary: "New namespace {{ $labels.namespace }} exceeded $100 cost in first 24 hours"
            description: |
              Namespace {{ $labels.namespace }} was created within the last 24 hours and has
              already incurred more than $100 in costs.
              24h spend: ${{ printf "%.2f" $value }}

              This may indicate an accidental deployment or runaway resource allocation.
              Verify: {{ $externalURL }}/d/finops-cost-overview?var-namespace={{ $labels.namespace }}
            runbook_url: "https://github.com/your-org/cicd-reference/blob/main/finops/docs/runbooks/investigate-cost-spike.md"

        # ── Cluster-wide unusual cost growth ────────────────────────────────
        - alert: ClusterCostAnomalyGrowth
          expr: |
            (
              sum(kubecost_namespace_cost_hourly)
              -
              sum(avg_over_time(kubecost_namespace_cost_hourly[7d]))
            )
            /
            sum(avg_over_time(kubecost_namespace_cost_hourly[7d]))
            > 0.30
          for: 60m
          labels:
            severity: warning
            component: finops
            type: cost-anomaly
            anomaly_type: cluster-growth
          annotations:
            summary: "Cluster-wide cost has grown >30% vs 7-day average"
            description: |
              Total cluster costs are {{ printf "%.1f" (mulf $value 100) }}% higher than
              the 7-day rolling average. This may indicate cluster-wide resource sprawl.
              Review: {{ $externalURL }}/d/finops-cost-overview

# finops/prometheus/budget-alerts.yaml
# Prometheus alerting rules for budget threshold monitoring.
# Triggers at 80% (warning), 100% (critical), and 120% (emergency).
#
# Apply with:
#   kubectl apply -f finops/prometheus/budget-alerts.yaml -n monitoring
# Or use: ./finops/scripts/deploy-budget-alerts.sh

apiVersion: monitoring.coreos.com/v1
kind: PrometheusRule
metadata:
  name: finops-budget-alerts
  namespace: monitoring
  labels:
    app: kube-prometheus-stack
    release: kube-prometheus-stack
    finops.org/component: budget-alerting
spec:
  groups:
    - name: finops.budget.thresholds
      interval: 5m
      rules:
        # ── Warning: 80% of monthly budget ──────────────────────────────────
        - alert: BudgetThresholdWarning
          expr: |
            (
              sum by (cost_center) (finops_budget_current_spend)
              /
              sum by (cost_center) (finops_budget_threshold)
            ) >= 0.80
            and
            (
              sum by (cost_center) (finops_budget_current_spend)
              /
              sum by (cost_center) (finops_budget_threshold)
            ) < 1.00
          for: 10m
          labels:
            severity: warning
            component: finops
            type: budget
          annotations:
            summary: "Budget Warning — {{ $labels.cost_center }} has reached 80% of monthly budget"
            description: |
              Cost center {{ $labels.cost_center }} is at {{ printf "%.1f" (mulf $value 100) }}% of its monthly budget.
              Current spend: ${{ printf "%.2f" (query "sum by (cost_center) (finops_budget_current_spend{cost_center=\"" $labels.cost_center "\"})" | first | value) }}
              Monthly threshold: ${{ printf "%.2f" (query "sum by (cost_center) (finops_budget_threshold{cost_center=\"" $labels.cost_center "\"})" | first | value) }}
            runbook_url: "https://github.com/your-org/cicd-reference/blob/main/finops/docs/runbooks/investigate-cost-spike.md"
            dashboard_url: "{{ $externalURL }}/d/finops-budget-tracking?var-cost_center={{ $labels.cost_center }}"

        # ── Critical: 100% of monthly budget ────────────────────────────────
        - alert: BudgetThresholdCritical
          expr: |
            (
              sum by (cost_center) (finops_budget_current_spend)
              /
              sum by (cost_center) (finops_budget_threshold)
            ) >= 1.00
            and
            (
              sum by (cost_center) (finops_budget_current_spend)
              /
              sum by (cost_center) (finops_budget_threshold)
            ) < 1.20
          for: 5m
          labels:
            severity: critical
            component: finops
            type: budget
          annotations:
            summary: "Budget Exceeded — {{ $labels.cost_center }} has reached 100% of monthly budget"
            description: |
              Cost center {{ $labels.cost_center }} has EXCEEDED its monthly budget.
              Utilization: {{ printf "%.1f" (mulf $value 100) }}%
              Immediate review required.
            runbook_url: "https://github.com/your-org/cicd-reference/blob/main/finops/docs/runbooks/investigate-cost-spike.md"
            dashboard_url: "{{ $externalURL }}/d/finops-budget-tracking?var-cost_center={{ $labels.cost_center }}"

        # ── Emergency: 120% of monthly budget ───────────────────────────────
        - alert: BudgetThresholdEmergency
          expr: |
            (
              sum by (cost_center) (finops_budget_current_spend)
              /
              sum by (cost_center) (finops_budget_threshold)
            ) >= 1.20
          for: 5m
          labels:
            severity: critical
            component: finops
            type: budget
            escalation: emergency
          annotations:
            summary: "EMERGENCY — {{ $labels.cost_center }} has exceeded 120% of monthly budget"
            description: |
              EMERGENCY: Cost center {{ $labels.cost_center }} is at {{ printf "%.1f" (mulf $value 100) }}% of budget.
              This indicates a runaway cost scenario. Immediate action required.
            runbook_url: "https://github.com/your-org/cicd-reference/blob/main/finops/docs/runbooks/investigate-cost-spike.md"
            dashboard_url: "{{ $externalURL }}/d/finops-budget-tracking?var-cost_center={{ $labels.cost_center }}"

        # ── Namespace approaching limit ──────────────────────────────────────
        - alert: NamespaceHighCost
          expr: |
            sum by (namespace, cost_center) (kubecost_namespace_cost_hourly) * 730
            > 5000
          for: 30m
          labels:
            severity: warning
            component: finops
            type: namespace-cost
          annotations:
            summary: "High monthly cost projected for namespace {{ $labels.namespace }}"
            description: |
              Namespace {{ $labels.namespace }} (cost center: {{ $labels.cost_center }}) is projected to cost
              ${{ printf "%.2f" $value }} this month based on current hourly spend.
            dashboard_url: "{{ $externalURL }}/d/finops-cost-overview?var-namespace={{ $labels.namespace }}"

        # ── Cost monitoring data stale ───────────────────────────────────────
        - alert: CostMonitoringDataStale
          expr: |
            (time() - max(kubecost_last_sync_timestamp)) > 21600
          for: 15m
          labels:
            severity: warning
            component: finops
            type: data-quality
          annotations:
            summary: "Cost monitoring data is stale (>6 hours old)"
            description: |
              Kubecost/OpenCost has not received fresh data in over 6 hours.
              Cost reports and alerts may be inaccurate.
              Check Kubecost/OpenCost connectivity to cloud provider billing APIs.
            runbook_url: "https://github.com/your-org/cicd-reference/blob/main/finops/docs/troubleshooting.md#cost-monitoring-data-stale"

# finops/prometheus/tag-compliance-alerts.yaml
# Prometheus alerting rules for cost tag compliance.
# Triggers when >5% of pods lack required finops.org labels.
#
# Apply: kubectl apply -f finops/prometheus/tag-compliance-alerts.yaml -n monitoring

apiVersion: monitoring.coreos.com/v1
kind: PrometheusRule
metadata:
  name: finops-tag-compliance-alerts
  namespace: monitoring
  labels:
    app: kube-prometheus-stack
    release: kube-prometheus-stack
    finops.org/component: tag-compliance
spec:
  groups:
    - name: finops.tag.compliance
      interval: 15m
      rules:
        # ── Missing cost center label ─────────────────────────────────────────
        - alert: CostTagComplianceLow
          expr: |
            (
              1 - (
                count(kube_pod_labels{label_finops_org_costcenter!=""})
                /
                count(kube_pod_info)
              )
            ) * 100 > 5
          for: 30m
          labels:
            severity: warning
            component: finops
            type: tag-compliance
          annotations:
            summary: "Cost tag compliance below 95% — {{ printf \"%.1f\" $value }}% of pods missing finops.org/costcenter"
            description: |
              {{ printf "%.1f" $value }}% of pods in the cluster are missing the required
              'finops.org/costcenter' label. This degrades chargeback reporting accuracy.

              Threshold: 5% non-compliance triggers this alert.
              Action: Run tag validation: kubectl exec -n finops deploy/finops-tools -- \
                python validate-cost-tags.py --all-namespaces

              See tagging schema: https://github.com/your-org/cicd-reference/blob/main/finops/docs/cost-tagging-schema.md
            dashboard_url: "{{ $externalURL }}/d/finops-tag-compliance"

        # ── Missing environment label ─────────────────────────────────────────
        - alert: EnvironmentTagComplianceLow
          expr: |
            (
              1 - (
                count(kube_pod_labels{label_finops_org_environment!=""})
                /
                count(kube_pod_info)
              )
            ) * 100 > 5
          for: 30m
          labels:
            severity: warning
            component: finops
            type: tag-compliance
          annotations:
            summary: "Environment tag compliance below 95% — {{ printf \"%.1f\" $value }}% missing finops.org/environment"
            description: |
              {{ printf "%.1f" $value }}% of pods are missing the 'finops.org/environment' label.
              Valid values: dev, staging, production.
            dashboard_url: "{{ $externalURL }}/d/finops-tag-compliance"

        # ── Per-namespace compliance warning ──────────────────────────────────
        - alert: NamespaceTagNonCompliant
          expr: |
            (
              1 - (
                sum by (namespace) (kube_pod_labels{label_finops_org_costcenter!=""})
                /
                sum by (namespace) (kube_pod_info)
              )
            ) * 100 > 20
          for: 15m
          labels:
            severity: warning
            component: finops
            type: tag-compliance
          annotations:
            summary: "Namespace {{ $labels.namespace }} has >20% pods missing cost labels"
            description: |
              Namespace {{ $labels.namespace }}: {{ printf "%.1f" $value }}% of pods are
              missing finops.org/costcenter labels. This namespace will appear as 'untagged'
              in cost reports.

# FinOps PR Review Checklist Template

Add this checklist to your GitHub PR template (.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md)
or GitLab MR template (.gitlab/merge_request_templates/FinOps.md)
whenever a PR includes infrastructure changes, new workloads, or Kubernetes manifests.

Usage: Copy the checklist section below into your PR description.

## FinOps Review Checklist

> Complete this checklist for PRs that add or modify Kubernetes workloads, Terraform infrastructure, or resource requests.

### Cost Labels ✅

- [ ] All new Pods/Deployments/StatefulSets have `finops.org/costcenter` label
- [ ] All new Pods/Deployments/StatefulSets have `finops.org/environment` label (dev/staging/production)
- [ ] Labels match an existing cost center in [`finops/config/budgets.yaml`](../finops/config/budgets.yaml)

### Resource Requests ✅

- [ ] CPU and memory `requests` and `limits` are explicitly set for all containers
- [ ] Resource requests are aligned with VPA recommendations (if available)
- [ ] No container requests more than 4 CPU cores or 8Gi memory without a PodDisruptionBudget
- [ ] GPU workloads have `finops.org/gpu-approved: "true"` annotation and supporting metadata

### Infrastructure Cost (Terraform changes only) ✅

- [ ] Infracost estimate has been reviewed in this PR's CI check
- [ ] Monthly cost increase is within the configured threshold (< 20% or < $500)
- [ ] If threshold is exceeded, approval from FinOps team has been obtained
- [ ] New cloud resources have appropriate cost allocation tags (AWS tags / Azure tags / GCP labels)

### VPA Recommendations (pre-production deployment) ✅

- [ ] VPA recommendations have been checked for affected workloads
- [ ] CPU/memory requests are within 20% of VPA target recommendations
- [ ] High-priority rightsizing opportunities (> 20% savings) have been addressed or deferred with justification

### Cost Impact Documentation ✅

- [ ] Estimated monthly cost impact is documented in the PR description
- [ ] Any significant cost increases (> $100/month) have a business justification
- [ ] Temporary or experimental workloads have a defined removal date
