# =============================================================================
# SLO Burn-Rate Alerts — api-gateway example
# Extends observability/prometheus/alerts/slo-rules.yaml using a separate file.
# =============================================================================
# Burn-rate thresholds (14.4, 6, 3, 1) are from the Google SRE Workbook
# multi-window burn-rate model and must not be changed.
#
# Tier durations are fixed to reduce flapping while preserving response value:
# - Tier 1 for: 2m    (short stabilization for immediate page)
# - Tier 2 for: 15m   (filters short-lived bursts)
# - Tier 3 for: 1h    (sustained degradation before ticket)
# - Tier 4 for: 3h    (trend-level warning only)

apiVersion: monitoring.coreos.com/v1
kind: PrometheusRule
metadata:
  name: slo-burn-rate-alerts-api-gateway
  namespace: monitoring
  labels:
    app: kube-prometheus-stack
    release: kube-prometheus-stack
    slo: "true"
spec:
  groups:
    - name: slo.api_gateway.availability.alerts
      rules:
        # Tier 1: burn rate >= 14.4 means error budget will be exhausted in ~2 hours.
        # Action: page immediately, open incident channel now.
        - alert: SLOBurnRateCritical
          expr: |
            slo:api_gateway:availability_burn_rate:1h >= 14.4
            and
            slo:api_gateway:availability_burn_rate:5m >= 14.4
          for: 2m
          labels:
            severity: critical
            team: platform
            slo: api-gateway-availability
          annotations:
            summary: "api-gateway availability burning budget at {{ $value | humanize }}x"
            description: |
              Tier 1 burn-rate alert for api-gateway availability.
              Budget exhaustion ETA is approximately 2 hours at this burn rate.
              Immediate action: page on-call and start incident response.
            runbook_url: "https://github.com/your-org/repo/blob/main/docs/runbooks/slo-breach-response.md" # <-- CHANGE THIS: set the runbook URL; valid value is an accessible runbook URL for this service.
            dashboard_url: "https://grafana.example.com/d/slo-api-gateway" # <-- CHANGE THIS: set the Grafana dashboard URL; valid value is your SLO dashboard URL.

        # Tier 2: burn rate >= 6 means error budget will be exhausted in ~5 days.
        # Action: page and investigate within 15 minutes.
        - alert: SLOBurnRateHigh
          expr: |
            slo:api_gateway:availability_burn_rate:6h >= 6
            and
            slo:api_gateway:availability_burn_rate:30m >= 6
          for: 15m
          labels:
            severity: critical
            team: platform
            slo: api-gateway-availability
          annotations:
            summary: "api-gateway availability burning budget at {{ $value | humanize }}x"
            description: |
              Tier 2 burn-rate alert for api-gateway availability.
              Budget exhaustion ETA is approximately 5 days at this burn rate.
              Immediate action: page on-call and begin mitigation within 15 minutes.
            runbook_url: "https://github.com/your-org/repo/blob/main/docs/runbooks/slo-breach-response.md" # <-- CHANGE THIS: set runbook URL for this service.
            dashboard_url: "https://grafana.example.com/d/slo-api-gateway" # <-- CHANGE THIS: set dashboard URL for this service.

        # Tier 3: burn rate >= 3 means error budget will be exhausted in ~10 days.
        # Action: create ticket and investigate within 1 hour.
        - alert: SLOBurnRateMedium
          expr: |
            slo:api_gateway:availability_burn_rate:24h >= 3
            and
            slo:api_gateway:availability_burn_rate:2h >= 3
          for: 1h
          labels:
            severity: warning
            team: platform
            slo: api-gateway-availability
          annotations:
            summary: "api-gateway availability burning budget at {{ $value | humanize }}x"
            description: |
              Tier 3 burn-rate alert for api-gateway availability.
              Budget exhaustion ETA is approximately 10 days at this burn rate.
              Action: create a reliability ticket and investigate within 1 hour.
            runbook_url: "https://github.com/your-org/repo/blob/main/docs/runbooks/slo-breach-response.md" # <-- CHANGE THIS: set runbook URL for this service.
            dashboard_url: "https://grafana.example.com/d/slo-api-gateway" # <-- CHANGE THIS: set dashboard URL for this service.

        # Tier 4: burn rate >= 1 means service is on track to miss month-end target.
        # Action: warning only, review in next standup and plan corrective work.
        - alert: SLOBurnRateLow
          expr: |
            slo:api_gateway:availability_burn_rate:72h >= 1
            and
            slo:api_gateway:availability_burn_rate:6h >= 1
          for: 3h
          labels:
            severity: info
            team: platform
            slo: api-gateway-availability
          annotations:
            summary: "api-gateway availability is on track to miss SLO"
            description: |
              Tier 4 warning for api-gateway availability.
              Burn rate indicates month-end SLO miss risk if trend continues.
              Action: review in standup and prioritize reliability fixes.
            runbook_url: "https://github.com/your-org/repo/blob/main/docs/runbooks/slo-breach-response.md" # <-- CHANGE THIS: set runbook URL for this service.
            dashboard_url: "https://grafana.example.com/d/slo-api-gateway" # <-- CHANGE THIS: set dashboard URL for this service.

        - alert: SLOErrorBudgetExhausted
          expr: slo:api_gateway:availability_error_budget_remaining:30d <= 0
          for: 5m
          labels:
            severity: critical
            team: platform
            slo: api-gateway-availability
          annotations:
            summary: "api-gateway availability error budget exhausted"
            description: "All monthly error budget is consumed. Every additional error is an SLO violation."
            runbook_url: "https://github.com/your-org/repo/blob/main/docs/runbooks/slo-breach-response.md" # <-- CHANGE THIS: set runbook URL for this service.
            dashboard_url: "https://grafana.example.com/d/slo-api-gateway" # <-- CHANGE THIS: set dashboard URL for this service.

    - name: slo.api_gateway.latency.alerts
      rules:
        - alert: SLOLatencyBurnRateCritical
          expr: |
            slo:api_gateway:latency_burn_rate:1h >= 14.4
            and
            slo:api_gateway:latency_burn_rate:5m >= 14.4
          for: 2m
          labels:
            severity: critical
            team: platform
            slo: api-gateway-latency
          annotations:
            summary: "api-gateway latency burning budget at {{ $value | humanize }}x"
            description: "Tier 1 latency burn. Budget exhaustion ETA is approximately 2 hours. Page immediately."
            runbook_url: "https://github.com/your-org/repo/blob/main/docs/runbooks/slo-breach-response.md" # <-- CHANGE THIS: set runbook URL for this service.
            dashboard_url: "https://grafana.example.com/d/slo-api-gateway" # <-- CHANGE THIS: set dashboard URL for this service.

        - alert: SLOLatencyBurnRateHigh
          expr: |
            slo:api_gateway:latency_burn_rate:6h >= 6
            and
            slo:api_gateway:latency_burn_rate:30m >= 6
          for: 15m
          labels:
            severity: critical
            team: platform
            slo: api-gateway-latency
          annotations:
            summary: "api-gateway latency burning budget at {{ $value | humanize }}x"
            description: "Tier 2 latency burn. Budget exhaustion ETA is approximately 5 days. Investigate within 15 minutes."
            runbook_url: "https://github.com/your-org/repo/blob/main/docs/runbooks/slo-breach-response.md" # <-- CHANGE THIS: set runbook URL for this service.
            dashboard_url: "https://grafana.example.com/d/slo-api-gateway" # <-- CHANGE THIS: set dashboard URL for this service.

        - alert: SLOLatencyBurnRateMedium
          expr: |
            slo:api_gateway:latency_burn_rate:24h >= 3
            and
            slo:api_gateway:latency_burn_rate:2h >= 3
          for: 1h
          labels:
            severity: warning
            team: platform
            slo: api-gateway-latency
          annotations:
            summary: "api-gateway latency burning budget at {{ $value | humanize }}x"
            description: "Tier 3 latency burn. Budget exhaustion ETA is approximately 10 days. File ticket and investigate within 1 hour."
            runbook_url: "https://github.com/your-org/repo/blob/main/docs/runbooks/slo-breach-response.md" # <-- CHANGE THIS: set runbook URL for this service.
            dashboard_url: "https://grafana.example.com/d/slo-api-gateway" # <-- CHANGE THIS: set dashboard URL for this service.

        - alert: SLOLatencyBurnRateLow
          expr: |
            slo:api_gateway:latency_burn_rate:72h >= 1
            and
            slo:api_gateway:latency_burn_rate:6h >= 1
          for: 3h
          labels:
            severity: info
            team: platform
            slo: api-gateway-latency
          annotations:
            summary: "api-gateway latency trend indicates month-end SLO miss risk"
            description: "Tier 4 latency warning. Burn trend indicates likely month-end SLO miss without corrective action."
            runbook_url: "https://github.com/your-org/repo/blob/main/docs/runbooks/slo-breach-response.md" # <-- CHANGE THIS: set runbook URL for this service.
            dashboard_url: "https://grafana.example.com/d/slo-api-gateway" # <-- CHANGE THIS: set dashboard URL for this service.

        - alert: SLOLatencyErrorBudgetExhausted
          expr: slo:api_gateway:latency_error_budget_remaining:30d <= 0
          for: 5m
          labels:
            severity: critical
            team: platform
            slo: api-gateway-latency
          annotations:
            summary: "api-gateway latency error budget exhausted"
            description: "All monthly latency error budget is consumed. Additional latency misses violate the SLO."
            runbook_url: "https://github.com/your-org/repo/blob/main/docs/runbooks/slo-breach-response.md" # <-- CHANGE THIS: set runbook URL for this service.
            dashboard_url: "https://grafana.example.com/d/slo-api-gateway" # <-- CHANGE THIS: set dashboard URL for this service.

---
# =============================================================================
# SLO Recording Rules and Multi-Window Multi-Burn-Rate Alerts
# =============================================================================
#
# TEMPLATE: WHEN TO USE
#   Copy this file for each service you want to hold to an SLO. Replace the
#   metric names, SLO targets, and labels marked # <-- CHANGE THIS.
#   Apply with: kubectl apply -f slo-rules.yaml
#
# APPROACH — Multi-Window Multi-Burn-Rate (Google SRE Workbook, Chapter 5)
#   Rather than alerting when errors exceed a simple threshold, these rules
#   track how quickly you are burning through your monthly error budget.
#   A burn rate of 1× means you will exhaust the budget in exactly 30 days.
#   A burn rate of 14.4× means you burn the full month's budget in 2 hours.
#
#   Each alert fires when BOTH a long window (trend) AND a short window
#   (confirmation) exceed the same burn-rate threshold. The dual window
#   suppresses false pages from momentary spikes and ensures slow-burn
#   degradation is caught before it silently drains the budget.
#
#   Threshold and window pairs used here (for a 99.9% availability SLO):
#   ┌───────────────┬───────────────┬──────────────┬────────────┬────────────┐
#   │ Alert name    │ Long window   │ Short window │ Burn rate  │ Severity   │
#   ├───────────────┼───────────────┼──────────────┼────────────┼────────────┤
#   │ SloFastBurn   │ 1h            │ 5m           │ 14.4×      │ critical   │
#   │ SloFastBurn   │ 6h            │ 30m          │ 6×         │ critical   │
#   │ SloSlowBurn   │ 1d            │ 2h           │ 3×         │ warning    │
#   │ SloSlowBurn   │ 3d            │ 6h           │ 1×         │ warning    │
#   └───────────────┴───────────────┴──────────────┴────────────┴────────────┘
#
# SLOTH / PYRRA COMPATIBILITY
#   If you adopt Sloth (https://sloth.dev) or Pyrra (https://github.com/pyrra-dev/pyrra)
#   to auto-generate these rules from a declarative SLO spec, you can delete this file
#   and replace it with a SLO Custom Resource. The recording rule naming used here
#   matches the Sloth output convention so migration is drop-in.
#
#   Example Sloth SLO spec (for reference — not applied by this file):
#
#     apiVersion: sloth.slok.dev/v1
#     kind: PrometheusServiceLevel
#     metadata:
#       name: my-service-availability
#       namespace: monitoring
#     spec:
#       service: "my-service"                     # <-- CHANGE THIS
#       slos:
#         - name: "requests-availability"
#           objective: 99.9                        # <-- CHANGE THIS
#           sli:
#             events:
#               errorQuery: >-
#                 sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="my-service",code=~"5.."}[{{.window}}]))
#               totalQuery: >-
#                 sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="my-service"}[{{.window}}]))
#           alerting:
#             name: MyServiceAvailability
#             annotations:
#               runbook_url: https://runbooks.example.com/myserviceavailability
#
# WHAT TO CHANGE:
#   1. Replace every `job="my-service"` with your actual Prometheus job label.
#   2. Replace `http_requests_total` with your service's request-counter metric.
#   3. Replace `code=~"5.."` with the error-selector for your metric.
#   4. Adjust the `slo_target` annotation on every alert (0.999 = 99.9%).
#   5. Update runbook_url to your real runbook location.
#   6. Clone the entire file for each additional service.
#
# PREREQUISITES:
#   - kube-prometheus-stack installed (observability/prometheus/values.yaml)
#   - Your service exposes a request counter with an error dimension
#     (e.g. http_requests_total{code=~"5.."} for HTTP, or a custom metric)
# =============================================================================

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Part 1 — Availability SLO: 99.9% of requests succeed
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# Error ratio = error requests / total requests.
# We record it at seven window widths because Prometheus cannot evaluate a
# rule like `rate(metric[6h])` inside a recording rule defined in the same group.
# Pre-computing these ratios makes the alert expressions instantaneous lookups.
#
apiVersion: monitoring.coreos.com/v1
kind: PrometheusRule
metadata:
  name: slo-availability-my-service           # <-- CHANGE THIS
  namespace: monitoring
  labels:
    # This label makes kube-prometheus-stack pick up this PrometheusRule automatically
    # (matches ruleSelector in observability/prometheus/values.yaml).
    app: kube-prometheus-stack
    release: kube-prometheus-stack
spec:
  groups:

    # ── Recording rules — error ratios over multiple windows ──────────────
    - name: slo:my-service:availability:ratio_rate  # <-- CHANGE THIS (service name)
      interval: 30s
      rules:

        # Note 1: The 5m and 30m windows are the "short" confirmation windows.
        # They are evaluated frequently (every 30s) to detect the start of a burn quickly.
        - record: slo:service_errors_total:ratio_rate5m
          expr: >-
            sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="my-service", code=~"5.."}[5m]))  # <-- CHANGE THIS
            /
            sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="my-service"}[5m]))               # <-- CHANGE THIS
          labels:
            service: my-service   # <-- CHANGE THIS: matches the job label above

        - record: slo:service_errors_total:ratio_rate30m
          expr: >-
            sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="my-service", code=~"5.."}[30m]))
            /
            sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="my-service"}[30m]))
          labels:
            service: my-service   # <-- CHANGE THIS

        # Note 2: The 1h and 6h windows are the primary "long" windows for fast burn detection.
        # 1h × 14.4× burn = 100% error budget consumed in 2 hours (page immediately).
        # 6h × 6× burn = budget consumed in 5 hours (page before half-day milestone).
        - record: slo:service_errors_total:ratio_rate1h
          expr: >-
            sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="my-service", code=~"5.."}[1h]))
            /
            sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="my-service"}[1h]))
          labels:
            service: my-service   # <-- CHANGE THIS

        - record: slo:service_errors_total:ratio_rate6h
          expr: >-
            sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="my-service", code=~"5.."}[6h]))
            /
            sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="my-service"}[6h]))
          labels:
            service: my-service   # <-- CHANGE THIS

        # Note 3: 2h and 1d windows drive the "warning" slow-burn alerts.
        # 1d × 3× burn = budget consumed in 10 days (ticket + investigate).
        - record: slo:service_errors_total:ratio_rate2h
          expr: >-
            sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="my-service", code=~"5.."}[2h]))
            /
            sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="my-service"}[2h]))
          labels:
            service: my-service   # <-- CHANGE THIS

        - record: slo:service_errors_total:ratio_rate1d
          expr: >-
            sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="my-service", code=~"5.."}[1d]))
            /
            sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="my-service"}[1d]))
          labels:
            service: my-service   # <-- CHANGE THIS

        # Note 4: The 3d window is the lowest-sensitivity check.
        # 3d × 1× burn = the service is right on the 30-day SLO boundary — ticket before it tips.
        - record: slo:service_errors_total:ratio_rate3d
          expr: >-
            sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="my-service", code=~"5.."}[3d]))
            /
            sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="my-service"}[3d]))
          labels:
            service: my-service   # <-- CHANGE THIS

    # ── Burn-rate alerts — four pairs covering the full burn-rate ladder ───
    - name: slo:my-service:availability:burnrate  # <-- CHANGE THIS
      rules:

        # ── CRITICAL: fast burn (14.4× over 1h, confirmed by 5m) ──────────
        # Note 5: This alert fires when the 1-hour error rate exceeds 14.4× the error budget.
        # For a 99.9% SLO: error_budget = 0.001; threshold = 14.4 × 0.001 = 0.0144.
        # It self-resets (no for: clause) because a 14.4× burn that stops is resolved.
        # The `and` operator requires BOTH windows to be over threshold — the 5m window
        # confirms the burn is ongoing and not a leftover artefact of a resolved spike.
        - alert: SloFastBurn
          expr: >-
            (
              slo:service_errors_total:ratio_rate1h{service="my-service"}  # <-- CHANGE THIS
              > (14.4 * (1 - 0.999))                                       # <-- CHANGE THIS: 1 - slo_target
            )
            and
            (
              slo:service_errors_total:ratio_rate5m{service="my-service"}  # <-- CHANGE THIS
              > (14.4 * (1 - 0.999))
            )
          labels:
            severity: critical
            service: my-service   # <-- CHANGE THIS
            slo: availability
          annotations:
            summary: "{{ $labels.service }}: high error rate burning budget at 14.4× (SLO: 99.9%)"
            description: >-
              The 1-hour error ratio for {{ $labels.service }} is {{ $value | humanizePercentage }},
              which exceeds 14.4× the allowed error budget. At this rate the full monthly error budget
              will be consumed in approximately 2 hours.
            slo_target: "0.999"                                                       # <-- CHANGE THIS
            burn_rate: "14.4"
            runbook_url: https://runbooks.example.com/slofastburn                     # <-- CHANGE THIS

        # ── CRITICAL: fast burn (6× over 6h, confirmed by 30m) ───────────
        # Note 6: This pair catches burns that started several hours ago but weren't caught
        # by the 14.4× threshold (e.g. a 7× burn that oscillates below 14.4×).
        # For a 99.9% SLO: threshold = 6 × 0.001 = 0.006.
        - alert: SloFastBurn
          expr: >-
            (
              slo:service_errors_total:ratio_rate6h{service="my-service"}  # <-- CHANGE THIS
              > (6 * (1 - 0.999))
            )
            and
            (
              slo:service_errors_total:ratio_rate30m{service="my-service"} # <-- CHANGE THIS
              > (6 * (1 - 0.999))
            )
          labels:
            severity: critical
            service: my-service   # <-- CHANGE THIS
            slo: availability
          annotations:
            summary: "{{ $labels.service }}: sustained error rate burning budget at 6× (SLO: 99.9%)"
            description: >-
              The 6-hour error ratio for {{ $labels.service }} is {{ $value | humanizePercentage }},
              exceeding 6× the allowed error budget. At this rate the monthly budget will be exhausted
              in approximately 5 hours.
            slo_target: "0.999"
            burn_rate: "6"
            runbook_url: https://runbooks.example.com/slofastburn   # <-- CHANGE THIS

        # ── WARNING: slow burn (3× over 1d, confirmed by 2h) ─────────────
        # Note 7: 3× burn does not warrant an immediate page but should generate a ticket.
        # At 3×, the budget is consumed in 10 days — enough time to schedule a fix,
        # but not enough to ignore until the next sprint cycle.
        - alert: SloSlowBurn
          expr: >-
            (
              slo:service_errors_total:ratio_rate1d{service="my-service"}  # <-- CHANGE THIS
              > (3 * (1 - 0.999))
            )
            and
            (
              slo:service_errors_total:ratio_rate2h{service="my-service"}  # <-- CHANGE THIS
              > (3 * (1 - 0.999))
            )
          labels:
            severity: warning
            service: my-service   # <-- CHANGE THIS
            slo: availability
          annotations:
            summary: "{{ $labels.service }}: error rate burning budget at 3× — create a ticket (SLO: 99.9%)"
            description: >-
              The 1-day error ratio for {{ $labels.service }} is {{ $value | humanizePercentage }},
              which is 3× the allowed error budget. If this rate persists the monthly budget will be
              fully consumed in approximately 10 days.
            slo_target: "0.999"
            burn_rate: "3"
            runbook_url: https://runbooks.example.com/sloslowburn   # <-- CHANGE THIS

        # ── WARNING: slow burn (1× over 3d, confirmed by 6h) ─────────────
        # Note 8: 1× burn means the service is exactly on the boundary of meeting its SLO.
        # Three days of sustained 1× burn consumes 10% of the monthly budget — still recoverable
        # but a signal that something in the environment needs attention.
        - alert: SloSlowBurn
          expr: >-
            (
              slo:service_errors_total:ratio_rate3d{service="my-service"}  # <-- CHANGE THIS
              > (1 * (1 - 0.999))
            )
            and
            (
              slo:service_errors_total:ratio_rate6h{service="my-service"}  # <-- CHANGE THIS
              > (1 * (1 - 0.999))
            )
          labels:
            severity: warning
            service: my-service   # <-- CHANGE THIS
            slo: availability
          annotations:
            summary: "{{ $labels.service }}: error rate matches budget burn rate exactly — review soon (SLO: 99.9%)"
            description: >-
              The 3-day error ratio for {{ $labels.service }} is {{ $value | humanizePercentage }},
              which is at the boundary of the allowed error budget. If unchanged over 30 days the
              SLO will be exactly missed.
            slo_target: "0.999"
            burn_rate: "1"
            runbook_url: https://runbooks.example.com/sloslowburn   # <-- CHANGE THIS

---
# =============================================================================
# Part 2 — Latency SLO: 99% of requests complete in under 500 ms
# =============================================================================
#
# Latency SLOs require a histogram metric (native histogram or classic _bucket).
# The error ratio here is: requests that exceeded the latency target / total requests.
# Replace `http_request_duration_seconds` with your histogram metric name.
# Replace `0.5` (500 ms) with your latency target in seconds.
#
# <-- CHANGE THIS: if your service does not expose a request-duration histogram,
# this entire section can be removed. Latency SLOs require histogram metrics.
#
apiVersion: monitoring.coreos.com/v1
kind: PrometheusRule
metadata:
  name: slo-latency-my-service   # <-- CHANGE THIS
  namespace: monitoring
  labels:
    app: kube-prometheus-stack
    release: kube-prometheus-stack
spec:
  groups:

    # ── Recording rules — latency "error" ratios (requests > target) ──────
    - name: slo:my-service:latency:ratio_rate   # <-- CHANGE THIS
      interval: 30s
      rules:

        # Note 9: For latency SLOs the "error" is a request that missed the target.
        # We compute: (requests exceeding the threshold) / (total requests).
        # With a classic histogram: requests that DID meet the target are in the ≤ bucket;
        # requests that missed are total minus that bucket.
        - record: slo:service_latency:ratio_rate5m
          expr: >-
            1 - (
              sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="my-service", le="0.5"}[5m]))  # <-- CHANGE THIS
              /
              sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_count{job="my-service"}[5m]))             # <-- CHANGE THIS
            )
          labels:
            service: my-service   # <-- CHANGE THIS
            slo: latency

        - record: slo:service_latency:ratio_rate30m
          expr: >-
            1 - (
              sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="my-service", le="0.5"}[30m]))
              /
              sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_count{job="my-service"}[30m]))
            )
          labels:
            service: my-service   # <-- CHANGE THIS
            slo: latency

        - record: slo:service_latency:ratio_rate1h
          expr: >-
            1 - (
              sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="my-service", le="0.5"}[1h]))
              /
              sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_count{job="my-service"}[1h]))
            )
          labels:
            service: my-service   # <-- CHANGE THIS
            slo: latency

        - record: slo:service_latency:ratio_rate6h
          expr: >-
            1 - (
              sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="my-service", le="0.5"}[6h]))
              /
              sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_count{job="my-service"}[6h]))
            )
          labels:
            service: my-service   # <-- CHANGE THIS
            slo: latency

        - record: slo:service_latency:ratio_rate1d
          expr: >-
            1 - (
              sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="my-service", le="0.5"}[1d]))
              /
              sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_count{job="my-service"}[1d]))
            )
          labels:
            service: my-service   # <-- CHANGE THIS
            slo: latency

        - record: slo:service_latency:ratio_rate3d
          expr: >-
            1 - (
              sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="my-service", le="0.5"}[3d]))
              /
              sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_count{job="my-service"}[3d]))
            )
          labels:
            service: my-service   # <-- CHANGE THIS
            slo: latency

    # ── Burn-rate alerts (99% latency SLO, error budget = 1%) ────────────
    - name: slo:my-service:latency:burnrate   # <-- CHANGE THIS
      rules:

        - alert: SloLatencyFastBurn
          # Note 10: Same multi-window logic as availability but targeting the latency ratio.
          # For a 99% SLO: error_budget = 0.01; 14.4× threshold = 0.144.
          expr: >-
            (
              slo:service_latency:ratio_rate1h{service="my-service", slo="latency"}   # <-- CHANGE THIS
              > (14.4 * (1 - 0.99))
            )
            and
            (
              slo:service_latency:ratio_rate5m{service="my-service", slo="latency"}   # <-- CHANGE THIS
              > (14.4 * (1 - 0.99))
            )
          labels:
            severity: critical
            service: my-service   # <-- CHANGE THIS
            slo: latency
          annotations:
            summary: "{{ $labels.service }}: high latency burning budget at 14.4× (SLO: 99% < 500ms)"
            description: >-
              The 1-hour slow-request ratio for {{ $labels.service }} is {{ $value | humanizePercentage }},
              exceeding 14.4× the allowed latency budget. At this rate the monthly budget will be
              consumed in approximately 2 hours.
            slo_target: "0.99"     # <-- CHANGE THIS
            burn_rate: "14.4"
            runbook_url: https://runbooks.example.com/slolatencyfastburn   # <-- CHANGE THIS

        - alert: SloLatencyFastBurn
          expr: >-
            (
              slo:service_latency:ratio_rate6h{service="my-service", slo="latency"}   # <-- CHANGE THIS
              > (6 * (1 - 0.99))
            )
            and
            (
              slo:service_latency:ratio_rate30m{service="my-service", slo="latency"}  # <-- CHANGE THIS
              > (6 * (1 - 0.99))
            )
          labels:
            severity: critical
            service: my-service   # <-- CHANGE THIS
            slo: latency
          annotations:
            summary: "{{ $labels.service }}: sustained latency burning budget at 6× (SLO: 99% < 500ms)"
            description: >-
              The 6-hour slow-request ratio for {{ $labels.service }} is {{ $value | humanizePercentage }},
              exceeding 6× the allowed latency budget.
            slo_target: "0.99"     # <-- CHANGE THIS
            burn_rate: "6"
            runbook_url: https://runbooks.example.com/slolatencyfastburn   # <-- CHANGE THIS

        - alert: SloLatencySlowBurn
          expr: >-
            (
              slo:service_latency:ratio_rate1d{service="my-service", slo="latency"}   # <-- CHANGE THIS
              > (3 * (1 - 0.99))
            )
            and
            (
              slo:service_latency:ratio_rate2h
              > (3 * (1 - 0.99))
            )
          labels:
            severity: warning
            service: my-service   # <-- CHANGE THIS
            slo: latency
          annotations:
            summary: "{{ $labels.service }}: latency burning budget at 3× — create a ticket (SLO: 99% < 500ms)"
            description: >-
              The 1-day slow-request ratio for {{ $labels.service }} is {{ $value | humanizePercentage }}.
              If this rate persists the monthly latency budget will be consumed in approximately 10 days.
            slo_target: "0.99"     # <-- CHANGE THIS
            burn_rate: "3"
            runbook_url: https://runbooks.example.com/slolatencyslowburn   # <-- CHANGE THIS

---
# ============================================================
# TEMPLATE: Prometheus - Fleet Aggregation Recording Rules
# WHEN TO USE: Aggregate per-cluster metrics into fleet-level views
# PREREQUISITES: cluster_name and environment labels present on scraped metrics
# SECRETS NEEDED: None
# WHAT TO CHANGE: Metric names and labels for your telemetry conventions
# RELATED FILES: observability/prometheus/values.yaml
# MATURITY: Beta
# ============================================================

apiVersion: monitoring.coreos.com/v1
kind: PrometheusRule
metadata:
  name: fleet-aggregation
  namespace: monitoring
spec:
  groups:
    - name: fleet.aggregate
      interval: 5m
      rules:
        - record: fleet:up:ratio
          expr: avg(up) by (cluster_name, environment)
          labels:
            fleet: "true"

        - record: fleet:pod_restart_rate:5m
          expr: sum(rate(kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total[5m])) by (cluster_name, namespace)

        - record: fleet:kyverno_violations:count
          expr: sum(kyverno_policy_results_total{result="fail"}) by (cluster_name, policy_name)

---
# ============================================================
# TEMPLATE: SLO Recording Rules — Burn Rates
# WHEN TO USE: Pre-compute SLO error ratios, burn rates, and error-budget remaining.
# MATURITY: Stable
# ============================================================
# Naming convention required in this repository:
#   slo:<service>:<metric>:<window>
# Example: slo:api_gateway:availability_error_ratio:1h
#
# Recording rules are mandatory. Do not compute multi-window ratios directly
# inside alert expressions. At fleet scale, direct multi-window expressions create
# O(n) query load per evaluation interval; recording rules reduce alerts to O(1)
# lookups and keep evaluation latency stable.

apiVersion: monitoring.coreos.com/v1
kind: PrometheusRule
metadata:
  name: slo-burn-rates-api-gateway
  namespace: monitoring
  labels:
    app: kube-prometheus-stack
    release: kube-prometheus-stack
    slo: "true"
spec:
  groups:
    - name: slo.api_gateway.availability.recording
      interval: 30s
      rules:
        - record: slo:api_gateway:good_requests_rate:5m
          expr: sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="api-gateway",status_code!~"5.."}[5m]))
        - record: slo:api_gateway:total_requests_rate:5m
          expr: sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="api-gateway"}[5m]))

        - record: slo:api_gateway:availability_error_ratio:1m
          expr: |
            sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="api-gateway",status_code=~"5.."}[1m]))
            /
            sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="api-gateway"}[1m]))
        - record: slo:api_gateway:availability_error_ratio:5m
          expr: |
            sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="api-gateway",status_code=~"5.."}[5m]))
            /
            sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="api-gateway"}[5m]))
        - record: slo:api_gateway:availability_error_ratio:30m
          expr: |
            sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="api-gateway",status_code=~"5.."}[30m]))
            /
            sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="api-gateway"}[30m]))
        - record: slo:api_gateway:availability_error_ratio:1h
          expr: |
            sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="api-gateway",status_code=~"5.."}[1h]))
            /
            sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="api-gateway"}[1h]))
        - record: slo:api_gateway:availability_error_ratio:2h
          expr: |
            sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="api-gateway",status_code=~"5.."}[2h]))
            /
            sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="api-gateway"}[2h]))
        - record: slo:api_gateway:availability_error_ratio:6h
          expr: |
            sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="api-gateway",status_code=~"5.."}[6h]))
            /
            sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="api-gateway"}[6h]))
        - record: slo:api_gateway:availability_error_ratio:24h
          expr: |
            sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="api-gateway",status_code=~"5.."}[24h]))
            /
            sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="api-gateway"}[24h]))
        - record: slo:api_gateway:availability_error_ratio:72h
          expr: |
            sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="api-gateway",status_code=~"5.."}[72h]))
            /
            sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="api-gateway"}[72h]))

        - record: slo:api_gateway:availability_error_budget_remaining:30d
          expr: |
            1 - (
              (
                sum(increase(http_requests_total{job="api-gateway",status_code=~"5.."}[30d]))
                /
                sum(increase(http_requests_total{job="api-gateway"}[30d]))
              )
              / (1 - 0.999)
            )

        - record: slo:api_gateway:availability_burn_rate:5m
          expr: slo:api_gateway:availability_error_ratio:5m / (1 - 0.999)
        - record: slo:api_gateway:availability_burn_rate:30m
          expr: slo:api_gateway:availability_error_ratio:30m / (1 - 0.999)
        - record: slo:api_gateway:availability_burn_rate:1h
          expr: slo:api_gateway:availability_error_ratio:1h / (1 - 0.999)
        - record: slo:api_gateway:availability_burn_rate:2h
          expr: slo:api_gateway:availability_error_ratio:2h / (1 - 0.999)
        - record: slo:api_gateway:availability_burn_rate:6h
          expr: slo:api_gateway:availability_error_ratio:6h / (1 - 0.999)
        - record: slo:api_gateway:availability_burn_rate:24h
          expr: slo:api_gateway:availability_error_ratio:24h / (1 - 0.999)
        - record: slo:api_gateway:availability_burn_rate:72h
          expr: slo:api_gateway:availability_error_ratio:72h / (1 - 0.999)

    - name: slo.api_gateway.latency.recording
      interval: 30s
      rules:
        - record: slo:api_gateway:latency_error_ratio:1m
          expr: |
            1 - (
              sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="api-gateway",le="0.5"}[1m]))
              /
              sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_count{job="api-gateway"}[1m]))
            )
        - record: slo:api_gateway:latency_error_ratio:5m
          expr: |
            1 - (
              sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="api-gateway",le="0.5"}[5m]))
              /
              sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_count{job="api-gateway"}[5m]))
            )
        - record: slo:api_gateway:latency_error_ratio:30m
          expr: |
            1 - (
              sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="api-gateway",le="0.5"}[30m]))
              /
              sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_count{job="api-gateway"}[30m]))
            )
        - record: slo:api_gateway:latency_error_ratio:1h
          expr: |
            1 - (
              sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="api-gateway",le="0.5"}[1h]))
              /
              sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_count{job="api-gateway"}[1h]))
            )
        - record: slo:api_gateway:latency_error_ratio:2h
          expr: |
            1 - (
              sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="api-gateway",le="0.5"}[2h]))
              /
              sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_count{job="api-gateway"}[2h]))
            )
        - record: slo:api_gateway:latency_error_ratio:6h
          expr: |
            1 - (
              sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="api-gateway",le="0.5"}[6h]))
              /
              sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_count{job="api-gateway"}[6h]))
            )
        - record: slo:api_gateway:latency_error_ratio:24h
          expr: |
            1 - (
              sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="api-gateway",le="0.5"}[24h]))
              /
              sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_count{job="api-gateway"}[24h]))
            )
        - record: slo:api_gateway:latency_error_ratio:72h
          expr: |
            1 - (
              sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="api-gateway",le="0.5"}[72h]))
              /
              sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_count{job="api-gateway"}[72h]))
            )

        - record: slo:api_gateway:latency_error_budget_remaining:30d
          expr: |
            1 - (
              (
                1 - (
                  sum(increase(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="api-gateway",le="0.5"}[30d]))
                  /
                  sum(increase(http_request_duration_seconds_count{job="api-gateway"}[30d]))
                )
              )
              / (1 - 0.99)
            )

        - record: slo:api_gateway:latency_burn_rate:5m
          expr: slo:api_gateway:latency_error_ratio:5m / (1 - 0.99)
        - record: slo:api_gateway:latency_burn_rate:30m
          expr: slo:api_gateway:latency_error_ratio:30m / (1 - 0.99)
        - record: slo:api_gateway:latency_burn_rate:1h
          expr: slo:api_gateway:latency_error_ratio:1h / (1 - 0.99)
        - record: slo:api_gateway:latency_burn_rate:2h
          expr: slo:api_gateway:latency_error_ratio:2h / (1 - 0.99)
        - record: slo:api_gateway:latency_burn_rate:6h
          expr: slo:api_gateway:latency_error_ratio:6h / (1 - 0.99)
        - record: slo:api_gateway:latency_burn_rate:24h
          expr: slo:api_gateway:latency_error_ratio:24h / (1 - 0.99)
        - record: slo:api_gateway:latency_burn_rate:72h
          expr: slo:api_gateway:latency_error_ratio:72h / (1 - 0.99)

# ============================================================
# TEMPLATE: Prometheus SLO — Availability
# WHEN TO USE: You want multi-window burn-rate alerting for
#   a request-success-rate SLO (i.e., fraction of non-5xx requests).
#
# SLO TARGET: 99.9% availability  (error budget = 43m 49s per 30 days)
#
# WHAT TO CHANGE:
#   - SLO_TARGET annotation (default: 0.999)     # <-- CHANGE THIS
#   - job label filter (default: "my-service")   # <-- CHANGE THIS
#   - namespace label in metadata                # <-- CHANGE THIS
#   - Burn-rate thresholds if SLO target changes # <-- CHANGE THIS
#
# RELATED FILES: observability/prometheus/slos/README.md
#                observability/prometheus/slos/latency-slo.yaml
#                observability/prometheus/alerts/slo-rules.yaml
# MATURITY: Stable
# ============================================================

# Note 1: PrometheusRule is a CRD provided by the Prometheus Operator
# (kube-prometheus-stack). It is automatically discovered by any Prometheus
# instance with the matching label selector.
apiVersion: monitoring.coreos.com/v1
kind: PrometheusRule
metadata:
  name: availability-slo                        # <-- CHANGE THIS: use your service name, e.g. payments-availability-slo
  namespace: monitoring                          # <-- CHANGE THIS: namespace where Prometheus Operator runs
  labels:
    # Note 2: The Prometheus Operator watches for PrometheusRule resources that
    # match the ruleSelector on the Prometheus CR. kube-prometheus-stack sets
    # this to `release: kube-prometheus-stack` by default.
    release: kube-prometheus-stack               # <-- CHANGE THIS: match your Prometheus Operator release name
    app: kube-prometheus-stack
  annotations:
    # Note 3: Document the SLO metadata in annotations for human reference.
    # These are not used by Prometheus but appear in alert notifications.
    SLO_TARGET: "0.999"                          # <-- CHANGE THIS: e.g. "0.995" for 99.5%
    SLO_WINDOW: "30d"
    SERVICE: "my-service"                        # <-- CHANGE THIS: your service name
spec:
  groups:

    # ── Recording Rules ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    # Note 4: Recording rules pre-compute the error ratio over multiple time windows.
    # This makes alert evaluation fast (single metric lookup instead of two-range joins)
    # and makes the values available in Grafana dashboards.
    #
    # The metric name convention `slo:sli_error:ratio_rate<window>` is used by
    # the standard SLO dashboards (Grafana ID 14348, Sloth, Pyrra).
    #
    # Formula: (5xx requests / total requests) over the window
    # "error" = any 5xx response (server-side fault, not client error)
    - name: availability-slo-recording
      interval: 30s                              # <-- CHANGE THIS: how often rules are evaluated
      rules:
        # Note 5: Each recording rule covers one of the burn-rate windows.
        # Having all windows pre-computed means alert rules do just a simple comparison,
        # keeping alert evaluation latency under 1 second.
        - record: slo:sli_error:ratio_rate5m
          expr: |
            sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="my-service", code=~"5.."}[5m]))  # <-- CHANGE THIS: job label and metric name
            /
            sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="my-service"}[5m]))               # <-- CHANGE THIS
          labels:
            slo: availability
            service: my-service                  # <-- CHANGE THIS

        - record: slo:sli_error:ratio_rate30m
          expr: |
            sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="my-service", code=~"5.."}[30m]))
            /
            sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="my-service"}[30m]))
          labels:
            slo: availability
            service: my-service                  # <-- CHANGE THIS

        - record: slo:sli_error:ratio_rate1h
          expr: |
            sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="my-service", code=~"5.."}[1h]))
            /
            sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="my-service"}[1h]))
          labels:
            slo: availability
            service: my-service

        - record: slo:sli_error:ratio_rate2h
          expr: |
            sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="my-service", code=~"5.."}[2h]))
            /
            sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="my-service"}[2h]))
          labels:
            slo: availability
            service: my-service

        - record: slo:sli_error:ratio_rate6h
          expr: |
            sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="my-service", code=~"5.."}[6h]))
            /
            sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="my-service"}[6h]))
          labels:
            slo: availability
            service: my-service

        - record: slo:sli_error:ratio_rate1d
          expr: |
            sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="my-service", code=~"5.."}[1d]))
            /
            sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="my-service"}[1d]))
          labels:
            slo: availability
            service: my-service

        - record: slo:sli_error:ratio_rate3d
          expr: |
            sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="my-service", code=~"5.."}[3d]))
            /
            sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="my-service"}[3d]))
          labels:
            slo: availability
            service: my-service

    # ── Alerting Rules ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    # Note 6: The three alert tiers implement the multi-window burn rate strategy
    # from the Google SRE Workbook. See observability/prometheus/slos/README.md
    # for the full explanation.
    #
    # Thresholds are derived from: burn_rate × (1 - SLO_TARGET)
    #   - 14× burn = (1 - 0.999) × 14 = 0.014  → exhausts budget in ~50h
    #   - 6×  burn = (1 - 0.999) × 6  = 0.006  → exhausts budget in ~5 days
    #   - 3×  burn = (1 - 0.999) × 3  = 0.003  → exhausts budget in ~10 days
    #
    # If you change SLO_TARGET you MUST recalculate these thresholds.        # <-- CHANGE THIS
    - name: availability-slo-alerts
      rules:

        # ── Critical: Fast Burn (page immediately) ─────────────────────
        # Note 7: Two-window condition: BOTH windows must exceed the threshold.
        # The short window (5m) catches the onset of the incident quickly.
        # The long window (1h) prevents alerting on a brief spike that will
        # self-resolve without exhausting significant budget.
        - alert: SLOAvailabilityFastBurnCritical
          expr: |
            (
              slo:sli_error:ratio_rate5m{service="my-service"} > (14 * (1 - 0.999))  # <-- CHANGE THIS: service label and SLO target
              and
              slo:sli_error:ratio_rate1h{service="my-service"} > (14 * (1 - 0.999))  # <-- CHANGE THIS
            )
          for: 2m
          labels:
            severity: critical
            slo: availability
            service: my-service                  # <-- CHANGE THIS
          annotations:
            summary: "SLO availability fast burn — critical ({{ $labels.service }})"
            description: >
              The error rate for {{ $labels.service }} is burning the availability error budget
              at 14× the acceptable rate. At this pace the entire 30-day budget will be
              exhausted in approximately 50 hours.
              Current 5m error ratio: {{ $value | humanizePercentage }}.
            runbook_url: "https://your-wiki.example.com/runbooks/slo-availability"  # <-- CHANGE THIS
            dashboard_url: "https://grafana.example.com/d/slo-availability"         # <-- CHANGE THIS

        # ── Warning: Medium Burn (ticket, investigate today) ───────────
        # Note 8: This tier catches burns that are fast enough to exhaust the budget
        # within 5 days but not fast enough to warrant an immediate page.
        # Use 6h + 3d windows to smooth out noise from normal traffic variance.
        - alert: SLOAvailabilityFastBurnWarning
          expr: |
            (
              slo:sli_error:ratio_rate30m{service="my-service"} > (6 * (1 - 0.999))  # <-- CHANGE THIS
              and
              slo:sli_error:ratio_rate6h{service="my-service"}  > (6 * (1 - 0.999))  # <-- CHANGE THIS
            )
          for: 15m
          labels:
            severity: warning
            slo: availability
            service: my-service                  # <-- CHANGE THIS
          annotations:
            summary: "SLO availability burn elevated — warning ({{ $labels.service }})"
            description: >
              The error rate for {{ $labels.service }} is burning the availability error budget
              at 6× the acceptable rate. At this pace the entire 30-day budget will be
              exhausted in approximately 5 days.
              Current 30m error ratio: {{ $value | humanizePercentage }}.
            runbook_url: "https://your-wiki.example.com/runbooks/slo-availability"  # <-- CHANGE THIS

        # ── Warning: Slow Burn (ticket, investigate this week) ─────────
        # Note 9: This tier catches a sustained low-level error rate that would
        # silently exhaust the error budget over 10+ days without any alert.
        # The very long windows (6h AND 3d) mean this alert only fires for
        # genuinely persistent issues, not transient deployments or restarts.
        - alert: SLOAvailabilitySlowBurnWarning
          expr: |
            (
              slo:sli_error:ratio_rate6h{service="my-service"} > (3 * (1 - 0.999))   # <-- CHANGE THIS
              and
              slo:sli_error:ratio_rate3d{service="my-service"} > (3 * (1 - 0.999))   # <-- CHANGE THIS
            )
          for: 1h
          labels:
            severity: warning
            slo: availability
            service: my-service                  # <-- CHANGE THIS
          annotations:
            summary: "SLO availability slow burn — warning ({{ $labels.service }})"
            description: >
              The error rate for {{ $labels.service }} has been burning the availability error
              budget at 3× the acceptable rate for over 6 hours. This is a sustained degradation.
              At this pace the 30-day error budget will be exhausted in approximately 10 days.
              Current 6h error ratio: {{ $value | humanizePercentage }}.
            runbook_url: "https://your-wiki.example.com/runbooks/slo-availability"  # <-- CHANGE THIS

# ============================================================
# TEMPLATE: Prometheus SLO — Latency
# WHEN TO USE: You want multi-window burn-rate alerting for
#   a request-latency SLO (fraction of requests below a threshold).
#
# SLO TARGET: 99% of requests complete in < 500ms
#
# WHAT TO CHANGE:
#   - SLO_TARGET annotation (default: 0.99)               # <-- CHANGE THIS
#   - LATENCY_THRESHOLD_SECONDS annotation (default: 0.5) # <-- CHANGE THIS
#   - job label filter (default: "my-service")            # <-- CHANGE THIS
#   - histogram bucket le value to match threshold        # <-- CHANGE THIS
#   - namespace label in metadata                         # <-- CHANGE THIS
#
# PREREQUISITES:
#   Your service must expose an http_request_duration_seconds histogram
#   with bucket boundaries that include your threshold.
#   Standard Prometheus client histograms include: .005, .01, .025, .05, .1,
#   .25, .5, 1, 2.5, 5, 10. For a 500ms SLO use le="0.5".
#   For a 200ms SLO use le="0.25" (closest bucket below 200ms).
#
# RELATED FILES: observability/prometheus/slos/README.md
#                observability/prometheus/slos/availability-slo.yaml
# MATURITY: Stable
# ============================================================

# Note 1: PrometheusRule is a CRD provided by the Prometheus Operator.
# Discovered automatically by Prometheus instances matching the label selector.
apiVersion: monitoring.coreos.com/v1
kind: PrometheusRule
metadata:
  name: latency-slo                              # <-- CHANGE THIS: use your service name, e.g. payments-latency-slo
  namespace: monitoring                          # <-- CHANGE THIS
  labels:
    release: kube-prometheus-stack               # <-- CHANGE THIS: match your Prometheus Operator release name
    app: kube-prometheus-stack
  annotations:
    SLO_TARGET: "0.99"                           # <-- CHANGE THIS: fraction of requests that must meet the latency target
    LATENCY_THRESHOLD_SECONDS: "0.5"             # <-- CHANGE THIS: P99 latency threshold in seconds
    SERVICE: "my-service"                        # <-- CHANGE THIS
spec:
  groups:

    # ── Recording Rules ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    # Note 2: Latency SLOs measure the fraction of requests BELOW a threshold,
    # using the histogram bucket for that threshold.
    #
    # Formula for the "good request" ratio:
    #   rate(histogram_bucket{le="0.5"}[window]) / rate(histogram_count[window])
    #
    # This is the inverse of the error ratio used in the availability SLO:
    #   error_ratio = 1 - good_ratio
    # We record the error ratio (1 - good) to keep the same direction as
    # the availability SLO and reuse the same burn-rate thresholds.
    - name: latency-slo-recording
      interval: 30s
      rules:
        # Note 3: `le="0.5"` selects the 500ms histogram bucket.
        # This bucket counts all requests that completed in ≤ 500ms.
        # Change `le` to match your latency threshold.       # <-- CHANGE THIS: le bucket
        - record: slo:sli_latency_error:ratio_rate5m
          expr: |
            1 - (
              sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="my-service", le="0.5"}[5m]))  # <-- CHANGE THIS: job and le
              /
              sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_count{job="my-service"}[5m]))              # <-- CHANGE THIS: job
            )
          labels:
            slo: latency
            service: my-service                  # <-- CHANGE THIS

        - record: slo:sli_latency_error:ratio_rate30m
          expr: |
            1 - (
              sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="my-service", le="0.5"}[30m]))
              /
              sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_count{job="my-service"}[30m]))
            )
          labels:
            slo: latency
            service: my-service

        - record: slo:sli_latency_error:ratio_rate1h
          expr: |
            1 - (
              sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="my-service", le="0.5"}[1h]))
              /
              sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_count{job="my-service"}[1h]))
            )
          labels:
            slo: latency
            service: my-service

        - record: slo:sli_latency_error:ratio_rate2h
          expr: |
            1 - (
              sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="my-service", le="0.5"}[2h]))
              /
              sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_count{job="my-service"}[2h]))
            )
          labels:
            slo: latency
            service: my-service

        - record: slo:sli_latency_error:ratio_rate6h
          expr: |
            1 - (
              sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="my-service", le="0.5"}[6h]))
              /
              sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_count{job="my-service"}[6h]))
            )
          labels:
            slo: latency
            service: my-service

        - record: slo:sli_latency_error:ratio_rate1d
          expr: |
            1 - (
              sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="my-service", le="0.5"}[1d]))
              /
              sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_count{job="my-service"}[1d]))
            )
          labels:
            slo: latency
            service: my-service

        - record: slo:sli_latency_error:ratio_rate3d
          expr: |
            1 - (
              sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="my-service", le="0.5"}[3d]))
              /
              sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_count{job="my-service"}[3d]))
            )
          labels:
            slo: latency
            service: my-service

    # ── Alerting Rules ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    # Note 4: Burn-rate thresholds for a 99% SLO differ from a 99.9% SLO
    # because the error budget is larger (1% vs 0.1%).
    #
    # Thresholds: burn_rate × (1 - 0.99) = burn_rate × 0.01
    #   - 14× burn = 0.14  → exhausts budget in ~50h
    #   - 6×  burn = 0.06  → exhausts budget in ~5 days
    #   - 3×  burn = 0.03  → exhausts budget in ~10 days
    #                                                # <-- CHANGE THIS if SLO_TARGET changes
    - name: latency-slo-alerts
      rules:

        # ── Critical: Fast Burn (page immediately) ─────────────────────
        # Note 5: Two-window condition prevents false positives from brief spikes.
        # At 14× burn rate, 50h of error budget will be consumed — page immediately.
        - alert: SLOLatencyFastBurnCritical
          expr: |
            (
              slo:sli_latency_error:ratio_rate5m{service="my-service"}  > (14 * (1 - 0.99))  # <-- CHANGE THIS: service and SLO target
              and
              slo:sli_latency_error:ratio_rate1h{service="my-service"}  > (14 * (1 - 0.99))  # <-- CHANGE THIS
            )
          for: 2m
          labels:
            severity: critical
            slo: latency
            service: my-service                  # <-- CHANGE THIS
          annotations:
            summary: "SLO latency fast burn — critical ({{ $labels.service }})"
            description: >
              P99 latency for {{ $labels.service }} is burning the latency error budget
              at 14× the acceptable rate. The threshold is 500ms.              # <-- CHANGE THIS: threshold in message
              At this pace the entire 30-day budget will be exhausted in approximately 50 hours.
              Current 5m latency error ratio: {{ $value | humanizePercentage }}.
            runbook_url: "https://your-wiki.example.com/runbooks/slo-latency"  # <-- CHANGE THIS
            dashboard_url: "https://grafana.example.com/d/slo-latency"         # <-- CHANGE THIS

        # ── Warning: Medium Burn (ticket, investigate today) ───────────
        - alert: SLOLatencyFastBurnWarning
          expr: |
            (
              slo:sli_latency_error:ratio_rate30m{service="my-service"} > (6 * (1 - 0.99))   # <-- CHANGE THIS
              and
              slo:sli_latency_error:ratio_rate6h{service="my-service"}  > (6 * (1 - 0.99))   # <-- CHANGE THIS
            )
          for: 15m
          labels:
            severity: warning
            slo: latency
            service: my-service                  # <-- CHANGE THIS
          annotations:
            summary: "SLO latency burn elevated — warning ({{ $labels.service }})"
            description: >
              P99 latency for {{ $labels.service }} is burning the latency error budget
              at 6× the acceptable rate (threshold: 500ms).                   # <-- CHANGE THIS: threshold in message
              At this pace the entire 30-day budget will be exhausted in approximately 5 days.
              Current 30m latency error ratio: {{ $value | humanizePercentage }}.
            runbook_url: "https://your-wiki.example.com/runbooks/slo-latency"  # <-- CHANGE THIS

        # ── Warning: Slow Burn (ticket, investigate this week) ─────────
        # Note 6: Slow burn for latency often indicates a gradual database or
        # downstream service degradation. The 6h+3d windows confirm it is
        # a sustained trend, not a temporary deployment artifact.
        - alert: SLOLatencySlowBurnWarning
          expr: |
            (
              slo:sli_latency_error:ratio_rate6h{service="my-service"} > (3 * (1 - 0.99))    # <-- CHANGE THIS
              and
              slo:sli_latency_error:ratio_rate3d{service="my-service"} > (3 * (1 - 0.99))    # <-- CHANGE THIS
            )
          for: 1h
          labels:
            severity: warning
            slo: latency
            service: my-service                  # <-- CHANGE THIS
          annotations:
            summary: "SLO latency slow burn — warning ({{ $labels.service }})"
            description: >
              P99 latency for {{ $labels.service }} has been above the 500ms threshold # <-- CHANGE THIS: threshold
              at 3× the acceptable error rate for over 6 hours. Sustained degradation detected.
              At this pace the 30-day error budget will be exhausted in approximately 10 days.
              Current 6h latency error ratio: {{ $value | humanizePercentage }}.
            runbook_url: "https://your-wiki.example.com/runbooks/slo-latency"  # <-- CHANGE THIS

apiVersion: slo/v1
kind: ServiceLevelObjective
metadata:
  name: api-gateway-availability
  service: api-gateway
  namespace: production # <-- CHANGE THIS: set workload namespace; valid values are your Kubernetes namespaces from overlays.
  team: platform # <-- CHANGE THIS: set owning team label; valid values are team labels used on Deployments.
  owner: platform-oncall@example.com # <-- CHANGE THIS: set on-call contact email or PagerDuty identifier; source from team roster.
  runbook_url: https://github.com/your-org/repo/blob/main/docs/runbooks/slo-breach-response.md # <-- CHANGE THIS: set runbook URL for this service; source docs/runbooks/.

spec:
  type: availability
  target: 99.9 # <-- CHANGE THIS: set availability target; valid values usually 99.0 to 99.95 based on baseline.
  window: 30d # <-- CHANGE THIS: set to 7d while baseline is unknown, then 30d.

  good_events:
    metric: http_requests_total
    filters:
      job: api-gateway # <-- CHANGE THIS: must match Prometheus job label from scrape config.
      status_code: "2xx|3xx" # <-- CHANGE THIS: define success codes; valid regex depends on service contract.

  total_events:
    metric: http_requests_total
    filters:
      job: api-gateway # <-- CHANGE THIS: must match Prometheus job label.

  compliance:
    soc2_controls: ["CC7.2", "CC7.4"]
    review_cadence: quarterly

---
# ============================================================
# TEMPLATE: Service SLO Definition Example — Latency
# WHEN TO USE: Copy and adapt for request-latency SLOs.
# MATURITY: Stable
# ============================================================
# Why histogram buckets (_bucket) and not summary percentiles (_p99):
# - Histogram buckets are aggregatable across pods and instances.
# - Summary quantiles are pre-aggregated at scrape target scope and cannot be
#   merged correctly across replicas.
# - Burn-rate math requires consistent good/total event counting, which buckets provide.
#
# Choosing the le threshold:
# - Set threshold to your measured p95 baseline first, not an aspirational number.
# - Example: if observed p95 is 420ms, start with le="0.5" then improve over time.
# - Review threshold quarterly with service and product stakeholders.
#
# Pod-level vs ingress-level latency:
# - Pod-level metrics isolate application and dependency behavior.
# - Ingress-level metrics include network and edge behavior seen by users.
# - For user-facing SLOs, prefer ingress-level metrics when available; for
#   service-internal SLOs, pod-level is acceptable.

apiVersion: slo/v1
kind: ServiceLevelObjective
metadata:
  name: api-gateway-latency
  service: api-gateway
  namespace: production # <-- CHANGE THIS: set workload namespace; valid values are namespace names in Kubernetes overlays.
  team: platform # <-- CHANGE THIS: set owning team label; valid values match team labels in Deployment metadata.
  owner: platform-oncall@example.com # <-- CHANGE THIS: set owner email or PagerDuty identifier; source from team on-call roster.
  runbook_url: https://github.com/your-org/repo/blob/main/docs/runbooks/slo-breach-response.md # <-- CHANGE THIS: set service runbook URL.

spec:
  type: latency
  target: 99.0 # <-- CHANGE THIS: set latency success target; valid values usually 95.0 to 99.9 based on baseline and business need.
  window: 30d # <-- CHANGE THIS: use 7d for new services, then 30d after baseline stabilizes.

  good_events:
    metric: http_request_duration_seconds_bucket
    filters:
      job: api-gateway # <-- CHANGE THIS: set Prometheus job label for this service.
      le: "0.5" # <-- CHANGE THIS: set latency objective bucket in seconds; valid values must exist in your histogram buckets.

  total_events:
    metric: http_request_duration_seconds_count
    filters:
      job: api-gateway # <-- CHANGE THIS: set the same job label used in good_events.

  compliance:
    soc2_controls: ["CC7.2", "CC7.4"]
    review_cadence: quarterly

# ============================================================
# SLO Definition Schema
# Copy this file to observability/prometheus/slos/<your-service>-slo.yaml
# Then run: make slo-generate SERVICE=<your-service>
# This generates the recording rules and alert rules for your SLO.
# MATURITY: Stable
# WHEN TO USE: Any service that needs a reliability target and alerting
# ============================================================
# Common mistakes teams make:
# 1) Setting the target too high without a business need (for example 99.99%)
#    creates alert fatigue and unsustainable on-call load.
# 2) Using the wrong total-events metric (for example counting only 5xx as total)
#    hides real user-impacting failures like timeouts or policy-driven failures.
# 3) Starting with a 30d window before measuring a baseline leads to immediate
#    SLO violations; start with 7d, measure, then move to 30d.

apiVersion: slo/v1
kind: ServiceLevelObjective
metadata:
  name: my-service-availability
  service: my-service
  namespace: production
  team: platform
  owner: platform-team@example.com # <-- CHANGE THIS: set to team email or PagerDuty service key; valid values are RFC5322 emails or PD integration identifiers; source from team on-call ownership docs.
  runbook_url: https://github.com/your-org/repo/blob/main/docs/runbooks/my-service.md # <-- CHANGE THIS: set to the service runbook URL; valid value is a reachable markdown runbook URL; source from docs/runbooks/.

spec:
  # SLO type: availability | latency | throughput | error-rate
  type: availability

  # The reliability target.
  # 99.9% = 43.8 minutes/month downtime budget
  # 99.5% = 3.6 hours/month downtime budget
  # 99.0% = 7.3 hours/month downtime budget
  # Guardrail: do not set above measured baseline.
  target: 99.9

  # 30d is standard after baseline is proven.
  # Use 7d first for new services.
  window: 30d

  good_events:
    metric: http_requests_total
    filters:
      job: my-service # <-- CHANGE THIS: must match Prometheus job label; valid value is the exact job label from Prometheus target discovery.
      status_code: "2xx" # <-- CHANGE THIS: set success criteria; valid values include regex classes like 2xx or service-specific success labels.

  total_events:
    metric: http_requests_total
    filters:
      job: my-service # <-- CHANGE THIS: must match Prometheus job label; valid value is exact job label from Prometheus.

  # Optional alert routing overrides.
  # alerts:
  #   critical:
  #     pagerduty_service: PXXXXXX # <-- CHANGE THIS: set team PagerDuty service id; valid value is PD service id (for example P123ABC); source PagerDuty service settings.
  #   warning:
  #     slack_channel: "#my-team-alerts" # <-- CHANGE THIS: set team Slack channel; valid value is #channel-name.

  compliance:
    soc2_controls: ["CC7.2", "CC7.4"]
    review_cadence: quarterly

# kube-prometheus-stack values for chart 55.x
# Production teams should layer environment-specific overrides on top of this file
# instead of editing shared defaults directly.

prometheus:
  prometheusSpec:
    retention: 30d # Keeps one month of metrics for trend analysis and incident review.
    scrapeInterval: 30s # Matches the health check intervals in base deployment closely enough without oversampling them.
    evaluationInterval: 30s
    serviceMonitorSelectorNilUsesHelmValues: false # Allows ServiceMonitors outside the chart's namespace and release labels to be discovered.
    serviceMonitorSelector: {}
    serviceMonitorNamespaceSelector: {}
    podMonitorSelectorNilUsesHelmValues: false
    podMonitorSelector: {}
    podMonitorNamespaceSelector: {}
    ruleSelectorNilUsesHelmValues: false # Lets Prometheus pick up PrometheusRule resources managed outside the Helm release.
    ruleSelector: {}
    ruleNamespaceSelector: {}
    resources:
      requests:
        cpu: 500m
        memory: 2Gi
      limits:
        cpu: "2"
        memory: 6Gi
    storageSpec:
      volumeClaimTemplate:
        spec:
          accessModes:
            - ReadWriteOnce
          resources:
            requests:
              storage: 50Gi # Sized for 30 days of cluster plus app metrics in a small-to-mid production cluster.
    # Discover Services that explicitly opt in with monitoring: "true".
    additionalScrapeConfigs:
      - job_name: kubernetes-service-endpoints-opt-in
        kubernetes_sd_configs:
          - role: endpoints
        relabel_configs:
          - source_labels:
              - __meta_kubernetes_service_label_monitoring
            action: keep
            regex: "true"
          - source_labels:
              - __meta_kubernetes_service_annotation_prometheus_io_scheme
            action: replace
            regex: (https?)
            target_label: __scheme__
          - source_labels:
              - __meta_kubernetes_service_annotation_prometheus_io_path
            action: replace
            regex: (.+)
            target_label: __metrics_path__
          - source_labels:
              - __address__
              - __meta_kubernetes_service_annotation_prometheus_io_port
            action: replace
            regex: ([^:]+)(?::\d+)?;(\d+)
            replacement: $1:$2
            target_label: __address__
          - action: labelmap
            regex: __meta_kubernetes_service_label_(.+)
          - source_labels:
              - __meta_kubernetes_namespace
            target_label: namespace
          - source_labels:
              - __meta_kubernetes_service_name
            target_label: service

    # Common production additions teams often enable later:
    # thanos:
    #   objectStorageConfig:
    #     existingSecret:
    #       name: thanos-objstore-config # <-- CHANGE THIS
    #       key: objstore.yml
    # remoteWrite:
    #   - url: https://remote-write.example.com/api/v1/write # <-- CHANGE THIS
    #     basicAuth:
    #       username:
    #         name: remote-write-auth # <-- CHANGE THIS
    #         key: username
    #       password:
    #         name: remote-write-auth # <-- CHANGE THIS
    #         key: password

alertmanager:
  enabled: true
  alertmanagerSpec:
    replicas: 2
    retention: 120h
    additionalArgs:
      - --config.expand-env
    # Source these credentials from Kubernetes Secrets or an external secret controller.
    # See docs/guides/secrets-management.md for the recommended secret-management patterns.
    containers:
      - name: alertmanager
        env:
          - name: SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL
            valueFrom:
              secretKeyRef:
                name: observability-alertmanager-secrets # <-- CHANGE THIS
                key: slack-webhook-url
          - name: PAGERDUTY_KEY
            valueFrom:
              secretKeyRef:
                name: observability-alertmanager-secrets # <-- CHANGE THIS
                key: pagerduty-key
    resources:
      requests:
        cpu: 200m
        memory: 512Mi
      limits:
        cpu: 1
        memory: 1Gi
  config:
    global:
      resolve_timeout: 5m
    route:
      receiver: slack-warnings
      group_by:
        - alertname
        - namespace
        - severity
      group_wait: 30s
      group_interval: 5m
      repeat_interval: 4h
      routes:
        - receiver: pagerduty-critical
          matchers:
            - severity="critical"
        - receiver: slack-warnings
          matchers:
            - severity="warning"
    receivers:
      - name: slack-warnings
        slack_configs:
          - api_url: ${SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL}
            channel: "#platform-alerts" # <-- CHANGE THIS
            send_resolved: true
            title: >-
              [{{ .Status | toUpper }}] {{ .CommonLabels.alertname }} in {{ .CommonLabels.namespace }}
            text: >-
              {{ range .Alerts -}}
              *Summary:* {{ .Annotations.summary }}
              *Description:* {{ .Annotations.description }}
              *Severity:* {{ .Labels.severity }}
              *Runbook:* {{ .Annotations.runbook_url }}
              {{ end }}
      - name: pagerduty-critical
        pagerduty_configs:
          - routing_key: ${PAGERDUTY_KEY}
            send_resolved: true
            severity: "{{ .CommonLabels.severity }}"
            description: >-
              {{ .CommonLabels.alertname }} in {{ .CommonLabels.namespace }}
            client: Alertmanager
            client_url: http://alertmanager-operated.monitoring.svc:9093 # <-- CHANGE THIS
            details:
              summary: "{{ .CommonAnnotations.summary }}"
              description: "{{ .CommonAnnotations.description }}"
              namespace: "{{ .CommonLabels.namespace }}"
              alertname: "{{ .CommonLabels.alertname }}"

grafana:
  enabled: true
  defaultDashboardsEnabled: true
  admin:
    existingSecret: grafana-admin-credentials # <-- CHANGE THIS
    userKey: admin-user
    passwordKey: admin-password
  persistence:
    enabled: true
    accessModes:
      - ReadWriteOnce
    size: 10Gi # Enough room for dashboards, plugins, and retained Grafana state without over-allocating by default.
  ingress:
    enabled: true
    ingressClassName: nginx
    hosts:
      - grafana.example.com # <-- CHANGE THIS
    path: /
    pathType: Prefix
  sidecar:
    dashboards:
      enabled: true
      searchNamespace: ALL
      label: grafana_dashboard
      labelValue: "1"
  resources:
    requests:
      cpu: 100m
      memory: 256Mi
    limits:
      cpu: 500m
      memory: 1Gi
