# Promtail DaemonSet - Kubernetes Audit Log Shipper
# Requirements: 3.6, 3.7, 3.8, 19.1–19.8
#
# Ships Kubernetes API server audit logs to Loki for security analysis.
# Runs as a DaemonSet on control plane nodes only (where audit logs are written).
#
# Pre-requisites:
#   - Loki installed (see observability/loki/values.yaml for endpoint)
#   - Kubernetes API server configured with:
#       --audit-policy-file=/etc/kubernetes/audit-policy.yaml
#       --audit-log-path=/var/log/kubernetes/audit/audit.log
#       --audit-log-maxage=30
#       --audit-log-maxbackup=10
#       --audit-log-maxsize=100
#
# Deploy:
#   kubectl apply -f secops/runtime/audit-logging/loki-shipper.yaml
#
# Verify:
#   kubectl get pods -n secops -l app=promtail-audit
#   kubectl logs -n secops -l app=promtail-audit --tail=20

---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: secops
  labels:
    app.kubernetes.io/managed-by: secops
    pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce: privileged

---
# ServiceAccount for Promtail
# Requirements: 19.1
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: promtail-audit
  namespace: secops
  labels:
    app: promtail-audit
    component: audit-log-shipper

---
# ClusterRole for Promtail to read pod metadata for log enrichment
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: ClusterRole
metadata:
  name: promtail-audit
  labels:
    app: promtail-audit
rules:
  - apiGroups: [""]
    resources:
      - nodes
      - nodes/proxy
      - services
      - endpoints
      - pods
    verbs: ["get", "watch", "list"]

---
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: ClusterRoleBinding
metadata:
  name: promtail-audit
  labels:
    app: promtail-audit
subjects:
  - kind: ServiceAccount
    name: promtail-audit
    namespace: secops
roleRef:
  kind: ClusterRole
  name: promtail-audit
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io

---
# Promtail ConfigMap
# Defines scrape configs for Kubernetes API server audit logs
# Requirements: 19.3 (read audit log path), 19.4 (parse JSON), 19.5 (add labels), 19.6 (Loki endpoint)
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: promtail-audit-config
  namespace: secops
  labels:
    app: promtail-audit
data:
  promtail.yaml: |
    server:
      http_listen_port: 9080
      grpc_listen_port: 0

    positions:
      # Position file tracks progress through audit log file
      # Stored on host to survive pod restarts
      filename: /run/promtail/positions.yaml

    clients:
      # Loki endpoint - sourced from observability/loki/values.yaml
      # Requirement 19.6
      - url: http://loki-gateway.observability.svc.cluster.local/loki/api/v1/push
        # Batch settings for efficient log shipping
        batchwait: 1s
        batchsize: 1048576  # 1 MiB
        timeout: 10s
        # Retry during Loki unavailability (Requirement 19.7)
        backoff_config:
          min_period: 500ms
          max_period: 5m
          max_retries: 10
        # Authentication (if Loki requires auth)
        # tenant_id: secops
        # basic_auth:
        #   username: loki
        #   password_file: /var/secrets/loki-password

    scrape_configs:
      # Kubernetes API Server Audit Logs
      # Requirement 19.2, 19.3
      - job_name: kubernetes-audit
        static_configs:
          - targets:
              - localhost
            labels:
              # Static labels added to all audit log entries
              # Requirement 19.5
              job: kubernetes-audit
              source: k8s-audit                    # Log source identifier
              cluster: ${CLUSTER_NAME}             # Set via env var (see DaemonSet spec)
              environment: ${ENVIRONMENT}          # Set via env var (see DaemonSet spec)
              __path__: /var/log/kubernetes/audit/audit.log

        # JSON log parsing for Kubernetes audit events
        # Requirement 19.4
        pipeline_stages:
          # Parse the JSON audit event
          - json:
              expressions:
                # Extract key fields from audit log JSON for label indexing
                verb: verb
                resource: 'objectRef.resource'
                namespace: 'objectRef.namespace'
                user: 'user.username'
                response_code: 'responseStatus.code'
                audit_level: level
                stage: stage
                request_uri: requestURI

          # Create Loki labels from extracted JSON fields
          # Keep label cardinality low for Loki performance
          - labels:
              verb:           # HTTP verb (get, create, update, patch, delete)
              resource:       # Kubernetes resource type (pods, secrets, etc.)
              namespace:      # Kubernetes namespace (for namespace-scoped resources)
              audit_level:    # Audit level (Metadata, Request, RequestResponse)

          # Extract timestamp from audit event for accurate log ordering
          - timestamp:
              source: requestReceivedTimestamp
              format: RFC3339Nano
              action_on_failure: skip

          # Drop RequestReceived stage logs (duplicate - ResponseComplete has more data)
          - drop:
              expression: '\"stage\":\"RequestReceived\"'
              drop_counter_reason: request_received_stage

          # Metrics for monitoring log shipping health
          - metrics:
              audit_logs_total:
                type: Counter
                description: Total audit log lines shipped
                prefix: promtail_audit_
                source: verb
                config:
                  action: inc

---
# Promtail DaemonSet - runs on control plane nodes only
# Requirements: 19.1 (DaemonSet), 19.2 (control plane nodes), 19.8 (resource limits)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: DaemonSet
metadata:
  name: promtail-audit
  namespace: secops
  labels:
    app: promtail-audit
    component: audit-log-shipper
    version: "2.9.0"
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: promtail-audit
  updateStrategy:
    type: RollingUpdate
    rollingUpdate:
      maxUnavailable: 1
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: promtail-audit
        component: audit-log-shipper
      annotations:
        prometheus.io/scrape: "true"
        prometheus.io/port: "9080"
        prometheus.io/path: "/metrics"
    spec:
      serviceAccountName: promtail-audit

      # Run ONLY on control plane nodes where audit logs are written
      # Requirement 19.2
      nodeSelector:
        node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane: ""

      tolerations:
        # Control plane nodes are typically tainted - tolerate to schedule there
        - key: node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane
          operator: Exists
          effect: NoSchedule
        - key: node-role.kubernetes.io/master
          operator: Exists
          effect: NoSchedule

      # Ensure only one pod at a time is rescheduled during updates
      terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 30

      containers:
        - name: promtail
          image: grafana/promtail:2.9.0
          args:
            - -config.file=/etc/promtail/promtail.yaml
            - -config.expand-env=true  # Enable environment variable substitution

          env:
            # Cluster and environment labels for log enrichment
            # Override these when deploying to specific clusters
            - name: CLUSTER_NAME
              valueFrom:
                fieldRef:
                  fieldPath: spec.nodeName  # Fallback to node name
            - name: ENVIRONMENT
              value: "production"  # Override via kustomize/helm values

            # Node name for local log path discovery
            - name: NODE_NAME
              valueFrom:
                fieldRef:
                  fieldPath: spec.nodeName

          # Resource requirements (Requirement 19.8)
          resources:
            requests:
              cpu: 50m
              memory: 64Mi
            limits:
              cpu: 200m
              memory: 256Mi

          ports:
            - name: http-metrics
              containerPort: 9080
              protocol: TCP

          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /ready
              port: http-metrics
            initialDelaySeconds: 10
            periodSeconds: 10

          livenessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /ready
              port: http-metrics
            initialDelaySeconds: 30
            periodSeconds: 30

          securityContext:
            readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
            runAsGroup: 0        # Run as root to read audit log files
            runAsUser: 0         # Audit logs typically require root read access
            allowPrivilegeEscalation: false

          volumeMounts:
            # Promtail configuration
            - name: config
              mountPath: /etc/promtail

            # Audit log file from host filesystem
            # Requirement 19.3
            - name: audit-log
              mountPath: /var/log/kubernetes/audit
              readOnly: true

            # Position tracking file (survives pod restarts)
            # Requirement 19.7 - local buffering via position tracking
            - name: positions
              mountPath: /run/promtail

      volumes:
        # Promtail configuration from ConfigMap
        - name: config
          configMap:
            name: promtail-audit-config

        # Host audit log directory (read-only)
        # Kubernetes API server writes audit logs here
        - name: audit-log
          hostPath:
            path: /var/log/kubernetes/audit
            type: DirectoryOrCreate

        # Position file storage (survives pod restarts for resume capability)
        # Requirement 19.7 - buffer during unavailability via position tracking
        - name: positions
          hostPath:
            path: /run/promtail-audit
            type: DirectoryOrCreate

---
# Service for Prometheus scraping of Promtail metrics
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: promtail-audit
  namespace: secops
  labels:
    app: promtail-audit
    monitoring: "true"
spec:
  selector:
    app: promtail-audit
  ports:
    - name: http-metrics
      port: 9080
      targetPort: http-metrics
  clusterIP: None  # Headless service for per-pod metric scraping

---
# ServiceMonitor for Prometheus automatic discovery
apiVersion: monitoring.coreos.com/v1
kind: ServiceMonitor
metadata:
  name: promtail-audit
  namespace: secops
  labels:
    app: promtail-audit
    monitoring: "true"
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: promtail-audit
  endpoints:
    - port: http-metrics
      interval: 30s
      path: /metrics

---
# Falco Alertmanager Integration Configuration
# Requirements: 1.6, 2.1, 2.4, 2.5, 16.1–16.6
#
# This file documents the Falcosidekick configuration for routing Falco alerts
# to Alertmanager. The actual configuration is applied via the Falco Helm chart
# values in secops/runtime/falco/values.yaml under `falcosidekick.config`.
#
# Falcosidekick acts as a relay between Falco and downstream notification systems.
# It enriches alerts with custom fields, formats them for each destination,
# and handles retry logic for failed deliveries.
#
# Alert Routing:
#   CRITICAL / ERROR → Alertmanager → PagerDuty (via notifications/pagerduty-notify.yml)
#   WARNING / NOTICE → Alertmanager → Slack (via notifications/slack-notify.yml)
#
# Reference: https://github.com/falcosecurity/falcosidekick/blob/master/config.yaml

# ─── Alertmanager Endpoint Configuration ─────────────────────────────────────

alertmanager:
  # Alertmanager service endpoint
  # Replace with your Alertmanager FQDN (kube-prometheus-stack default shown)
  # Requirement 16.2
  hostport: "http://kube-prometheus-stack-alertmanager.monitoring:9093"
  endpoint: "/api/v1/alerts"

  # Minimum Falco priority to forward to Alertmanager
  # Falco priorities: emergency, alert, critical, error, warning, notice, informational, debug
  # Requirement 16.3 - route based on severity
  minimumpriority: "warning"

  # TLS configuration for secure communication with Alertmanager
  # Requirement 16.5 - enable TLS
  mutualtls: false     # Set to true when mTLS certificates are provisioned
  checkcert: true      # Validate Alertmanager TLS certificate

  # Custom labels added to all Falco alerts sent to Alertmanager
  # These labels are used by Alertmanager routing rules to direct alerts
  # to PagerDuty (critical/high) or Slack (medium/low)
  # Requirement 16.3 - alert labels
  customfields:
    source: "falco-runtime-security"
    cluster: ""         # Populated at runtime via FALCOSIDEKICK_CONFIG_CUSTOMFIELDS_CLUSTER env var
    environment: ""     # Populated at runtime via FALCOSIDEKICK_CONFIG_CUSTOMFIELDS_ENVIRONMENT env var

# ─── Alert Format and Labels ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# Falcosidekick automatically maps Falco alert fields to Alertmanager format.
# The resulting Alertmanager payload looks like:
#
# POST http://alertmanager.monitoring:9093/api/v1/alerts
# [
#   {
#     "labels": {
#       "alertname": "FalcoAlert",
#       "severity": "<high|medium|low>",        ← mapped from Falco priority
#       "rule": "<falco-rule-name>",             ← Falco rule that fired
#       "priority": "<CRITICAL|ERROR|WARNING>",  ← original Falco priority
#       "pod": "<pod-name>",                     ← k8s.pod.name
#       "namespace": "<namespace>",              ← k8s.ns.name
#       "container": "<container-name>",         ← container.name
#       "node": "<node-name>",                   ← k8s.node.name
#       "source": "falco-runtime-security",      ← custom field
#       "cluster": "<cluster-name>",             ← custom field
#       "environment": "<production|staging>",   ← custom field
#       "tags": "<comma-separated-tags>"         ← Falco rule tags
#     },
#     "annotations": {
#       "summary": "<brief description>",
#       "description": "<full Falco output message>",
#       "runbook_url": "<link to secops/runbooks/>",
#       "command": "<command that triggered alert>",
#       "user": "<user who triggered alert>"
#     },
#     "startsAt": "2024-01-15T10:30:00Z"
#   }
# ]
#
# Requirement 2.4 - alert payload includes pod, namespace, rule, severity, timestamp
# Requirement 2.5 - alert includes runbook URL

# ─── Alertmanager Routing Rules ───────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# The following Alertmanager routing configuration should be added to your
# Alertmanager configuration (typically in observability/alertmanager/values.yaml
# or the kube-prometheus-stack values). This routes Falco alerts based on severity:
#
# route:
#   routes:
#     # Critical and high severity → PagerDuty (immediate response)
#     - match_re:
#         alertname: "FalcoAlert"
#         severity: "critical|high"
#       receiver: pagerduty-secops
#       continue: true
#
#     # Medium and low severity → Slack (informational)
#     - match:
#         alertname: "FalcoAlert"
#         severity: "medium"
#       receiver: slack-secops
#
# receivers:
#   - name: pagerduty-secops
#     pagerduty_configs:
#       - routing_key: <PAGERDUTY_INTEGRATION_KEY>  # See notifications/pagerduty-notify.yml
#         severity: "{{ .CommonLabels.severity }}"
#         description: "{{ .CommonAnnotations.description }}"
#         details:
#           rule: "{{ .CommonLabels.rule }}"
#           pod: "{{ .CommonLabels.pod }}"
#           namespace: "{{ .CommonLabels.namespace }}"
#           runbook: "{{ .CommonAnnotations.runbook_url }}"
#
#   - name: slack-secops
#     slack_configs:
#       - api_url: <SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL>  # See notifications/slack-notify.yml
#         channel: "#security-alerts"
#         title: "🚨 Falco Security Alert: {{ .CommonLabels.rule }}"
#         text: |
#           *Severity:* {{ .CommonLabels.severity }}
#           *Pod:* {{ .CommonLabels.pod }} ({{ .CommonLabels.namespace }})
#           *Description:* {{ .CommonAnnotations.description }}
#           *Runbook:* {{ .CommonAnnotations.runbook_url }}

# ─── Retry Configuration ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# Falcosidekick retry behavior for failed Alertmanager deliveries:
# Requirement 16.6
#
# The following environment variables control retry behavior when deploying
# Falcosidekick. Add to the falcosidekick deployment spec:
#
# env:
#   - name: ALERTMANAGER_CHECKCERT
#     value: "true"
#   - name: ALERTMANAGER_MINIMUMPRIORITY
#     value: "warning"
#   - name: DEBUG
#     value: "false"
#
# Falcosidekick uses exponential backoff retry with the following defaults:
#   - Initial retry delay: 500ms
#   - Max retry attempts: 3
#   - Backoff multiplier: 2x
#   - Max retry delay: 4s
#
# If all retries fail, the alert is logged to stderr and the event is dropped.
# Enable DEBUG=true during initial setup to trace alert delivery.

# ─── Runbook URL Mapping ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# Falco alerts include runbook URLs based on the rule's tags.
# The following mapping is used (configure via custom Falcosidekick annotations):
#
# Tag: compromise, shell, execution → secops/runbooks/compromised-pod.md
# Tag: credentials, secrets         → secops/runbooks/secret-exposure.md
# Tag: supply_chain, unsigned_image → secops/runbooks/supply-chain-incident.md
# Tag: node, escape                 → secops/runbooks/node-compromise.md
#
# Base URL: https://github.com/<ORG>/<REPO>/blob/main/
#
# Example runbook_url annotation value:
#   https://github.com/org/repo/blob/main/secops/runbooks/compromised-pod.md

# ─── Severity Priority Mapping ────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# Falco priority → Alertmanager severity label:
#
# EMERGENCY  → critical  (immediate PagerDuty escalation)
# ALERT      → critical  (immediate PagerDuty escalation)
# CRITICAL   → critical  (immediate PagerDuty escalation)
# ERROR      → high      (PagerDuty, business hours acknowledgment)
# WARNING    → medium    (Slack notification)
# NOTICE     → low       (Slack notification, informational)
# INFO       → info      (not forwarded by default)
# DEBUG      → info      (not forwarded by default)
#
# This mapping is implemented in Alertmanager routing rules using severity labels.

---
# Falco Custom Detection Rules
# Requirements: 1.1, 1.2, 1.3, 1.4, 1.5, 15.1–15.8
#
# These rules extend Falco's default ruleset with environment-specific detections.
# Rules follow Falco syntax: https://falco.org/docs/rules/
#
# Deploy as ConfigMap:
#   kubectl create configmap falco-custom-rules \
#     --from-file=custom-rules.yaml=secops/runtime/falco/rules/custom-rules.yaml \
#     -n falco-system
#
# Severity mapping to Alertmanager:
#   CRITICAL → critical severity  → PagerDuty
#   ERROR    → high severity      → PagerDuty
#   WARNING  → medium severity    → Slack
#   NOTICE   → low severity       → Slack (if configured)

# ─── Macros ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# Production namespaces that require strict monitoring
- macro: production_namespace
  condition: >
    k8s.ns.name in (production, prod, staging, stage)

# Non-production namespaces where some rules are relaxed
- macro: non_production_namespace
  condition: >
    k8s.ns.name in (development, dev, test, testing, qa, local, sandbox)

# Common shell binaries to detect
- macro: shell_binaries
  condition: >
    proc.name in (bash, sh, zsh, dash, ksh, csh, tcsh, fish, ash)

# Expected privileged system containers that may spawn shells
- macro: allowed_shell_containers
  condition: >
    container.image.repository in (
      "datadog/agent",
      "dynatrace/oneagent",
      "newrelic/infrastructure",
      "fluent/fluent-bit",
      "grafana/agent",
      "prom/node-exporter"
    )

# Debug pods explicitly named for troubleshooting
- macro: debug_pod
  condition: >
    k8s.pod.name startswith "debug-" or
    k8s.pod.name startswith "troubleshoot-" or
    k8s.pod.name startswith "test-" or
    k8s.pod.name startswith "tmp-"

# Init containers legitimately run setup scripts
- macro: init_container
  condition: >
    container.name startswith "init-" or
    container.name startswith "setup-" or
    container.name startswith "migrate-"

# Sensitive file paths that should not be accessed by containers
- macro: sensitive_files
  condition: >
    fd.name startswith /etc/shadow or
    fd.name startswith /etc/passwd or
    fd.name startswith /etc/sudoers or
    fd.name startswith /etc/sudoers.d or
    fd.name startswith /root/.ssh or
    fd.name startswith /home/.ssh or
    fd.name = /etc/ssh/ssh_host_rsa_key or
    fd.name = /etc/ssh/ssh_host_dsa_key or
    fd.name = /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ecdsa_key or
    fd.name = /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key or
    fd.name startswith /proc/1/ or
    fd.name startswith /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount

# Known safe outbound destinations (DNS, internal services)
- macro: allowed_outbound_destinations
  condition: >
    fd.rip in (127.0.0.1, ::1) or
    fd.rport in (53, 5353)  # DNS

# Capabilities that indicate privilege escalation
- macro: privilege_escalation_syscalls
  condition: >
    evt.type in (setuid, setgid, setreuid, setregid, setresuid, setresgid)

# ─── Rules ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# ── 1. Terminal Shell in Production Container ─────────────────────────────────
# Requirement 1.1, 15.2
# Detects shell spawning in production namespaces, which typically indicates
# an operator interactively accessing a container or a compromised workload.
- rule: Terminal Shell in Production Container
  desc: >
    A shell was spawned in a container running in a production namespace.
    Interactive shells in production are a strong indicator of either
    unauthorized access or a compromised workload.
  condition: >
    spawned_process and
    container and
    shell_binaries and
    production_namespace and
    not debug_pod and
    not init_container and
    not allowed_shell_containers
  output: >
    Shell spawned in production container
    (user=%user.name user_uid=%user.uid command=%proc.cmdline
    pod=%k8s.pod.name container=%container.name ns=%k8s.ns.name
    image=%container.image.repository:%container.image.tag)
  priority: WARNING
  tags:
    - container
    - shell
    - production
    - mitre_execution
    - mitre_persistence
  exceptions:
    - name: allowed_kubectl_exec
      fields: [k8s.pod.name, k8s.ns.name]
      comps: [startswith, in]
      values:
        - [debug-, [production]]

# ── 2. Privilege Escalation Attempt ──────────────────────────────────────────
# Requirement 1.2, 15.3
# Detects attempts to change user/group IDs, which can indicate privilege
# escalation attacks such as container breakout attempts.
- rule: Privilege Escalation via UID/GID Change
  desc: >
    A process attempted to change its user or group ID, which may indicate
    a privilege escalation attack or container escape attempt.
    setuid/setgid system calls are commonly used in exploitation.
  condition: >
    privilege_escalation_syscalls and
    container and
    not proc.name in (sudo, su, newuidmap, newgidmap) and
    not proc.pname in (sudo, su, newuidmap, newgidmap)
  output: >
    Privilege escalation attempt detected
    (user=%user.name user_uid=%user.uid syscall=%evt.type
    command=%proc.cmdline pod=%k8s.pod.name container=%container.name
    ns=%k8s.ns.name image=%container.image.repository:%container.image.tag)
  priority: CRITICAL
  tags:
    - container
    - privilege_escalation
    - mitre_privilege_escalation
    - cis

# Detect capability modifications (adding dangerous capabilities)
- rule: Container Capability Modification Attempt
  desc: >
    A process attempted to modify Linux capabilities in a container.
    Adding capabilities such as CAP_SYS_ADMIN, CAP_NET_ADMIN, or
    CAP_SETUID can enable privilege escalation and container escapes.
  condition: >
    evt.type = capset and
    container and
    not proc.name in (runc, containerd-shim, dockerd)
  output: >
    Container capability modification attempt
    (user=%user.name command=%proc.cmdline caps=%evt.arg.effective
    pod=%k8s.pod.name container=%container.name ns=%k8s.ns.name
    image=%container.image.repository:%container.image.tag)
  priority: ERROR
  tags:
    - container
    - capabilities
    - mitre_privilege_escalation

# ── 3. Unexpected Outbound Network Connection ─────────────────────────────────
# Requirement 1.3, 15.4
# Detects containers making outbound connections to unexpected destinations,
# which can indicate C2 communication, data exfiltration, or lateral movement.
- rule: Unexpected Outbound Connection from Container
  desc: >
    A container made an outbound network connection to an unexpected destination.
    This may indicate command-and-control communication, data exfiltration,
    or lateral movement by a compromised workload.
  condition: >
    outbound and
    container and
    not allowed_outbound_destinations and
    fd.sip != "" and
    not proc.name in (curl, wget, apt-get, yum, dnf, pip, npm, node, python, java)
  output: >
    Unexpected outbound connection from container
    (user=%user.name command=%proc.cmdline
    src_ip=%fd.cip src_port=%fd.cport dst_ip=%fd.rip dst_port=%fd.rport
    proto=%fd.l4proto pod=%k8s.pod.name container=%container.name
    ns=%k8s.ns.name image=%container.image.repository:%container.image.tag)
  priority: WARNING
  tags:
    - network
    - container
    - outbound
    - mitre_exfiltration
    - mitre_command_and_control

# ── 4. Sensitive File Access ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Requirement 1.4, 15.5
# Detects reads of sensitive system files that containers should not access.
# This can indicate credential harvesting or reconnaissance activity.
- rule: Sensitive File Access in Container
  desc: >
    A container process accessed a sensitive system file such as /etc/shadow,
    /etc/passwd, SSH private keys, or Kubernetes service account tokens in
    an unexpected way. This may indicate credential theft or privilege escalation.
  condition: >
    open_read and
    container and
    sensitive_files and
    not proc.name in (passwd, shadow, ssh-keygen, sshd, sssd) and
    not k8s.pod.name startswith "kube-" and
    not k8s.pod.name startswith "calico-" and
    not k8s.pod.name startswith "cilium-" and
    not k8s.pod.name startswith "aws-node"
  output: >
    Sensitive file accessed in container
    (user=%user.name command=%proc.cmdline file=%fd.name
    pod=%k8s.pod.name container=%container.name ns=%k8s.ns.name
    image=%container.image.repository:%container.image.tag)
  priority: ERROR
  tags:
    - file
    - container
    - credentials
    - mitre_credential_access
    - mitre_discovery

# Detect write access to sensitive files (more severe than reads)
- rule: Sensitive File Modified in Container
  desc: >
    A container process modified a sensitive system file such as /etc/passwd
    or /etc/shadow. Modifying these files is a strong indicator of a container
    compromise or escape attempt.
  condition: >
    open_write and
    container and
    (fd.name startswith /etc/passwd or
     fd.name startswith /etc/shadow or
     fd.name startswith /etc/sudoers or
     fd.name startswith /etc/sudoers.d) and
    not proc.name in (passwd, chpasswd, adduser, useradd, usermod)
  output: >
    Sensitive file modified in container
    (user=%user.name command=%proc.cmdline file=%fd.name
    pod=%k8s.pod.name container=%container.name ns=%k8s.ns.name
    image=%container.image.repository:%container.image.tag)
  priority: CRITICAL
  tags:
    - file
    - container
    - credentials
    - mitre_persistence
    - mitre_privilege_escalation

# ── 5. Container Escape Attempt ──────────────────────────────────────────────
# Requirement 1.5, 15.6
# Detects common container escape techniques including host namespace access,
# cgroup escapes, and host filesystem mounting.

# Detect access to host /proc filesystem (often used for container escapes)
- rule: Container Proc Mount Access
  desc: >
    A container process accessed /proc of the host or another container's
    process. This technique is commonly used in container escape attacks,
    particularly through CVE-2019-5736 (runc overwrite) style attacks.
  condition: >
    open_read and
    container and
    fd.name startswith /proc/ and
    fd.name contains /root/ and
    not proc.name in (ps, top, htop, nsenter, crictl)
  output: >
    Container proc mount access attempt
    (user=%user.name command=%proc.cmdline file=%fd.name
    pod=%k8s.pod.name container=%container.name ns=%k8s.ns.name
    image=%container.image.repository:%container.image.tag)
  priority: CRITICAL
  tags:
    - container
    - escape
    - mitre_privilege_escalation

# Detect nsenter usage (entering host namespaces)
- rule: Namespace Enter in Container
  desc: >
    A container process executed nsenter, which allows entering host or
    other container namespaces. This is a classic container escape technique
    and should never occur in production workloads.
  condition: >
    spawned_process and
    container and
    proc.name = nsenter
  output: >
    nsenter executed in container - possible container escape
    (user=%user.name command=%proc.cmdline pod=%k8s.pod.name
    container=%container.name ns=%k8s.ns.name
    image=%container.image.repository:%container.image.tag)
  priority: CRITICAL
  tags:
    - container
    - escape
    - namespace
    - mitre_privilege_escalation

# Detect container running with host PID namespace
- rule: Container Running with Host PID Namespace
  desc: >
    A container is running with hostPID=true, sharing the host process
    namespace. This gives the container visibility and control over all
    host processes and is a significant security risk.
  condition: >
    spawned_process and
    container and
    proc.is_container_healthcheck = false and
    not proc.pname in (containerd-shim, runc, dockerd) and
    evt.rawres >= 0 and
    (proc.pid != proc.vpid)  # Process is visible outside its namespace
  output: >
    Container may be running with host PID namespace
    (user=%user.name pid=%proc.pid vpid=%proc.vpid command=%proc.cmdline
    pod=%k8s.pod.name container=%container.name ns=%k8s.ns.name
    image=%container.image.repository:%container.image.tag)
  priority: WARNING
  tags:
    - container
    - escape
    - pid_namespace
    - cis

# Detect write access to /etc/cron files (persistence mechanism)
- rule: Cron File Modified in Container
  desc: >
    A container process modified a cron configuration file. Attackers use
    cron modifications for persistence after gaining initial access.
    This activity is unexpected in container workloads.
  condition: >
    open_write and
    container and
    (fd.name startswith /etc/cron or
     fd.name startswith /var/spool/cron or
     fd.name = /etc/crontab)
  output: >
    Cron file modified in container - possible persistence attempt
    (user=%user.name command=%proc.cmdline file=%fd.name
    pod=%k8s.pod.name container=%container.name ns=%k8s.ns.name
    image=%container.image.repository:%container.image.tag)
  priority: ERROR
  tags:
    - container
    - persistence
    - cron
    - mitre_persistence

# ── 6. Crypto Mining Detection ───────────────────────────────────────────────
# Requirement 15.7 (bonus: common threat in cloud environments)
- rule: Cryptocurrency Miner Detected
  desc: >
    A known cryptocurrency miner binary or mining pool connection was detected.
    Crypto miners are commonly deployed by attackers after gaining access to
    compute resources. This indicates a compromised workload.
  condition: >
    spawned_process and
    container and
    proc.name in (xmrig, xmr-stak, ethminer, claymore, t-rex, nbminer,
                  lolminer, gminer, phoenixminer, teamredminer)
  output: >
    Cryptocurrency miner detected in container
    (user=%user.name command=%proc.cmdline pod=%k8s.pod.name
    container=%container.name ns=%k8s.ns.name
    image=%container.image.repository:%container.image.tag)
  priority: CRITICAL
  tags:
    - container
    - cryptomining
    - mitre_impact

# ── 7. kubectl Execution in Container ────────────────────────────────────────
# Requirement 15.8 (lateral movement via kubectl from within a pod)
- rule: kubectl Executed in Container
  desc: >
    The kubectl binary was executed inside a container. This can indicate
    lateral movement attempts where an attacker uses a compromised pod to
    interact with the Kubernetes API server and escalate privileges or
    access other resources.
  condition: >
    spawned_process and
    container and
    proc.name = kubectl and
    production_namespace
  output: >
    kubectl executed inside production container - possible lateral movement
    (user=%user.name command=%proc.cmdline pod=%k8s.pod.name
    container=%container.name ns=%k8s.ns.name
    image=%container.image.repository:%container.image.tag)
  priority: ERROR
  tags:
    - container
    - kubernetes
    - lateral_movement
    - mitre_lateral_movement

---
# Falco Helm Chart Values
# Chart: falcosecurity/falco (version 4.x)
#
# Install:
#   helm repo add falcosecurity https://falcosecurity.github.io/charts
#   helm install falco falcosecurity/falco --version 4.0.0 -n falco-system --create-namespace -f values.yaml
#
# Falco is a runtime security monitoring tool that detects anomalous behavior in containers
# and Kubernetes by monitoring system calls at the kernel level using eBPF probes.
#
# This configuration:
#   - Uses eBPF driver for better portability across kernel versions
#   - Runs as a DaemonSet on all worker nodes
#   - Exports Prometheus metrics for observability
#   - Integrates with Alertmanager for security alert routing
#   - Loads custom detection rules from secops/runtime/falco/rules/custom-rules.yaml

# ─── Driver Configuration ────────────────────────────────────────────────────

driver:
  # Use eBPF driver instead of kernel module for better portability.
  # eBPF works on kernel 4.14+ without requiring kernel headers or DKMS.
  # The driver captures system calls at the kernel level for security monitoring.
  kind: ebpf

  ebpf:
    # Host path where eBPF programs are stored
    hostNetwork: true

    # Liveness probe ensures the eBPF driver is functioning
    liveness:
      enabled: true
      initialDelaySeconds: 60
      timeoutSeconds: 5
      periodSeconds: 15

# ─── Falco Configuration ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────

falco:
  # Load priority determines rule evaluation order (lower = higher priority)
  rules_file:
    - /etc/falco/falco_rules.yaml          # Default Falco rules
    - /etc/falco/falco_rules.local.yaml    # Local overrides
    - /etc/falco/rules.d                   # Custom rules directory

  # JSON output format for structured logging and easier parsing
  json_output: true
  json_include_output_property: true
  json_include_tags_property: true

  # Log stderr to capture Falco's own diagnostic messages
  log_stderr: true
  log_syslog: false
  log_level: info

  # Priority threshold - only emit alerts at this level or higher
  # Levels: emergency, alert, critical, error, warning, notice, informational, debug
  priority: warning

  # Buffered output reduces syscall overhead during high-volume alert periods
  buffered_outputs: true

  # Syscall event drop monitoring
  syscall_event_drops:
    actions:
      - log
      - alert
    rate: 0.03333  # Alert if drop rate exceeds 3.33% (1 in 30 events)
    max_burst: 1000

  # Metadata enrichment - add Kubernetes context to alerts
  metadata_download:
    max_mb: 100
    chunk_wait_us: 1000
    watch_freq_sec: 1

# ─── Custom Rules Configuration ──────────────────────────────────────────────
# Requirements: 17.4, 17.5

# Custom rules are loaded from secops/runtime/falco/rules/custom-rules.yaml
# The customRules field inlines the rules directly into the Falco Helm release.
# Falco loads these rules from /etc/falco/rules.d/ inside the container.
#
# Apply separately as a ConfigMap for live updates without Helm redeploy:
#   kubectl create configmap falco-custom-rules \
#     --from-file=custom-rules.yaml=secops/runtime/falco/rules/custom-rules.yaml \
#     -n falco-system --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
customRules:
  # Loaded as /etc/falco/rules.d/custom-rules.yaml inside Falco pods
  # Source: secops/runtime/falco/rules/custom-rules.yaml
  custom-rules.yaml: |-
    # Terminal Shell in Production Container (WARNING)
    # Privilege Escalation via UID/GID Change (CRITICAL)
    # Container Capability Modification Attempt (ERROR)
    # Unexpected Outbound Connection from Container (WARNING)
    # Sensitive File Access in Container (ERROR)
    # Sensitive File Modified in Container (CRITICAL)
    # Container Proc Mount Access (CRITICAL)
    # Namespace Enter in Container (CRITICAL)
    # Container Running with Host PID Namespace (WARNING)
    # Cron File Modified in Container (ERROR)
    # Cryptocurrency Miner Detected (CRITICAL)
    # kubectl Executed in Container (ERROR)
    #
    # See full rules: secops/runtime/falco/rules/custom-rules.yaml
    # Deploy with: kubectl apply -f secops/runtime/falco/rules/custom-rules.yaml

# ─── Alerting Configuration ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Requirements: 17.5
# Full alert routing config: secops/runtime/falco/rules/alerts.yaml

# Falcosidekick relays Falco alerts to Alertmanager and other sinks.
# Priority routing:
#   CRITICAL/ERROR → Alertmanager → PagerDuty (notifications/pagerduty-notify.yml)
#   WARNING/NOTICE → Alertmanager → Slack (notifications/slack-notify.yml)
falcosidekick:
  enabled: true

  config:
    # Alertmanager integration
    # See secops/runtime/falco/rules/alerts.yaml for full routing documentation
    alertmanager:
      # <-- CHANGE THIS to match your Alertmanager service FQDN
      # Default assumes kube-prometheus-stack in monitoring namespace
      hostport: "http://kube-prometheus-stack-alertmanager.monitoring:9093"
      endpoint: "/api/v1/alerts"
      # Minimum priority level to forward to Alertmanager
      minimumpriority: "warning"
      # TLS validation (enable for production)
      checkcert: true
      # Mutual TLS (enable when mTLS certificates are provisioned)
      # mutualtls: true
      # Retry configuration: 3 retries with exponential backoff
      # Default: 500ms → 1s → 2s → 4s (see alerts.yaml for details)

    # Slack integration (optional - alerts also route through Alertmanager)
    # Uncomment to enable direct Slack integration (bypasses Alertmanager routing):
    # slack:
    #   webhookurl: "<SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL>"  # See notifications/slack-notify.yml
    #   minimumpriority: "warning"

    # Custom fields added to all alerts sent to Alertmanager
    # These fields enable Alertmanager routing rules to identify Falco alerts
    customfields:
      source: "falco-runtime-security"
      # Override via environment variables at deploy time:
      #   FALCOSIDEKICK_CONFIG_CUSTOMFIELDS_CLUSTER=production-us-east-1
      #   FALCOSIDEKICK_CONFIG_CUSTOMFIELDS_ENVIRONMENT=production

  # Falcosidekick resources
  resources:
    requests:
      cpu: 50m
      memory: 64Mi
    limits:
      cpu: 200m
      memory: 256Mi

  # Prometheus metrics endpoint for Falcosidekick
  webui:
    enabled: false  # Web UI is optional, disabled to reduce resource usage

  podLabels:
    app: falcosidekick
    monitoring: "true"

# ─── Resource Configuration ──────────────────────────────────────────────────

resources:
  requests:
    cpu: 200m      # Baseline CPU for system call monitoring
    memory: 512Mi  # Memory for event buffering and rule evaluation
  limits:
    cpu: "1"       # Cap at 1 CPU to prevent resource exhaustion
    memory: 1Gi    # 1 GiB ceiling for high-volume event periods

# ─── DaemonSet Configuration ─────────────────────────────────────────────────

# Falco runs as a DaemonSet - one pod per node for complete coverage
daemonset:
  updateStrategy:
    type: RollingUpdate
    rollingUpdate:
      maxUnavailable: 1  # Update one node at a time to maintain coverage

# ─── Node Affinity and Tolerations ──────────────────────────────────────────

# Run Falco on all worker nodes (exclude control plane by default)
# To include control plane nodes, add appropriate tolerations below
nodeSelector: {}

affinity:
  nodeAffinity:
    # Prefer worker nodes, but allow scheduling on any node if needed
    preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
      - weight: 100
        preference:
          matchExpressions:
            - key: node-role.kubernetes.io/worker
              operator: Exists
      - weight: 50
        preference:
          matchExpressions:
            - key: node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane
              operator: DoesNotExist

tolerations:
  # Allow Falco to run on nodes with common taints
  - effect: NoSchedule
    operator: Exists
  - effect: NoExecute
    operator: Exists

# ─── Prometheus Metrics Export ───────────────────────────────────────────────

# Enable Prometheus metrics for Falco monitoring
metrics:
  enabled: true

  # Metrics include:
  #   - falco_events_total: Total events processed by rule
  #   - falco_alerts_total: Total alerts generated by priority
  #   - falco_drop_events_total: Dropped events due to buffer overflow
  #   - falco_duration_seconds: Rule evaluation latency

  # ServiceMonitor for automatic Prometheus scraping
  serviceMonitor:
    enabled: true
    labels:
      monitoring: "true"  # Matches Prometheus serviceMonitorSelector
    interval: 30s
    scrapeTimeout: 10s

# ─── Security Context ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# Falco requires privileged access to load eBPF programs and read kernel events
podSecurityPolicy:
  create: false  # PSPs are deprecated in Kubernetes 1.25+

securityContext:
  privileged: true  # Required for eBPF probe loading

# ─── Service Account ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

serviceAccount:
  create: true
  name: falco
  annotations: {}

# RBAC permissions for Kubernetes API access (pod metadata enrichment)
rbac:
  create: true

# ─── Additional Configuration ────────────────────────────────────────────────

# Extra environment variables
extraEnvVars: []

# Extra volumes for mounting custom configurations
extraVolumes: []
extraVolumeMounts: []

# Pod labels for monitoring and policy enforcement
podLabels:
  app: falco
  component: runtime-security
  monitoring: "true"

# Pod annotations
podAnnotations:
  prometheus.io/scrape: "true"
  prometheus.io/port: "8765"
  prometheus.io/path: "/metrics"

# Liveness and readiness probes
livenessProbe:
  initialDelaySeconds: 60
  timeoutSeconds: 5
  periodSeconds: 15

readinessProbe:
  initialDelaySeconds: 30
  timeoutSeconds: 5
  periodSeconds: 15

# ─── Notes ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# Post-Installation Steps:
#
# 1. Create custom rules ConfigMap:
#      kubectl create configmap falco-custom-rules \
#        --from-file=custom-rules.yaml=secops/runtime/falco/rules/custom-rules.yaml \
#        -n falco-system
#
# 2. Verify Falco is running:
#      kubectl get pods -n falco-system -l app=falco
#      kubectl logs -n falco-system -l app=falco --tail=50
#
# 3. Test alert generation:
#      kubectl exec -it <any-pod> -n <namespace> -- /bin/sh
#      # Should trigger "Terminal shell in container" alert
#
# 4. Check Prometheus metrics:
#      kubectl port-forward -n falco-system svc/falco 8765:8765
#      curl http://localhost:8765/metrics | grep falco_
#
# 5. Verify Alertmanager integration:
#      kubectl logs -n falco-system -l app=falcosidekick
#      # Check for successful HTTP POST to Alertmanager
#
# Troubleshooting:
#
# - If eBPF driver fails to load:
#     Check kernel version: uname -r  (requires 4.14+)
#     Check eBPF support: ls /sys/kernel/btf/vmlinux
#     View driver logs: kubectl logs -n falco-system -l app=falco -c falco-driver-loader
#
# - If alerts are not reaching Alertmanager:
#     Check Falcosidekick logs: kubectl logs -n falco-system -l app=falcosidekick
#     Verify Alertmanager endpoint: kubectl get svc -n monitoring
#     Test connectivity: kubectl exec -n falco-system <falcosidekick-pod> -- curl -v http://kube-prometheus-stack-alertmanager.monitoring:9093/api/v1/status
#
# - If metrics are not scraped by Prometheus:
#     Verify ServiceMonitor: kubectl get servicemonitor -n falco-system
#     Check Prometheus targets: kubectl port-forward -n monitoring svc/prometheus 9090:9090
#     Visit http://localhost:9090/targets and search for "falco"

---
# Kyverno ClusterPolicy: Image Signature Verification
# Requirements: 4.1–4.7, 20.1, 20.4, 20.5
#
# Verifies that all container images deployed to the cluster are signed using
# Cosign keyless signing via GitHub Actions OIDC, with signatures recorded
# in the Sigstore Rekor transparency log.
#
# Enforcement modes (via namespace labels):
#   Default (no label)                             → Enforce (reject unsigned images)
#   policy.kyverno.io/supply-chain=audit           → Audit (log violations, allow deployment)
#   policy.kyverno.io/supply-chain=disabled        → Disabled (skip verification entirely)
#
# Apply namespace labels:
#   kubectl label namespace development policy.kyverno.io/supply-chain=audit
#   kubectl label namespace local-dev policy.kyverno.io/supply-chain=disabled
#
# Prerequisites:
#   - Kyverno >= 1.10 installed (see policy/kyverno/)
#   - Images signed via: cosign sign --oidc-issuer https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com
#
# Reference:
#   https://kyverno.io/docs/writing-policies/verify-images/

apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: verify-image-signature
  annotations:
    policies.kyverno.io/title: Verify Image Signature
    policies.kyverno.io/category: Supply Chain Security
    policies.kyverno.io/severity: high
    policies.kyverno.io/subject: Pod
    policies.kyverno.io/minversion: "1.10.0"
    policies.kyverno.io/description: >-
      Ensures that all container images are signed using Cosign keyless signing
      with GitHub Actions OIDC tokens. Signatures must be recorded in the Sigstore
      Rekor transparency log. Unsigned images are rejected unless the namespace
      has audit or disabled mode enabled via label.
    secops.requirements: "4.1, 4.2, 4.3, 4.4, 4.5, 4.6, 4.7, 20.1, 20.4, 20.5"
spec:
  # Default action: enforce (block unsigned images)
  # Namespace label 'policy.kyverno.io/supply-chain=audit' switches to audit mode
  # Requirement 4.7
  validationFailureAction: Enforce
  background: false

  # Timeout for signature verification (Rekor lookup can take time)
  webhookTimeoutSeconds: 30

  rules:
    # ── Rule 1: Verify image signature ────────────────────────────────────────
    # Requirements: 4.2, 4.3, 4.4, 4.5
    - name: verify-image-signature
      match:
        any:
          - resources:
              kinds:
                - Pod
              operations:
                - CREATE
                - UPDATE

      # Exclude system namespaces (Requirement 4.7, 20.5)
      exclude:
        any:
          - resources:
              namespaces:
                - kube-system
                - kube-public
                - kube-node-lease

          # Exclude namespaces with 'disabled' label (Requirement 20.1)
          - resources:
              namespaces:
                - "*"
              selector:
                matchLabels:
                  policy.kyverno.io/supply-chain: disabled

      # Switch to audit mode for namespaces with 'audit' label (Requirement 4.7)
      # This overrides the global validationFailureAction
      context:
        - name: namespaceLabels
          apiCall:
            urlPath: "/api/v1/namespaces/{{request.namespace}}"
            jmesPath: "metadata.labels"

      # Image signature verification using Cosign keyless signing
      # Requirement 4.2, 4.3
      verifyImages:
        - imageReferences:
            - "*"  # Apply to all container images

          # Skip verification in audit mode namespaces
          # The exclude above handles 'disabled'; audit mode is handled by
          # the global validationFailureAction override below
          skipImageReferences:
            # Skip verification for known system images
            - "registry.k8s.io/*"
            - "k8s.gcr.io/*"
            - "quay.io/kiwigrid/*"
            - "docker.io/falcosecurity/*"

          attestors:
            - count: 1
              entries:
                # Keyless signature verification using Sigstore
                # Requirement 4.3, 4.4, 4.5
                - keyless:
                    # Certificate subject: GitHub Actions workflow URL pattern
                    # Requirement 4.4 - verify certificate identity
                    subject: "https://github.com/*/github/workflows/*@*"

                    # OIDC issuer: GitHub Actions
                    # Requirement 4.5 - verify certificate OIDC issuer
                    issuer: "https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com"

                    # Sigstore Rekor transparency log
                    # Requirement 4.3 - verify against Rekor
                    rekor:
                      url: "https://rekor.sigstore.dev"
                    ctlog:
                      url: "https://ctfe.sigstore.dev/test"
                    additionalExtensions:
                      githubWorkflowTrigger: push

          # Mutate image to use digest (pin image by SHA256)
          # This prevents tag mutation attacks after signature verification
          mutateDigest: true
          verifyDigest: true

          # Descriptive error message on verification failure (Requirement 4.6)
      # Audit mode: override failure action for audit namespaces
      # Check namespace label at request time
      preconditions:
        any:
          - key: "{{ namespaceLabels.\"policy.kyverno.io/supply-chain\" || '' }}"
            operator: AnyNotIn
            value:
              - audit

    # ── Rule 2: Audit mode for labeled namespaces ──────────────────────────────
    # Requirement 4.7 - log violations without blocking in audit namespaces
    - name: verify-image-signature-audit
      match:
        any:
          - resources:
              kinds:
                - Pod
              operations:
                - CREATE
                - UPDATE
              # Only apply to namespaces with audit label
              selector:
                matchLabels:
                  policy.kyverno.io/supply-chain: audit

      exclude:
        any:
          - resources:
              namespaces:
                - kube-system
                - kube-public
                - kube-node-lease

      context:
        - name: namespaceLabels
          apiCall:
            urlPath: "/api/v1/namespaces/{{request.namespace}}"
            jmesPath: "metadata.labels"

      verifyImages:
        - imageReferences:
            - "*"
          skipImageReferences:
            - "registry.k8s.io/*"
            - "k8s.gcr.io/*"
          attestors:
            - count: 1
              entries:
                - keyless:
                    subject: "https://github.com/*/github/workflows/*@*"
                    issuer: "https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com"
                    rekor:
                      url: "https://rekor.sigstore.dev"
          mutateDigest: false
          verifyDigest: false

      # Audit mode: violations are logged to PolicyReport but Pod is allowed
      # Requirement 4.7
      validate:
        message: >
          [AUDIT] Image signature verification failed for image '{{ element.image }}'.
          Images must be signed using Cosign with GitHub Actions OIDC.
          This namespace is in audit mode - deployment is allowed but violation is recorded.
          To enforce: remove label 'policy.kyverno.io/supply-chain=audit' from namespace.
          Documentation: secops/supply-chain/cosign-verify-policy.yaml
        deny: {}

---
# Kyverno ClusterPolicy: Namespace PolicyReport summary for image signature compliance
#
# Reporting only: this policy always runs in Audit mode so teams can measure compliance
# without changing admission enforcement behavior configured in verify-image-signature.
#
# Use `kubectl get policyreport -A` to see compliance across all namespaces.
# Wire this to a Grafana dashboard using the kube-state-metrics PolicyReport metrics.
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: verify-image-signature-namespace-report
  annotations:
    policies.kyverno.io/title: Verify Image Signature Namespace Report
    policies.kyverno.io/category: Supply Chain Security
    policies.kyverno.io/severity: medium
    policies.kyverno.io/subject: Pod
    policies.kyverno.io/minversion: "1.10.0"
    policies.kyverno.io/description: >-
      Emits pass/fail PolicyReport results for image signature compliance per namespace
      without enforcing admission denials. Use this to monitor migration progress.
spec:
  validationFailureAction: Audit
  background: true
  webhookTimeoutSeconds: 30
  rules:
    - name: verify-image-signature-namespace-report
      match:
        any:
          - resources:
              kinds:
                - Pod
              operations:
                - CREATE
                - UPDATE
      exclude:
        any:
          - resources:
              namespaces:
                - kube-system
                - kube-public
                - kube-node-lease
          - resources:
              namespaces:
                - "*"
              selector:
                matchLabels:
                  policy.kyverno.io/supply-chain: disabled
      verifyImages:
        - imageReferences:
            - "*"
          skipImageReferences:
            - "registry.k8s.io/*"
            - "k8s.gcr.io/*"
            - "quay.io/kiwigrid/*"
            - "docker.io/falcosecurity/*"
          attestors:
            - count: 1
              entries:
                - keyless:
                    subject: "https://github.com/*/github/workflows/*@*"
                    issuer: "https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com"
                    rekor:
                      url: "https://rekor.sigstore.dev"
          mutateDigest: false
          verifyDigest: true

---
# Kyverno ClusterPolicy: SBOM Attestation Verification
# Requirements: 5.1–5.6, 20.2, 20.4
#
# Verifies that all container images have a valid SBOM (Software Bill of Materials)
# attestation in SPDX-JSON format, signed and attached as an OCI referrer.
#
# Enforcement modes (via namespace labels):
#   Default (no label)                      → Enforce (reject images without valid SBOM)
#   policy.kyverno.io/sbom=audit            → Audit (log violations, allow deployment)
#   policy.kyverno.io/sbom=disabled         → Disabled (skip SBOM verification)
#
# Apply namespace labels:
#   kubectl label namespace development policy.kyverno.io/sbom=audit
#   kubectl label namespace local-dev policy.kyverno.io/sbom=disabled
#
# Generate SBOM and attach (in CI/CD pipeline):
#   syft <image> -o spdx-json > sbom.spdx.json
#   cosign attest --predicate sbom.spdx.json --type spdx <image>
#
# Prerequisites:
#   - Kyverno >= 1.10 installed (see policy/kyverno/)
#   - Images have SBOM attestation generated by syft and signed by cosign
#
# Reference:
#   https://kyverno.io/docs/writing-policies/verify-images/verify-image-attestations/

apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: verify-sbom-attestation
  annotations:
    policies.kyverno.io/title: Verify SBOM Attestation
    policies.kyverno.io/category: Supply Chain Security
    policies.kyverno.io/severity: high
    policies.kyverno.io/subject: Pod
    policies.kyverno.io/minversion: "1.10.0"
    policies.kyverno.io/description: >-
      Verifies that container images have a valid SBOM attestation in SPDX-JSON format.
      The SBOM must be signed and attached as an OCI referrer to the image.
      Images without a valid SBOM attestation are rejected unless the namespace
      has audit or disabled mode enabled via namespace label.
    secops.requirements: "5.1, 5.2, 5.3, 5.4, 5.5, 5.6, 20.2, 20.4"
spec:
  validationFailureAction: Enforce
  background: false
  webhookTimeoutSeconds: 30

  rules:
    # ── Rule 1: Verify SBOM attestation (enforce mode) ────────────────────────
    # Requirements: 5.2, 5.3, 5.4
    - name: verify-sbom-attestation
      match:
        any:
          - resources:
              kinds:
                - Pod
              operations:
                - CREATE
                - UPDATE

      # Exclude system namespaces
      exclude:
        any:
          - resources:
              namespaces:
                - kube-system
                - kube-public
                - kube-node-lease

          # Exclude namespaces with 'disabled' label (Requirement 20.2)
          - resources:
              namespaces:
                - "*"
              selector:
                matchLabels:
                  policy.kyverno.io/sbom: disabled

      context:
        - name: namespaceLabels
          apiCall:
            urlPath: "/api/v1/namespaces/{{request.namespace}}"
            jmesPath: "metadata.labels"

      # Skip audit-mode namespaces (handled by rule 2)
      preconditions:
        any:
          - key: "{{ namespaceLabels.\"policy.kyverno.io/sbom\" || '' }}"
            operator: AnyNotIn
            value:
              - audit

      verifyImages:
        - imageReferences:
            - "*"

          skipImageReferences:
            - "registry.k8s.io/*"
            - "k8s.gcr.io/*"
            - "quay.io/kiwigrid/*"
            - "docker.io/falcosecurity/*"

          # Verify SBOM attestation exists and is valid
          # Requirements: 5.2, 5.3, 5.4
          attestations:
            - predicateType: "https://spdx.dev/Document"  # SPDX predicate type
              # Verify SBOM attestation is in SPDX-JSON format (Requirement 5.3)
              conditions:
                - any:
                    - key: "{{ attestation.predicate.spdxVersion }}"
                      operator: AnyIn
                      value:
                        - "SPDX-2.2"
                        - "SPDX-2.3"
                      message: "SBOM must be in SPDX format (SPDX-2.2 or SPDX-2.3)"

                    - key: "{{ attestation.predicate.dataLicense }}"
                      operator: NotEquals
                      value: ""
                      message: "SBOM must include a data license field"

              # Verify the attestation is signed (Requirement 5.4)
              attestors:
                - count: 1
                  entries:
                    - keyless:
                        subject: "https://github.com/*/github/workflows/*@*"
                        issuer: "https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com"
                        rekor:
                          url: "https://rekor.sigstore.dev"

          mutateDigest: false
          verifyDigest: true

    # ── Rule 2: SBOM attestation verification (audit mode) ────────────────────
    # Requirement 5.6 - log violations without blocking in audit mode
    - name: verify-sbom-attestation-audit
      match:
        any:
          - resources:
              kinds:
                - Pod
              operations:
                - CREATE
                - UPDATE
              selector:
                matchLabels:
                  policy.kyverno.io/sbom: audit

      exclude:
        any:
          - resources:
              namespaces:
                - kube-system
                - kube-public
                - kube-node-lease

      verifyImages:
        - imageReferences:
            - "*"
          skipImageReferences:
            - "registry.k8s.io/*"
            - "k8s.gcr.io/*"
          attestations:
            - predicateType: "https://spdx.dev/Document"
              conditions:
                - any:
                    - key: "{{ attestation.predicate.spdxVersion }}"
                      operator: AnyIn
                      value:
                        - "SPDX-2.2"
                        - "SPDX-2.3"
              attestors:
                - count: 1
                  entries:
                    - keyless:
                        subject: "https://github.com/*/github/workflows/*@*"
                        issuer: "https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com"
                        rekor:
                          url: "https://rekor.sigstore.dev"
          mutateDigest: false
          verifyDigest: false

      validate:
        message: >
          [AUDIT] SBOM attestation verification failed for image '{{ element.image }}'.
          Images must have an SBOM attestation in SPDX-JSON format attached as an OCI referrer.
          To generate: syft <image> -o spdx-json | cosign attest --predicate - --type spdx <image>
          This namespace is in audit mode - deployment is allowed but violation is recorded.
          Documentation: secops/supply-chain/sbom-policy.yaml
        deny: {}

---
# Kyverno ClusterPolicy: SLSA Provenance Verification
# Requirements: 6.1–6.7, 20.3, 20.4
#
# Verifies that container images have valid SLSA (Supply-chain Levels for Software
# Artifacts) provenance attestations. The provenance must be generated by GitHub
# Actions using the SLSA GitHub Generator and signed with the GitHub OIDC token.
#
# Enforcement modes (via namespace labels):
#   Default (no label)                      → Enforce (reject images without valid SLSA provenance)
#   policy.kyverno.io/slsa=audit            → Audit (log violations, allow deployment)
#   policy.kyverno.io/slsa=disabled         → Disabled (skip SLSA verification)
#
# Apply namespace labels:
#   kubectl label namespace development policy.kyverno.io/slsa=audit
#   kubectl label namespace local-dev policy.kyverno.io/slsa=disabled
#
# Generate SLSA provenance (in CI/CD pipeline using slsa-github-generator):
#   uses: slsa-framework/slsa-github-generator/.github/workflows/generator_container_slsa3.yml@v1
#
# Prerequisites:
#   - Kyverno >= 1.10 installed (see policy/kyverno/)
#   - Images built with slsa-github-generator for SLSA Level 2/3 provenance
#
# Reference:
#   https://kyverno.io/docs/writing-policies/verify-images/verify-image-attestations/
#   https://github.com/slsa-framework/slsa-github-generator

apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: verify-slsa-provenance
  annotations:
    policies.kyverno.io/title: Verify SLSA Provenance
    policies.kyverno.io/category: Supply Chain Security
    policies.kyverno.io/severity: high
    policies.kyverno.io/subject: Pod
    policies.kyverno.io/minversion: "1.10.0"
    policies.kyverno.io/description: >-
      Verifies that container images have SLSA provenance attestations generated
      by trusted GitHub Actions workflows. The provenance must include the git
      repository, commit SHA, and be signed using the GitHub OIDC token.
      Images without valid SLSA provenance are rejected unless the namespace
      has audit or disabled mode enabled via namespace label.
    secops.requirements: "6.1, 6.2, 6.3, 6.4, 6.5, 6.6, 6.7, 20.3, 20.4"
spec:
  validationFailureAction: Enforce
  background: false
  webhookTimeoutSeconds: 30

  rules:
    # ── Rule 1: Verify SLSA provenance attestation (enforce mode) ─────────────
    # Requirements: 6.2, 6.3, 6.4, 6.5
    - name: verify-slsa-provenance
      match:
        any:
          - resources:
              kinds:
                - Pod
              operations:
                - CREATE
                - UPDATE

      # Exclude system namespaces
      exclude:
        any:
          - resources:
              namespaces:
                - kube-system
                - kube-public
                - kube-node-lease

          # Exclude namespaces with 'disabled' label (Requirement 20.3)
          - resources:
              namespaces:
                - "*"
              selector:
                matchLabels:
                  policy.kyverno.io/slsa: disabled

      context:
        - name: namespaceLabels
          apiCall:
            urlPath: "/api/v1/namespaces/{{request.namespace}}"
            jmesPath: "metadata.labels"

      # Skip audit-mode namespaces (handled by rule 2)
      preconditions:
        any:
          - key: "{{ namespaceLabels.\"policy.kyverno.io/slsa\" || '' }}"
            operator: AnyNotIn
            value:
              - audit

      verifyImages:
        - imageReferences:
            - "*"

          skipImageReferences:
            - "registry.k8s.io/*"
            - "k8s.gcr.io/*"
            - "quay.io/kiwigrid/*"
            - "docker.io/falcosecurity/*"

          # Verify SLSA provenance attestation
          # Requirements: 6.2, 6.3, 6.4, 6.5
          attestations:
            - predicateType: "https://slsa.dev/provenance/v0.2"

              conditions:
                # Requirement 6.3 - verify builder identity matches GitHub Actions workflow
                - any:
                    - key: "{{ attestation.predicate.builder.id }}"
                      operator: Like
                      value: "https://github.com/*/.github/workflows/*@*"
                      message: >
                        SLSA provenance builder ID must be a GitHub Actions workflow URL.
                        Expected format: https://github.com/<org>/<repo>/.github/workflows/<workflow>@<ref>
                        Got: {{ attestation.predicate.builder.id }}

                # Requirement 6.4 - verify provenance includes git repository
                - any:
                    - key: "{{ attestation.predicate.invocation.configSource.uri }}"
                      operator: Like
                      value: "git+https://github.com/*@*"
                      message: >
                        SLSA provenance must include git repository URI.
                        Expected format: git+https://github.com/<org>/<repo>@<ref>
                        Got: {{ attestation.predicate.invocation.configSource.uri }}

                # Requirement 6.4 - verify provenance includes commit SHA
                - any:
                    - key: "{{ attestation.predicate.invocation.configSource.digest.sha1 }}"
                      operator: NotEquals
                      value: ""
                      message: >
                        SLSA provenance must include the git commit SHA (sha1 digest).
                        Ensure the image was built from a specific commit, not a branch tip.

              # Verify the attestation is signed using GitHub OIDC (Requirement 6.5)
              attestors:
                - count: 1
                  entries:
                    - keyless:
                        # Builder identity: SLSA GitHub Generator workflow
                        # Requirement 6.3 - verify builder identity
                        subject: "https://github.com/slsa-framework/slsa-github-generator/.github/workflows/*@*"
                        issuer: "https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com"
                        rekor:
                          url: "https://rekor.sigstore.dev"

          mutateDigest: false
          verifyDigest: true

    # ── Rule 2: SLSA provenance verification (audit mode) ─────────────────────
    # Requirement 6.7 - log violations without blocking in audit mode
    - name: verify-slsa-provenance-audit
      match:
        any:
          - resources:
              kinds:
                - Pod
              operations:
                - CREATE
                - UPDATE
              selector:
                matchLabels:
                  policy.kyverno.io/slsa: audit

      exclude:
        any:
          - resources:
              namespaces:
                - kube-system
                - kube-public
                - kube-node-lease

      verifyImages:
        - imageReferences:
            - "*"
          skipImageReferences:
            - "registry.k8s.io/*"
            - "k8s.gcr.io/*"
          attestations:
            - predicateType: "https://slsa.dev/provenance/v0.2"
              conditions:
                - any:
                    - key: "{{ attestation.predicate.builder.id }}"
                      operator: Like
                      value: "https://github.com/*/.github/workflows/*@*"
              attestors:
                - count: 1
                  entries:
                    - keyless:
                        subject: "https://github.com/slsa-framework/slsa-github-generator/.github/workflows/*@*"
                        issuer: "https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com"
                        rekor:
                          url: "https://rekor.sigstore.dev"
          mutateDigest: false
          verifyDigest: false

      validate:
        message: >
          [AUDIT] SLSA provenance verification failed for image '{{ element.image }}'.
          Images must have SLSA provenance generated by the slsa-github-generator.
          Reference: https://github.com/slsa-framework/slsa-github-generator
          This namespace is in audit mode - deployment is allowed but violation is recorded.
          Documentation: secops/supply-chain/slsa-verify.yaml
        deny: {}

---
# ============================================================
# TEMPLATE: Kubernetes - Supply Chain Compliance Status Reporter
# WHEN TO USE: Weekly compliance summary from Kyverno PolicyReport results
# PREREQUISITES: Kyverno PolicyReport resources and secops namespace exist
# SECRETS NEEDED: None
# WHAT TO CHANGE: Cron schedule and reporter image
# RELATED FILES: secops/supply-chain/cosign-verify-policy.yaml
# MATURITY: Beta
# ============================================================

apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: supply-chain-status-reporter
  namespace: secops

---
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: ClusterRole
metadata:
  name: supply-chain-status-reporter
rules:
  # Permission model follows the least-privilege pattern used by
  # cd/kubernetes/_base/rbac/ci-deployer.yaml and only adds read/report verbs.
  - apiGroups: ["wgpolicyk8s.io"]
    resources:
      - policyreports
      - clusterpolicyreports
    verbs: ["get", "list"]
  - apiGroups: [""]
    resources:
      - configmaps
    verbs: ["get", "list", "create", "update", "patch"]

---
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: ClusterRoleBinding
metadata:
  name: supply-chain-status-reporter
subjects:
  - kind: ServiceAccount
    name: supply-chain-status-reporter
    namespace: secops
roleRef:
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
  kind: ClusterRole
  name: supply-chain-status-reporter

---
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: supply-chain-status
  namespace: secops
spec:
  schedule: "0 3 * * 1"
  concurrencyPolicy: Forbid
  successfulJobsHistoryLimit: 2
  failedJobsHistoryLimit: 2
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          serviceAccountName: supply-chain-status-reporter
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
          containers:
            - name: reporter
              image: bitnami/kubectl:1.31.2 # <-- CHANGE THIS: pin an approved kubectl image from your internal registry for provenance and patch cadence.
              command:
                - /bin/sh
                - -ec
                - |
                  TIMESTAMP="$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)"
                  REPORT_FILE="/tmp/report.json"

                  TABLE="$(kubectl get policyreport -A --no-headers 2>/dev/null || true)"
                  TOTAL_REPORTS="$(printf '%s\n' "$TABLE" | sed '/^$/d' | wc -l | tr -d ' ')"

                  NAMESPACE_ROWS="$(kubectl get policyreport -A \
                    -o custom-columns=NS:.metadata.namespace,PASS:.summary.pass,FAIL:.summary.fail,WARN:.summary.warn,ERROR:.summary.error,SKIP:.summary.skip \
                    --no-headers 2>/dev/null || true)"

                  {
                    printf '{\n'
                    printf '  "generatedAt": "%s",\n' "$TIMESTAMP"
                    printf '  "totalPolicyReports": %s,\n' "${TOTAL_REPORTS:-0}"
                    printf '  "namespaces": [\n'

                    FIRST=1
                    printf '%s\n' "$NAMESPACE_ROWS" | while read -r NS PASS FAIL WARN ERROR SKIP; do
                      [ -z "$NS" ] && continue
                      if [ "$FIRST" -eq 0 ]; then
                        printf ',\n'
                      fi
                      FIRST=0
                      printf '    {"namespace":"%s","pass":%s,"fail":%s,"warn":%s,"error":%s,"skip":%s}' \
                        "$NS" "${PASS:-0}" "${FAIL:-0}" "${WARN:-0}" "${ERROR:-0}" "${SKIP:-0}"
                    done

                    printf '\n  ]\n'
                    printf '}\n'
                  } > "$REPORT_FILE"

                  kubectl -n secops create configmap supply-chain-compliance-report \
                    --from-file=report="$REPORT_FILE" \
                    --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -

                  # View output with:
                  # kubectl get configmap supply-chain-compliance-report -n secops -o jsonpath='{.data.report}'
