# ============================================================
# TEMPLATE: External Secrets Operator — AWS SecretStore (IRSA)
# WHEN TO USE: You are running on EKS and want ExternalSecrets to
#   pull secrets from AWS Secrets Manager using IAM Roles for
#   Service Accounts (IRSA) — no static AWS credentials in the cluster.
#
# PREREQUISITES:
#   1. External Secrets Operator installed:
#        helm repo add external-secrets https://charts.external-secrets.io
#        helm install external-secrets external-secrets/external-secrets \
#          -n external-secrets-system --create-namespace
#   2. IRSA role created with secretsmanager:GetSecretValue permission
#      and the trust policy allowing the ESO service account to assume it.
#      See: https://external-secrets.io/latest/provider/aws-secrets-manager/
#
# WHAT TO CHANGE: Lines marked  # <-- CHANGE THIS
# RELATED FILES: secrets/external-secrets/example-external-secret.yaml
#                secrets/rotation/aws-rotation.yml
#                terraform/aws-eks/main.tf
# MATURITY: Stable
# ============================================================

apiVersion: external-secrets.io/v1beta1
kind: ClusterSecretStore
metadata:
  name: aws-secret-store                        # <-- CHANGE THIS: one store per AWS account/region pair
  annotations:
    description: "Pulls secrets from AWS Secrets Manager via IRSA"
spec:
  provider:
    aws:
      service: SecretsManager
      region: us-east-1                         # <-- CHANGE THIS: your AWS region

      # Note 1: IRSA (IAM Roles for Service Accounts) is the preferred authentication
      # method on EKS. The External Secrets Operator service account is annotated with
      # the IAM role ARN. No static AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID is stored in the cluster.
      # The role must have the following policy:
      #   secretsmanager:GetSecretValue
      #   secretsmanager:DescribeSecret
      auth:
        jwt:
          serviceAccountRef:
            name: external-secrets               # <-- CHANGE THIS: ESO service account name (usually "external-secrets")
            namespace: external-secrets-system   # <-- CHANGE THIS: namespace where ESO is installed

---
# Note 2: The ServiceAccount below is the ESO controller's service account.
# Annotating it with the IAM role ARN tells the EKS IRSA webhook to inject
# AWS_WEB_IDENTITY_TOKEN_FILE and AWS_ROLE_ARN as environment variables,
# enabling the ESO pod to assume the role without any credentials.
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: external-secrets                        # <-- CHANGE THIS: must match spec.provider.aws.auth.jwt.serviceAccountRef.name above
  namespace: external-secrets-system            # <-- CHANGE THIS
  annotations:
    eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn: "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/external-secrets-irsa"  # <-- CHANGE THIS: your IAM role ARN

---
# ============================================================
# TEMPLATE: External Secrets Operator — Azure SecretStore (Workload Identity)
# WHEN TO USE: You are running on AKS and want ExternalSecrets to
#   pull secrets from Azure Key Vault using Workload Identity
#   (formerly AAD Pod Identity v2) — no client secrets in the cluster.
#
# PREREQUISITES:
#   1. External Secrets Operator installed (see aws-secret-store.yaml)
#   2. AKS cluster has Workload Identity enabled:
#        az aks update --enable-oidc-issuer --enable-workload-identity \
#          -g <rg> -n <cluster>
#   3. Managed Identity created with Key Vault Secrets User role on your vault.
#   4. Federated credential configured linking the Managed Identity to the
#      ESO Kubernetes ServiceAccount in the namespace where ESO runs.
#      See: https://external-secrets.io/latest/provider/azure-key-vault/
#
# WHAT TO CHANGE: Lines marked  # <-- CHANGE THIS
# RELATED FILES: secrets/external-secrets/example-external-secret.yaml
#                secrets/rotation/azure-rotation.yml
#                terraform/azure-aks/main.tf
# MATURITY: Stable
# ============================================================

apiVersion: external-secrets.io/v1beta1
kind: ClusterSecretStore
metadata:
  name: azure-secret-store                      # <-- CHANGE THIS
  annotations:
    description: "Pulls secrets from Azure Key Vault via Workload Identity"
spec:
  provider:
    azurekv:
      authType: WorkloadIdentity                # Note 1: WorkloadIdentity uses federated OIDC tokens — no client secret or certificate stored in the cluster

      # Note 2: The vaultUrl must be the full HTTPS URL of your Key Vault.
      # Find it in the Azure Portal: Key Vault → Overview → Vault URI
      vaultUrl: "https://my-keyvault.vault.azure.net"  # <-- CHANGE THIS

      serviceAccountRef:
        name: external-secrets                  # <-- CHANGE THIS: ESO service account name
        namespace: external-secrets-system      # <-- CHANGE THIS

---
# Note 3: The ServiceAccount must carry the azure.workload.identity/client-id
# annotation. The AKS Workload Identity mutating webhook injects the OIDC
# token into the ESO pod, which exchanges it for an Azure access token via
# the federated credential configured on the Managed Identity.
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: external-secrets                        # <-- CHANGE THIS
  namespace: external-secrets-system            # <-- CHANGE THIS
  annotations:
    azure.workload.identity/client-id: "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"  # <-- CHANGE THIS: Managed Identity client ID
  labels:
    azure.workload.identity/use: "true"

---
# ============================================================
# TEMPLATE: External Secrets Operator — ExternalSecret Example
# WHEN TO USE: After a ClusterSecretStore is configured (see the
#   aws/azure/gcp-secret-store.yaml files), this creates a
#   Kubernetes Secret that is automatically synced from the
#   upstream secret store.
#
# HOW IT WORKS:
#   ESO watches ExternalSecret resources. On every refreshInterval
#   it fetches the specified keys from the upstream store and writes
#   them into a Kubernetes Secret. If the upstream secret value
#   changes (e.g., after rotation), ESO updates the Kubernetes Secret
#   automatically. Pods pick up the new value on the next restart.
#
# WHAT TO CHANGE: Lines marked  # <-- CHANGE THIS
# RELATED FILES: secrets/external-secrets/aws-secret-store.yaml
#                secrets/external-secrets/azure-secret-store.yaml
#                secrets/external-secrets/gcp-secret-store.yaml
#                secrets/rotation/
# MATURITY: Stable
# ============================================================

apiVersion: external-secrets.io/v1beta1
kind: ExternalSecret
metadata:
  name: app-db-credentials # <-- CHANGE THIS: the name of the Kubernetes Secret to create
  namespace: default # <-- CHANGE THIS: namespace where the consuming pods run
spec:
  # Note 1: refreshInterval controls how often ESO checks the upstream store for
  # changes. A lower interval detects rotated secrets faster, but increases API
  # call volume to the secret store. 1 hour is a sensible default for most apps.
  # After a rotation event you can force an immediate sync with:
  #   kubectl annotate externalsecret app-db-credentials \
  #     force-sync=$(date +%s) --overwrite
  refreshInterval: 1h # <-- CHANGE THIS: balance freshness vs. API cost

  secretStoreRef:
    name: aws-secret-store # <-- CHANGE THIS: name of your ClusterSecretStore (aws/azure/gcp)
    kind: ClusterSecretStore

  target:
    name: app-db-credentials # <-- CHANGE THIS: Kubernetes Secret name (usually same as ExternalSecret name)
    creationPolicy: Owner # Note 2: Owner means ESO owns the Secret; it will be deleted if the ExternalSecret is deleted

  # Note 3: `data` maps individual keys from the upstream secret to keys in
  # the Kubernetes Secret. Use this when your upstream secret is a JSON object
  # and you want specific keys extracted.
  data:
    - secretKey: DB_HOST # Key in the Kubernetes Secret
      remoteRef:
        key: my-app/production/db # <-- CHANGE THIS: path/name in Secrets Manager, Key Vault, or Secret Manager
        property: host # <-- CHANGE THIS: JSON key within the upstream secret value

    - secretKey: DB_PORT
      remoteRef:
        key: my-app/production/db # <-- CHANGE THIS
        property: port # <-- CHANGE THIS

    - secretKey: DB_NAME
      remoteRef:
        key: my-app/production/db
        property: name

    - secretKey: DB_USER
      remoteRef:
        key: my-app/production/db
        property: username

    - secretKey: DB_PASSWORD
      remoteRef:
        key: my-app/production/db
        property: password

  # Note 4: Alternatively, use `dataFrom` to extract ALL keys from a JSON secret
  # at once. Uncomment the block below and remove the `data` block above.
  # dataFrom:
  #   - extract:
  #       key: my-app/production/db               # <-- CHANGE THIS
  #
  # The upstream secret must be a flat JSON object like:
  # { "DB_HOST": "...", "DB_PORT": "5432", ... }
  # All top-level keys are extracted and become Secret data keys.

---
# ============================================================
# TEMPLATE: External Secrets Operator — GCP SecretStore (Workload Identity)
# WHEN TO USE: You are running on GKE and want ExternalSecrets to
#   pull secrets from Google Secret Manager using GKE Workload Identity
#   — no service account key JSON stored in the cluster.
#
# PREREQUISITES:
#   1. External Secrets Operator installed (see aws-secret-store.yaml)
#   2. GKE cluster has Workload Identity enabled:
#        gcloud container clusters update <cluster> \
#          --workload-pool=<project>.svc.id.goog
#   3. GCP service account created with secretmanager.secretAccessor role.
#   4. IAM binding created linking the GCP SA to the Kubernetes SA:
#        gcloud iam service-accounts add-iam-policy-binding \
#          <gcp-sa>@<project>.iam.gserviceaccount.com \
#          --role roles/iam.workloadIdentityUser \
#          --member "serviceAccount:<project>.svc.id.goog[external-secrets-system/external-secrets]"
#      See: https://external-secrets.io/latest/provider/google-secrets-manager/
#
# WHAT TO CHANGE: Lines marked  # <-- CHANGE THIS
# RELATED FILES: secrets/external-secrets/example-external-secret.yaml
#                secrets/rotation/gcp-rotation.yml
#                terraform/gcp-gke/ (if present)
# MATURITY: Stable
# ============================================================

apiVersion: external-secrets.io/v1beta1
kind: ClusterSecretStore
metadata:
  name: gcp-secret-store                        # <-- CHANGE THIS
  annotations:
    description: "Pulls secrets from Google Secret Manager via Workload Identity"
spec:
  provider:
    gcpsm:
      projectID: my-gcp-project                 # <-- CHANGE THIS: your GCP project ID

      # Note 1: WorkloadIdentity binds the Kubernetes ServiceAccount to a GCP
      # service account via the projected token volume. The ESO pod presents the
      # Kubernetes OIDC token to GCP STS and receives a short-lived access token.
      auth:
        workloadIdentity:
          clusterLocation: us-central1           # <-- CHANGE THIS: your GKE region
          clusterName: my-cluster                # <-- CHANGE THIS
          clusterProjectID: my-gcp-project       # <-- CHANGE THIS
          serviceAccountRef:
            name: external-secrets               # <-- CHANGE THIS
            namespace: external-secrets-system   # <-- CHANGE THIS

---
# Note 2: Annotate the Kubernetes ServiceAccount with the GCP service account
# email. GKE's Workload Identity admission controller uses this annotation to
# know which GCP service account to impersonate.
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: external-secrets                        # <-- CHANGE THIS
  namespace: external-secrets-system            # <-- CHANGE THIS
  annotations:
    iam.gke.io/gcp-service-account: "external-secrets@my-gcp-project.iam.gserviceaccount.com"  # <-- CHANGE THIS

---
# ============================================================
# TEMPLATE: Secret Rotation — AWS Secrets Manager
# WHEN TO USE: Rotate a secret in AWS Secrets Manager on a schedule
#   or on demand, then force the External Secrets Operator to sync the
#   new value and restart the affected Deployment.
#
# PREREQUISITES:
#   - INFRA_AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID / INFRA_AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY in GitHub Secrets
#     (or use OIDC — see ci/github-actions/_shared/oidc-aws.yml)
#   - KUBECONFIG_BASE64: base64-encoded kubeconfig for the target cluster
#   - The secret must have rotation enabled in Secrets Manager (optional
#     for manual rotation, required for Lambda-based auto-rotation)
#
# WHAT TO CHANGE: Lines marked  # <-- CHANGE THIS
# RELATED FILES: secrets/external-secrets/aws-secret-store.yaml
#                secrets/external-secrets/example-external-secret.yaml
# MATURITY: Stable
# ============================================================

name: Rotate AWS Secret

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: "0 2 1 * *"        # <-- CHANGE THIS: rotate on the 1st of each month at 02:00 UTC
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      secret_name:
        description: "AWS Secrets Manager secret name/ARN to rotate"
        required: true
        default: "my-app/production/db"   # <-- CHANGE THIS
      environment:
        description: "Target environment"
        required: true
        default: "production"
        type: choice
        options:
          - production
          - staging
          - development

permissions:
  contents: read
  id-token: write             # Required for OIDC authentication to AWS

jobs:
  rotate:
    name: Rotate Secret
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    environment: ${{ github.event.inputs.environment || 'production' }}

    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      # Note 1: For OIDC-based auth (no static keys), replace this step with:
      # - name: Configure AWS credentials
      #   uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v4
      #   with:
      #     role-to-assume: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/github-actions-rotation
      #     aws-region: us-east-1
      - name: Configure AWS credentials
        uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v4
        with:
          aws-access-key-id: ${{ secrets.INFRA_AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID }}         # <-- CHANGE THIS
          aws-secret-access-key: ${{ secrets.INFRA_AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY }} # <-- CHANGE THIS
          aws-region: us-east-1                                              # <-- CHANGE THIS

      # Note 2: `rotate-secret` triggers the Secrets Manager rotation Lambda
      # that you configure on the secret. The Lambda must be configured separately
      # (see AWS docs for the SecretsManagerRotationTemplate Lambda blueprint).
      # If you are doing manual rotation (no Lambda), replace this step with
      # a script that generates a new value and calls `put-secret-value`.
      - name: Rotate secret
        run: |
          SECRET_NAME="${{ github.event.inputs.secret_name || 'my-app/production/db' }}"  # <-- CHANGE THIS
          echo "Rotating secret: ${SECRET_NAME}"
          aws secretsmanager rotate-secret \
            --secret-id "${SECRET_NAME}" \
            --rotate-immediately

          # Wait for rotation to complete (Lambda-based rotation is async)
          echo "Waiting for rotation to complete..."
          for i in $(seq 1 12); do
            STATUS=$(aws secretsmanager describe-secret \
              --secret-id "${SECRET_NAME}" \
              --query "RotationRules" \
              --output text 2>/dev/null || echo "none")
            LAST=$(aws secretsmanager describe-secret \
              --secret-id "${SECRET_NAME}" \
              --query "LastRotatedDate" \
              --output text)
            echo "  Attempt ${i}: LastRotatedDate=${LAST}"
            if [ "$LAST" != "None" ]; then
              ROTATED_EPOCH=$(date -d "${LAST}" +%s 2>/dev/null || date -j -f "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S" "${LAST}" +%s)
              NOW=$(date +%s)
              AGE=$((NOW - ROTATED_EPOCH))
              if [ "${AGE}" -lt 120 ]; then
                echo "Rotation completed."
                break
              fi
            fi
            sleep 10
          done

      # Note 3: After the upstream secret is updated, force the External Secrets
      # Operator to refresh the Kubernetes Secret immediately instead of waiting
      # for the next refreshInterval cycle.
      - name: Setup kubectl
        run: |
          echo "${{ secrets.KUBECONFIG_BASE64 }}" | base64 -d > /tmp/kubeconfig  # <-- CHANGE THIS
          echo "KUBECONFIG=/tmp/kubeconfig" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      - name: Force ESO sync
        run: |
          NAMESPACE="default"                          # <-- CHANGE THIS
          EXTERNAL_SECRET_NAME="app-db-credentials"   # <-- CHANGE THIS: name of the ExternalSecret resource
          kubectl annotate externalsecret "${EXTERNAL_SECRET_NAME}" \
            force-sync="$(date +%s)" \
            --overwrite \
            -n "${NAMESPACE}"
          echo "ESO sync triggered for ${EXTERNAL_SECRET_NAME}"

      # Note 4: Restart the Deployment so pods pick up the new secret value
      # from environment variables or mounted secret volumes.
      - name: Restart affected deployment
        run: |
          NAMESPACE="default"         # <-- CHANGE THIS
          DEPLOYMENT="my-app"         # <-- CHANGE THIS: name of the Deployment to restart
          kubectl rollout restart deployment/"${DEPLOYMENT}" -n "${NAMESPACE}"
          kubectl rollout status deployment/"${DEPLOYMENT}" -n "${NAMESPACE}" \
            --timeout=5m
          echo "Deployment ${DEPLOYMENT} restarted successfully."

      - name: Notify on failure
        if: failure()
        run: |
          echo "::error::Secret rotation failed. Manual intervention may be required."
          echo "Secret: ${{ github.event.inputs.secret_name }}"
          # Add Slack/Teams/PagerDuty notification here if needed
          # See notifications/ directory for templates

---
# ============================================================
# TEMPLATE: Secret Rotation — Azure Key Vault
# WHEN TO USE: Rotate a secret in Azure Key Vault on a schedule
#   or on demand, then force External Secrets Operator to sync the
#   new value and restart the affected Deployment.
#
# PREREQUISITES:
#   - AZURE_CLIENT_ID, AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET, AZURE_TENANT_ID,
#     AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID in GitHub Secrets
#     (or use OIDC — see ci/github-actions/_shared/ for examples)
#   - KUBECONFIG_BASE64: base64-encoded kubeconfig for the target cluster
#   - The service principal must have Key Vault Secrets Officer role
#     on the target Key Vault
#
# WHAT TO CHANGE: Lines marked  # <-- CHANGE THIS
# RELATED FILES: secrets/external-secrets/azure-secret-store.yaml
#                secrets/external-secrets/example-external-secret.yaml
# MATURITY: Stable
# ============================================================

name: Rotate Azure Key Vault Secret

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: "0 2 1 * *"        # <-- CHANGE THIS: rotate on the 1st of each month at 02:00 UTC
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      secret_name:
        description: "Key Vault secret name to rotate"
        required: true
        default: "db-password"  # <-- CHANGE THIS
      environment:
        description: "Target environment"
        required: true
        default: "production"
        type: choice
        options:
          - production
          - staging
          - development

permissions:
  contents: read
  id-token: write             # Required for OIDC authentication to Azure

jobs:
  rotate:
    name: Rotate Secret
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    environment: ${{ github.event.inputs.environment || 'production' }}

    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      # Note 1: For OIDC-based auth (no static credentials), replace this with:
      # - name: Azure Login
      #   uses: azure/login@v2
      #   with:
      #     client-id: ${{ secrets.AZURE_CLIENT_ID }}
      #     tenant-id: ${{ secrets.AZURE_TENANT_ID }}
      #     subscription-id: ${{ secrets.AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID }}
      - name: Azure Login
        uses: azure/login@v2
        with:
          creds: |
            {
              "clientId": "${{ secrets.AZURE_CLIENT_ID }}",
              "clientSecret": "${{ secrets.AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET }}",
              "tenantId": "${{ secrets.AZURE_TENANT_ID }}",
              "subscriptionId": "${{ secrets.AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID }}"
            }

      # Note 2: Generate a new secret value. For database passwords, use
      # openssl rand -base64 to create a cryptographically random string.
      # For API keys that cannot be randomly generated, replace this with
      # a call to the upstream API's key-rotation endpoint.
      - name: Generate new secret value
        id: generate
        run: |
          NEW_VALUE=$(openssl rand -base64 32 | tr -d '=/+' | head -c 32)
          echo "new_value=${NEW_VALUE}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "Generated new secret value (not logged)"

      - name: Set new secret in Key Vault
        run: |
          VAULT_NAME="my-keyvault"                          # <-- CHANGE THIS: your Key Vault name
          SECRET_NAME="${{ github.event.inputs.secret_name || 'db-password' }}"  # <-- CHANGE THIS
          az keyvault secret set \
            --vault-name "${VAULT_NAME}" \
            --name "${SECRET_NAME}" \
            --value "${{ steps.generate.outputs.new_value }}"
          echo "Secret '${SECRET_NAME}' updated in Key Vault '${VAULT_NAME}'"

      # Note 3: Force ESO sync so the Kubernetes Secret picks up the new value
      # immediately rather than waiting for the refreshInterval (default: 1h).
      - name: Setup kubectl
        run: |
          echo "${{ secrets.KUBECONFIG_BASE64 }}" | base64 -d > /tmp/kubeconfig  # <-- CHANGE THIS
          echo "KUBECONFIG=/tmp/kubeconfig" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      - name: Force ESO sync
        run: |
          NAMESPACE="default"                          # <-- CHANGE THIS
          EXTERNAL_SECRET_NAME="app-db-credentials"   # <-- CHANGE THIS
          kubectl annotate externalsecret "${EXTERNAL_SECRET_NAME}" \
            force-sync="$(date +%s)" \
            --overwrite \
            -n "${NAMESPACE}"
          echo "ESO sync triggered."

      # Note 4: If the rotated secret is a database password, you must update
      # the database itself as well. For managed databases (Azure Database for
      # PostgreSQL, SQL Database), add an `az` command here to reset the
      # admin/app password before restarting the pods.
      - name: Restart affected deployment
        run: |
          NAMESPACE="default"     # <-- CHANGE THIS
          DEPLOYMENT="my-app"     # <-- CHANGE THIS
          kubectl rollout restart deployment/"${DEPLOYMENT}" -n "${NAMESPACE}"
          kubectl rollout status deployment/"${DEPLOYMENT}" -n "${NAMESPACE}" \
            --timeout=5m
          echo "Deployment ${DEPLOYMENT} restarted successfully."

      - name: Azure Logout
        if: always()
        run: az logout

      - name: Notify on failure
        if: failure()
        run: |
          echo "::error::Secret rotation failed. Manual intervention may be required."

---
# ============================================================
# TEMPLATE: Secret Rotation — GCP Secret Manager
# WHEN TO USE: Rotate a secret in GCP Secret Manager on a schedule
#   or on demand, then force External Secrets Operator to sync the
#   new value and restart the affected Deployment.
#
# PREREQUISITES:
#   - Workload Identity Federation configured for GitHub Actions
#     (see: https://github.com/google-github-actions/auth#workload-identity-federation)
#   - The GCP service account must have secretmanager.secretVersionAdder and
#     secretmanager.viewer roles on the target secret
#   - KUBECONFIG_BASE64: base64-encoded kubeconfig for the target cluster
#
# WHAT TO CHANGE: Lines marked  # <-- CHANGE THIS
# RELATED FILES: secrets/external-secrets/gcp-secret-store.yaml
#                secrets/external-secrets/example-external-secret.yaml
# MATURITY: Stable
# ============================================================

name: Rotate GCP Secret

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: "0 2 1 * *"        # <-- CHANGE THIS: rotate on the 1st of each month at 02:00 UTC
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      secret_name:
        description: "GCP Secret Manager secret ID to rotate"
        required: true
        default: "my-app-db-password"  # <-- CHANGE THIS
      environment:
        description: "Target environment"
        required: true
        default: "production"
        type: choice
        options:
          - production
          - staging
          - development

permissions:
  contents: read
  id-token: write             # Required for Workload Identity Federation

jobs:
  rotate:
    name: Rotate Secret
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    environment: ${{ github.event.inputs.environment || 'production' }}

    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      # Note 1: google-github-actions/auth exchanges the GitHub OIDC token for
      # a short-lived Google access token via Workload Identity Federation.
      # No GCP service account key JSON is stored in GitHub Secrets.
      - name: Authenticate to GCP
        uses: google-github-actions/auth@v2
        with:
          workload_identity_provider: "projects/123456789/locations/global/workloadIdentityPools/github/providers/github"  # <-- CHANGE THIS
          service_account: "secret-rotator@my-gcp-project.iam.gserviceaccount.com"  # <-- CHANGE THIS

      - name: Setup gcloud CLI
        uses: google-github-actions/setup-gcloud@v2

      # Note 2: Generate a new random secret value. For non-random credentials
      # (API tokens, database admin passwords managed by the DB itself), replace
      # the openssl command with a call to the relevant provider's rotation API.
      - name: Generate new secret value
        id: generate
        run: |
          NEW_VALUE=$(openssl rand -base64 32 | tr -d '=/+' | head -c 32)
          echo "new_value=${NEW_VALUE}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "Generated new secret value (not logged)"

      # Note 3: GCP Secret Manager uses an immutable versioning model.
      # `gcloud secrets versions add` creates a new version (e.g., version/3).
      # The previous version (e.g., version/2) remains accessible until
      # explicitly disabled or destroyed. We disable the previous version
      # AFTER the new one is confirmed, providing a safe rollback window.
      - name: Add new secret version
        id: add_version
        run: |
          PROJECT_ID="my-gcp-project"                                          # <-- CHANGE THIS
          SECRET_NAME="${{ github.event.inputs.secret_name || 'my-app-db-password' }}"  # <-- CHANGE THIS

          # Get the current latest version before adding the new one
          PREV_VERSION=$(gcloud secrets versions list "${SECRET_NAME}" \
            --project="${PROJECT_ID}" \
            --filter="state=enabled" \
            --sort-by="~name" \
            --limit=1 \
            --format="value(name)" 2>/dev/null || echo "")

          echo "prev_version=${PREV_VERSION}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

          # Add new version
          printf '%s' "${{ steps.generate.outputs.new_value }}" | \
            gcloud secrets versions add "${SECRET_NAME}" \
              --project="${PROJECT_ID}" \
              --data-file=-

          echo "New version added for secret: ${SECRET_NAME}"

      - name: Disable previous secret version
        if: steps.add_version.outputs.prev_version != ''
        run: |
          PROJECT_ID="my-gcp-project"       # <-- CHANGE THIS
          SECRET_NAME="${{ github.event.inputs.secret_name || 'my-app-db-password' }}"
          PREV_VERSION="${{ steps.add_version.outputs.prev_version }}"

          echo "Disabling previous version: ${PREV_VERSION}"
          gcloud secrets versions disable "${PREV_VERSION}" \
            --project="${PROJECT_ID}" \
            --secret="${SECRET_NAME}"
          echo "Previous version disabled (not destroyed; available for rollback)."

      # Note 4: Force ESO sync — adds the `force-sync` annotation to the
      # ExternalSecret resource. ESO detects the annotation change and re-reads
      # the secret from GCP Secret Manager immediately.
      - name: Setup kubectl
        run: |
          echo "${{ secrets.KUBECONFIG_BASE64 }}" | base64 -d > /tmp/kubeconfig  # <-- CHANGE THIS
          echo "KUBECONFIG=/tmp/kubeconfig" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      - name: Force ESO sync
        run: |
          NAMESPACE="default"                          # <-- CHANGE THIS
          EXTERNAL_SECRET_NAME="app-db-credentials"   # <-- CHANGE THIS
          kubectl annotate externalsecret "${EXTERNAL_SECRET_NAME}" \
            force-sync="$(date +%s)" \
            --overwrite \
            -n "${NAMESPACE}"
          echo "ESO sync triggered."

      - name: Restart affected deployment
        run: |
          NAMESPACE="default"     # <-- CHANGE THIS
          DEPLOYMENT="my-app"     # <-- CHANGE THIS
          kubectl rollout restart deployment/"${DEPLOYMENT}" -n "${NAMESPACE}"
          kubectl rollout status deployment/"${DEPLOYMENT}" -n "${NAMESPACE}" \
            --timeout=5m
          echo "Deployment ${DEPLOYMENT} restarted successfully."

      - name: Notify on failure
        if: failure()
        run: |
          echo "::error::Secret rotation failed. Manual intervention may be required."

---
# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://taskfile.dev/schema.json
version: "3"

silent: true

dotenv:
  - .env
  - .env.local

vars:
  HELM_WEBAPP_CHART: cd/helm/webapp
  K8S_OVERLAYS: cd/kubernetes/_overlays
  TERRAFORM_DIR: terraform
  PYTHON: '{{.PYTHON | default "python3"}}'

requires:
  vars: []

tasks:
  # What: Runs the main repository validation gate (Python deps, catalog validation, FinOps tests, website build).
  # Run: task validate
  validate:
    desc: "Run the enterprise confidence gate for catalog, FinOps, and website"
    cmds:
      - task: python:deps
      - task: catalog:validate
      - task: finops:test
      - task: website:build

  # What: Installs Python development dependencies used by catalog and FinOps scripts.
  # Run: task python:deps
  python:deps:
    desc: "Install Python dependencies needed by catalog and FinOps validation"
    deps:
      - _require:python
    cmds:
      - "{{.PYTHON}} -m pip install -r requirements-dev.txt"

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # DOCKER
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

  # What: Builds a Docker image from a chosen Dockerfile and tags it.
  # Run: task docker:build IMAGE=myapp:dev DOCKERFILE=docker/node/Dockerfile
  docker:build:
    desc: "Build a Docker image. Args: IMAGE=<name:tag> DOCKERFILE=<path>"
    requires:
      vars: [IMAGE, DOCKERFILE]
    deps:
      - _require:docker
    cmds:
      - docker build -f "{{.DOCKERFILE}}" -t "{{.IMAGE}}" .

  # What: Scans a local Docker image with Trivy and fails on HIGH/CRITICAL findings.
  # Run: task docker:scan IMAGE=myapp:dev
  docker:scan:
    desc: "Scan a built image with Trivy. Args: IMAGE=<name:tag>"
    requires:
      vars: [IMAGE]
    deps:
      - _require:docker
    cmds:
      - trivy image --exit-code 1 --severity HIGH,CRITICAL "{{.IMAGE}}"

  # What: Lints every Dockerfile in the repo using the pre-commit hadolint hook.
  # Run: task docker:lint-dockerfiles
  docker:lint-dockerfiles:
    desc: "Lint every Dockerfile in the repository via pre-commit (hadolint)"
    deps:
      - _require:pre-commit
    cmds:
      - pre-commit run hadolint --all-files

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # KUBERNETES
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

  # What: Applies Kubernetes manifests for the dev overlay using kustomize.
  # Run: task k8s:apply-dev
  k8s:apply-dev:
    desc: "kubectl apply -k for the dev overlay"
    deps:
      - _require:kubectl
    cmds:
      - kubectl apply -k {{.K8S_OVERLAYS}}/dev

  # What: Applies Kubernetes manifests for the staging overlay using kustomize.
  # Run: task k8s:apply-staging
  k8s:apply-staging:
    desc: "kubectl apply -k for the staging overlay"
    deps:
      - _require:kubectl
    cmds:
      - kubectl apply -k {{.K8S_OVERLAYS}}/staging

  # What: Applies Kubernetes manifests for the prod overlay (with confirmation prompt).
  # Run: task k8s:apply-prod
  k8s:apply-prod:
    desc: "kubectl apply -k for the prod overlay (requires confirmation)"
    deps:
      - _require:kubectl
    prompt: "You are about to apply to PRODUCTION. Are you sure?"
    cmds:
      - kubectl apply -k {{.K8S_OVERLAYS}}/prod

  # What: Shows Kubernetes diff for a selected overlay before apply.
  # Run: task k8s:diff OVERLAY=dev
  k8s:diff:
    desc: "kubectl diff -k for an overlay. Args: OVERLAY=<dev|staging|prod>"
    requires:
      vars: [OVERLAY]
    deps:
      - _require:kubectl
    cmds:
      - kubectl diff -k {{.K8S_OVERLAYS}}/{{.OVERLAY}}

  # What: Waits for deployment/app rollout completion in a namespace.
  # Run: task k8s:rollout-status NAMESPACE=dev
  k8s:rollout-status:
    desc: "Check rollout status for deployment/app. Args: NAMESPACE=<ns>"
    requires:
      vars: [NAMESPACE]
    deps:
      - _require:kubectl
    cmds:
      - kubectl rollout status deployment/app -n {{.NAMESPACE}}

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # TERRAFORM
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

  # What: Initializes Terraform in a selected module directory.
  # Run: task tf:init MODULE=azure-aks
  tf:init:
    desc: "terraform init for a module. Args: MODULE=<path under terraform/>"
    requires:
      vars: [MODULE]
    deps:
      - _require:terraform
    dir: "{{.TERRAFORM_DIR}}/{{.MODULE}}"
    cmds:
      - terraform init

  # What: Creates a Terraform plan for a module/environment pair.
  # Run: task tf:plan MODULE=azure-aks ENV=dev
  tf:plan:
    desc: "terraform plan for a module + env. Args: MODULE=<path> ENV=<dev|staging|prod>"
    requires:
      vars: [MODULE, ENV]
    deps:
      - _require:terraform
    dir: "{{.TERRAFORM_DIR}}/{{.MODULE}}"
    cmds:
      - terraform plan -var-file="vars/{{.ENV}}.tfvars" -out="{{.ENV}}.tfplan"

  # What: Applies an existing Terraform plan file for a module/environment pair.
  # Run: task tf:apply MODULE=azure-aks ENV=dev
  tf:apply:
    desc: "terraform apply for a module + env (requires confirmation). Args: MODULE=<path> ENV=<dev|staging|prod>"
    requires:
      vars: [MODULE, ENV]
    deps:
      - _require:terraform
    prompt: "Apply Terraform changes to {{.ENV}} in module {{.MODULE}}?"
    dir: "{{.TERRAFORM_DIR}}/{{.MODULE}}"
    cmds:
      - terraform apply "{{.ENV}}.tfplan"

  # What: Runs terraform test in a selected module directory.
  # Run: task tf:test MODULE=azure-aks
  tf:test:
    desc: "Run terraform test for a module. Args: MODULE=<path>"
    requires:
      vars: [MODULE]
    deps:
      - _require:terraform
    dir: "{{.TERRAFORM_DIR}}/{{.MODULE}}"
    cmds:
      - terraform test

  # What: Checks Terraform formatting recursively in terraform/ via the pre-commit hook.
  # Run: task tf:fmt-check
  tf:fmt-check:
    desc: "Check Terraform formatting recursively across terraform/ (pre-commit terraform_fmt)"
    deps:
      - _require:terraform
      - _require:pre-commit
    cmds:
      - pre-commit run terraform_fmt --all-files

  # What: Lints every Terraform module with tflint via the pre-commit hook.
  # Run: task tf:lint
  tf:lint:
    desc: "Lint terraform/ with tflint (pre-commit terraform_tflint)"
    deps:
      - _require:terraform
      - _require:pre-commit
    cmds:
      - pre-commit run terraform_tflint --all-files

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # HELM
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

  # What: Runs helm lint against the webapp chart.
  # Run: task helm:lint
  helm:lint:
    desc: "helm lint the webapp chart"
    deps:
      - _require:helm
    cmds:
      - helm lint {{.HELM_WEBAPP_CHART}}

  # What: Renders chart templates with dev values without installing.
  # Run: task helm:template-dev
  helm:template-dev:
    desc: "Render the webapp chart with dev values"
    deps:
      - _require:helm
    cmds:
      - helm template webapp {{.HELM_WEBAPP_CHART}} -f {{.HELM_WEBAPP_CHART}}/values.dev.yaml

  # What: Shows Helm upgrade diff for a release/namespace using dev values.
  # Run: task helm:diff RELEASE=webapp NAMESPACE=dev
  helm:diff:
    desc: "Show diff for a Helm release upgrade. Args: RELEASE=<name> NAMESPACE=<ns>"
    requires:
      vars: [RELEASE, NAMESPACE]
    deps:
      - _require:helm
    cmds:
      - helm diff upgrade --allow-unreleased {{.RELEASE}} {{.HELM_WEBAPP_CHART}} -n {{.NAMESPACE}} -f {{.HELM_WEBAPP_CHART}}/values.dev.yaml

  # What: Installs the webapp chart into a namespace (default: dev).
  # Run: task helm:install-dev NAMESPACE=dev
  helm:install-dev:
    desc: "Install the webapp chart into the dev namespace. Args: NAMESPACE=<ns>"
    vars:
      NAMESPACE: '{{.NAMESPACE | default "dev"}}'
    deps:
      - _require:helm
    cmds:
      - helm install webapp {{.HELM_WEBAPP_CHART}} -n {{.NAMESPACE}} --create-namespace -f {{.HELM_WEBAPP_CHART}}/values.dev.yaml

  # What: Upgrades or installs the webapp chart in prod values (with confirmation).
  # Run: task helm:upgrade-prod NAMESPACE=prod
  helm:upgrade-prod:
    desc: "Upgrade the webapp chart in prod (requires confirmation). Args: NAMESPACE=<ns>"
    vars:
      NAMESPACE: '{{.NAMESPACE | default "prod"}}'
    deps:
      - _require:helm
    prompt: "Upgrade Helm release 'webapp' in namespace '{{.NAMESPACE}}' on PRODUCTION?"
    cmds:
      - helm upgrade --install webapp {{.HELM_WEBAPP_CHART}} -n {{.NAMESPACE}} --create-namespace -f {{.HELM_WEBAPP_CHART}}/values.prod.yaml

  # Run: task security:slo-validate
  security:slo-validate:
    desc: "Validate SLO YAML files are parseable and follow the slo:<service>:<metric>:<window> naming convention"
    deps:
      - _require:yq
    cmds:
      - |
        set -e
        find observability/prometheus/slos -name '*.yaml' -o -name '*.yml' | while read -r f; do
          yq eval '.' "$f" > /dev/null || { echo "Invalid YAML: $f"; exit 1; }
        done
      - |
        if grep -rE 'record:' observability/prometheus/slos/ | grep -vE 'record:\s+slo:'; then
          echo "SLO recording rules found that do not follow slo:<service>:<metric>:<window> convention" >&2
          exit 1
        fi

    internal: true
    preconditions:
      - sh: command -v kubectl
        msg: "'kubectl' is not on PATH — install kubectl: https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/tools/"

  # What: Checks that helm is installed and available on PATH (internal guard).
  # Run: task _require:helm
  _require:helm:
    internal: true
    preconditions:
      - sh: command -v helm
        msg: "'helm' is not on PATH — install Helm: https://helm.sh/docs/intro/install/"

  # What: Checks that terraform is installed and available on PATH (internal guard).

    preconditions:

  port        = var.container_port
  protocol    = "HTTP"
  vpc_id      = var.vpc_id
  target_type = "ip"

  health_check {
    path                = "/health" # <-- CHANGE THIS: your health endpoint

  protocol          = "HTTP"

    type             = "forward"
    target_group_arn = aws_lb_target_group.main.arn
  }

  name_prefix = "${var.project}-${var.environment}"

# ---------------------------------------------
# RDS Subnet Group
# ---------------------------------------------
resource "aws_db_subnet_group" "main" {
  name        = "dbsng-${local.name_prefix}"
  description = "Private subnets for RDS"
  subnet_ids  = var.private_subnet_ids
  tags        = local.db_tags
}

# Permit database traffic only from within the EKS VPC. Workloads can then be
# narrowed further with their own security-group rules as the platform evolves.
resource "aws_security_group" "rds" {
  name_prefix = "sg-rds-${local.name_prefix}-"
  description = "Database access from the EKS VPC"
  vpc_id      = var.vpc_id

  ingress {
    description = "PostgreSQL from VPC workloads"
    from_port   = 5432
    to_port     = 5432
    protocol    = "tcp"
    cidr_blocks = [var.vpc_cidr]
  }

  egress {
    from_port   = 0
    to_port     = 0
    protocol    = "-1"
    cidr_blocks = ["0.0.0.0/0"]
  }

  tags = local.db_tags
}

# ---------------------------------------------
# RDS Parameter Group — enable logical replication for PITR
# ---------------------------------------------
resource "aws_db_parameter_group" "main" {
  name   = "pg-${local.name_prefix}"
  family = "${var.db_engine}${split(".", var.db_engine_version)[0]}" # e.g. postgres16

  parameter {
    name  = "log_connections"
    value = "1"
  }
  parameter {
    name  = "log_disconnections"
    value = "1"
  }

  tags = local.db_tags
}

# ---------------------------------------------
# Primary RDS Instance

resource "aws_db_instance" "primary" {
  identifier     = "rds-${local.name_prefix}"
  instance_class = var.db_instance_class
  engine         = var.db_engine
  engine_version = var.db_engine_version
  db_name        = var.db_name

  # Credentials — pulled from Secrets Manager after rotation is set up
  # Use manage_master_user_password instead of hardcoding a password
  manage_master_user_password = true      # stores password in Secrets Manager automatically
  username                    = "dbadmin" # <-- CHANGE THIS

  # Storage
  allocated_storage     = 20  # GB  # <-- CHANGE THIS
  max_allocated_storage = 200 # enables autoscaling  # <-- CHANGE THIS
  storage_type          = "gp3"
  storage_encrypted     = true
  kms_key_id            = null # <-- CHANGE THIS: set to a CMK ARN for compliance

  # High Availability
  multi_az = true # always true in production

  # Networking
  db_subnet_group_name   = aws_db_subnet_group.main.name
  vpc_security_group_ids = [aws_security_group.rds.id]
  publicly_accessible    = false # never expose RDS to the internet

  # ── Backup configuration ──────────────────────────────────────────────
  backup_retention_period   = var.backup_retention_days # PITR window
  backup_window             = var.backup_window
  copy_tags_to_snapshot     = true
  delete_automated_backups  = false # keep backups even if instance is deleted
  skip_final_snapshot       = false # always take a final snapshot on destroy
  final_snapshot_identifier = "final-${local.name_prefix}-${formatdate("YYYYMMDDHHmm", timestamp())}"
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  maintenance_window          = var.maintenance_window
  auto_minor_version_upgrade  = true
  allow_major_version_upgrade = false

  performance_insights_enabled          = true
  performance_insights_retention_period = 7  # days (731 for long-term, costs extra)
  monitoring_interval                   = 60 # Enhanced Monitoring — 0 to disable
  monitoring_role_arn                   = aws_iam_role.rds_monitoring.arn

  enabled_cloudwatch_logs_exports = ["postgresql"] # <-- CHANGE THIS: depends on engine

  parameter_group_name = aws_db_parameter_group.main.name

  tags = local.db_tags
}

# ---------------------------------------------
# IAM role for Enhanced Monitoring
# ---------------------------------------------
resource "aws_iam_role" "rds_monitoring" {
  name = "role-rds-monitoring-${local.name_prefix}"
  assume_role_policy = jsonencode({
    Version = "2012-10-17"
    Statement = [{
      Effect    = "Allow"
      Principal = { Service = "monitoring.rds.amazonaws.com" }
      Action    = "sts:AssumeRole"
    }]
  })
}

resource "aws_iam_role_policy_attachment" "rds_monitoring" {
  role       = aws_iam_role.rds_monitoring.name
  policy_arn = "arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/service-role/AmazonRDSEnhancedMonitoringRole"
}

# ---------------------------------------------
# Cross-region Read Replica (DR target)
# Creates a replica in a secondary region — promotes it manually during DR
# ---------------------------------------------
resource "aws_db_instance" "dr_replica" {
  count = var.environment == "prod" ? 1 : 0 # only in production  # <-- CHANGE THIS

  provider   = aws.dr_region
  identifier = "rds-${local.name_prefix}-dr"

  # Read replica config
  replicate_source_db = aws_db_instance.primary.arn
  instance_class      = var.db_instance_class

  # Backup: replicas inherit retention from primary but set it explicitly
  backup_retention_period   = var.backup_retention_days
  backup_window             = var.backup_window
  skip_final_snapshot       = false
  final_snapshot_identifier = "final-dr-${local.name_prefix}"

  storage_encrypted   = true
  multi_az            = false # promote to multi-AZ only after DR failover if needed
  publicly_accessible = false

  auto_minor_version_upgrade = true
  tags                       = merge(local.db_tags, { Role = "dr-replica" })
}

# ---------------------------------------------
# Automated Snapshot Export to S3 (optional — for long-term archive)
# Exports the latest daily snapshot to S3 in Parquet format.
# Useful for compliance archiving and analytics.
# ---------------------------------------------
resource "aws_rds_export_task" "archive" {
  count = var.snapshot_s3_bucket != "" ? 1 : 0

  export_task_identifier = "export-${local.name_prefix}"
  source_arn             = aws_db_instance.primary.arn
  s3_bucket_name         = var.snapshot_s3_bucket # <-- CHANGE THIS
  s3_prefix              = "rds-exports/${local.name_prefix}/"
  iam_role_arn           = aws_iam_role.rds_export[0].arn
  kms_key_id             = aws_db_instance.primary.kms_key_id
}

resource "aws_iam_role" "rds_export" {
  count = var.snapshot_s3_bucket != "" ? 1 : 0
  name  = "role-rds-export-${local.name_prefix}"
  assume_role_policy = jsonencode({
    Version = "2012-10-17"
    Statement = [{
      Effect    = "Allow"
      Principal = { Service = "export.rds.amazonaws.com" }
      Action    = "sts:AssumeRole"
    }]
  })
}

# ---------------------------------------------
# CloudWatch Alarm — failed backups
# ---------------------------------------------
resource "aws_cloudwatch_metric_alarm" "rds_backup_missing" {
  alarm_name          = "alarm-rds-backup-missing-${local.name_prefix}"
  comparison_operator = "LessThanThreshold"
  evaluation_periods  = 1
  metric_name         = "BackupRetentionPeriodStorageUsed"
  namespace           = "AWS/RDS"
  period              = 86400 # 24 hours
  statistic           = "Sum"
  threshold           = 1 # alert if no backup storage is being used
  alarm_description   = "RDS automated backups appear to have stopped"

  dimensions = {
    DBInstanceIdentifier = aws_db_instance.primary.id
  }

  alarm_actions = [] # <-- CHANGE THIS: add your SNS topic ARN
  ok_actions    = []
}

# TEMPLATE: Terraform — Azure Database Backup & DR Policies
# WHEN TO USE: Enable alongside terraform/azure-aks/ to ensure
#              Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server (or MySQL)
#              has automated backups, geo-redundancy, and PITR configured.
# WHAT TO CHANGE: Lines marked  # <-- CHANGE THIS
# RELATED FILES: cd/kubernetes/_patterns/velero-backup.yaml
# MATURITY: Stable
# ============================================================

locals {
  name_prefix = "${var.project}-${var.environment}"
}

# ---------------------------------------------
# Private DNS Zone for Flexible Server
# ---------------------------------------------
resource "azurerm_private_dns_zone" "postgres" {
  name                = "${var.project}-${var.environment}.postgres.database.azure.com"
  resource_group_name = var.rg_name
  tags                = var.common_tags
}

resource "azurerm_private_dns_zone_virtual_network_link" "postgres" {
  name                 = "dns-link-postgres"
  private_dns_zone_id  = azurerm_private_dns_zone.postgres.id
  virtual_network_id   = var.vnet_id
  registration_enabled = false
}

# ---------------------------------------------
# PostgreSQL Flexible Server (Primary)
# ---------------------------------------------
resource "azurerm_postgresql_flexible_server" "primary" {
  name                = "psql-${var.project}-${var.environment}"
  resource_group_name = var.rg_name
  location            = var.location

  version    = var.db_version
  sku_name   = var.db_sku
  storage_mb = var.db_storage_mb

  # Credentials — store in Key Vault; retrieve with data source or use BYOK
  administrator_login    = var.db_admin_username
  administrator_password = random_password.db_admin.result # generated below

  # Networking — private access only
  delegated_subnet_id = azurerm_subnet.db.id
  private_dns_zone_id = azurerm_private_dns_zone.postgres.id

  # ── Backup configuration ─────────────────────────────────────────────
  backup_retention_days        = var.backup_retention_days
  geo_redundant_backup_enabled = var.geo_redundant_backup # enables cross-region restore
  # ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  # High Availability — zone-redundant for production
  high_availability {
    mode                      = "ZoneRedundant" # <-- CHANGE THIS: SameZone for lower cost
    standby_availability_zone = "2"             # <-- CHANGE THIS
  }

  maintenance_window {
    day_of_week  = 0 # Sunday
    start_hour   = 3 # 03:00 UTC  # <-- CHANGE THIS
    start_minute = 0
  }

  tags = merge(var.common_tags, { Component = "database" })

  depends_on = [azurerm_private_dns_zone_virtual_network_link.postgres]
}

# Generate a strong random password stored in Key Vault
resource "random_password" "db_admin" {
  length           = 32
  special          = true
  override_special = "!#$%^&*()-_=+[]{}|;:,.<>?"
  min_upper        = 2
  min_lower        = 2
  min_numeric      = 2
  min_special      = 2
}

# Store the generated password in Key Vault
resource "azurerm_key_vault_secret" "db_admin_password" {
  count        = var.key_vault_id != null ? 1 : 0
  name         = "db-admin-password"
  value        = random_password.db_admin.result
  key_vault_id = var.key_vault_id # <-- CHANGE THIS: supply an existing Key Vault ID

  # Set expiry so secret rotation (azure-keyvault-rotation.tf) triggers
  expiration_date = timeadd(timestamp(), "720h") # 30 days

  tags = var.common_tags
}

# ---------------------------------------------
# DB Subnet (separate from AKS subnet)
# ---------------------------------------------
resource "azurerm_subnet" "db" {
  name                 = "snet-db"
  resource_group_name  = var.rg_name
  virtual_network_name = var.vnet_name
  address_prefixes     = ["10.1.3.0/24"] # <-- CHANGE THIS: non-overlapping with AKS subnet

  delegation {
    name = "postgres-delegation"
    service_delegation {
      name = "Microsoft.DBforPostgreSQL/flexibleServers"
      actions = [
        "Microsoft.Network/virtualNetworks/subnets/join/action",
      ]
    }
  }
}

# ---------------------------------------------
# Geo-Replica in secondary region (DR target)
# Read replica in dr_location; promote manually during DR.
# ---------------------------------------------
resource "azurerm_postgresql_flexible_server" "dr_replica" {
  count = var.environment == "prod" ? 1 : 0 # <-- CHANGE THIS

  name                = "psql-${var.project}-${var.environment}-dr"
  resource_group_name = var.rg_name
  location            = var.dr_location

  # Geo-restore: source from the primary's latest backup
  create_mode                       = "GeoRestore"
  source_server_id                  = azurerm_postgresql_flexible_server.primary.id
  point_in_time_restore_time_in_utc = null # null = latest available backup

  version    = var.db_version
  sku_name   = var.db_sku
  storage_mb = var.db_storage_mb

  administrator_login    = var.db_admin_username
  administrator_password = random_password.db_admin.result

  backup_retention_days        = var.backup_retention_days
  geo_redundant_backup_enabled = false # DR replica doesn't need geo-backup

  tags = merge(var.common_tags, { Component = "database", Role = "dr-replica" })
}

# ---------------------------------------------
# Azure Monitor Alert — backup failures
# ---------------------------------------------
resource "azurerm_monitor_metric_alert" "db_backup_failed" {
  name                = "alert-db-backup-failed-${local.name_prefix}"
  resource_group_name = var.rg_name
  scopes              = [azurerm_postgresql_flexible_server.primary.id]
  description         = "PostgreSQL Flexible Server backup has failed"
  severity            = 1 # Critical

  criteria {
    metric_namespace = "Microsoft.DBforPostgreSQL/flexibleServers"
    metric_name      = "backup_storage_used"
    aggregation      = "Average"
    operator         = "LessThan"
    threshold        = 1 # alert if backup storage drops to zero
  }

  window_size = "P1D"
  frequency   = "PT1H"

  action {
    action_group_id = var.alert_action_group_id # <-- CHANGE THIS: pass in your action group
  }

  tags = var.common_tags
}

# ---------------------------------------------
# Log Analytics Workspace (for Container Insights)
# ---------------------------------------------
resource "azurerm_log_analytics_workspace" "main" {
  name                = "law-${var.project}-${var.environment}"
  resource_group_name = var.rg_name
  location            = var.location
  sku                 = "PerGB2018"
  retention_in_days   = 30

  tags = var.common_tags
}

# ---------------------------------------------
# Virtual Network + Subnet for AKS
# ---------------------------------------------
resource "azurerm_virtual_network" "main" {
  name                = "vnet-${var.project}-${var.environment}"
  resource_group_name = var.rg_name
  location            = var.location
  address_space       = [var.vnet_address_space]

  tags = var.common_tags
}

resource "azurerm_subnet" "aks" {
  name                 = "snet-aks"
  resource_group_name  = var.rg_name
  virtual_network_name = azurerm_virtual_network.main.name
  address_prefixes     = [var.aks_subnet_prefix]

}

# ---------------------------------------------
resource "google_artifact_registry_repository" "main" {
  repository_id = "${var.project}-${var.environment}"
  location      = var.gcp_region
  format        = "DOCKER"
  description   = "Docker repository for ${var.project} ${var.environment}"

  labels = var.common_labels

  depends_on = [var.apis_ready]
}

# IAM — Grant GKE access to Artifact Registry
# ---------------------------------------------
resource "google_project_iam_member" "gke_ar_reader" {
  project = var.gcp_project_id
  role    = "roles/artifactregistry.reader"
  member  = "serviceAccount:${var.gke_node_service_account}"
}

# ============================================================
# TEMPLATE: Terraform — GCP GKE Persistent Storage
# WHEN to USE: Add alongside terraform/gcp-gke/ to ensure GKE workloads have
#              persistent storage (Persistent Disk, Cloud Storage, or Memorystore)
#              configured before an incident forces your hand.
# WHAT to CHANGE: Lines marked  # <-- CHANGE THIS
# RELATED FILES: docs/guides/gke-persistent-storage.md
# MATURITY: Stable
# ============================================================

locals {
  name_prefix  = "${var.project}-${var.environment}"
  storage_tags = merge(var.common_labels, { Component = "persistent-storage" })
}

# ---------------------------------------------
# Persistent Disk (if using Persistent Disk)
# ---------------------------------------------
resource "google_compute_disk" "main" {
  count  = var.enable_persistent_storage && var.storage_type == "persistent-disk" ? 1 : 0
  name   = "pd-${local.name_prefix}-${var.storage_class_name}"
  zone   = var.storage_zone
  size   = var.storage_size
  type   = var.storage_disk_type
  labels = local.storage_tags

  lifecycle {
    create_before_destroy = true
  }
}

# ---------------------------------------------
# Cloud Storage Bucket (if using Cloud Storage)
# ---------------------------------------------
resource "google_storage_bucket" "main" {
  count                       = var.enable_persistent_storage && var.storage_type == "cloud-storage" ? 1 : 0
  name                        = "gs-${local.name_prefix}-${var.storage_class_name}"
  location                    = var.storage_location
  force_destroy               = var.storage_force_destroy
  uniform_bucket_level_access = var.storage_uniform_access
  labels                      = local.storage_tags

  lifecycle {
    create_before_destroy = true
  }
}

# ---------------------------------------------
# Memorystore (if using Memorystore)
# ---------------------------------------------
resource "google_memorystore_instance" "main" {
  count         = var.enable_persistent_storage && var.storage_type == "memorystore" ? 1 : 0
  instance_id   = "mem-${local.name_prefix}"
  location      = var.storage_location
  shard_count   = var.storage_node_count
  replica_count = var.storage_automatic_failover ? 1 : 0 # <-- CHANGE THIS: replicas per shard
  node_type     = "SHARED_CORE_NANO"                     # <-- CHANGE THIS: match your workload sizing
  labels        = local.storage_tags

  lifecycle {
    create_before_destroy = true
  }
}

# TEMPLATE: Terraform — Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE)
# WHEN TO USE: Provisioning a production-ready GKE cluster on GCP
# PREREQUISITES: GCP project, gcloud CLI authenticated
# SECRETS NEEDED: None (uses gcloud auth or service account key)
# WHAT TO CHANGE: Lines marked with # <-- CHANGE THIS
# RELATED FILES: cd/targets/gcp-gke/, cd/kubernetes/
# MATURITY: Stable
# LAYOUT: versions.tf (providers/APIs), network.tf (VPC/NAT),
#         artifact-registry.tf, gke.tf (cluster/node pool), iam.tf,
#         backup.tf (DR/backup), locals.tf (labels)
# ============================================================

terraform {
  required_version = ">= 1.5.0"

  required_providers {
    google = {
      source  = "hashicorp/google"
      version = "~> 7.45.0" # <-- CHANGE THIS: pin to latest stable
    }
  }

  # Uncomment and configure for remote state
  # backend "gcs" {
  #   bucket = "my-terraform-state"
  #   prefix = "gke/terraform.tfstate"
  # }
}

provider "google" {
  project = var.gcp_project_id
  region  = var.gcp_region
}

# ---------------------------------------------
# Enable Required APIs
# ---------------------------------------------
resource "google_project_service" "apis" {
  for_each = toset([
    "container.googleapis.com",
    "artifactregistry.googleapis.com",
    "compute.googleapis.com",
    "logging.googleapis.com",
    "monitoring.googleapis.com",
  ])

  project = var.gcp_project_id
  service = each.value

  disable_on_destroy = false
}
